rows.trigger: MANDATORY MINIMUM: 3-year minimum term of imprisonment upon conviction of aggravated assault or aggravated battery upon a person 65 years of age or older, plus a fine of not more than $10,000, mandatory restitution to the victim, and up to 500 hours of community service. rows.trigger: Section-wide note: s. 775.083 assigns no degree of offense anywhere. It is a fine-cap and cost schedule that consumes degrees assigned by other statutes. Every dollar figure in it is a fine ceiling or a court cost, never a value threshold that grades an offense, so min and max are null on every row. Never cite this section as the source of an offense degree.

Unnumbered operative text sits on both sides of the (a)-(g) ladder; the elision between them is marked. The lead-in does three things that appear nowhere in (a)-(g): it limits the fine authorization to an offense other than a capital felony; it makes a fine in addition to s. 775.082 punishment the default and allows a fine in lieu of that punishment only when specifically authorized by another statute; and it separately authorizes a fine for a noncriminal violation, for which (1)(e) supplies only the cap. The figures in (a)-(g) are ceilings a fine shall not exceed, not mandatory amounts, and no minimum fine exists anywhere in the section. The exclusion of capital felonies reaches only this subsection's fine authority; subsection (2) court costs still attach to a capital felony conviction. The closing flush text directs deposit into the s. 142.01 fund, permits deferral for inability to pay, and defines convicted or conviction to include a guilty or nolo contendere plea even where adjudication is withheld.
rows.quote: A person who has been convicted of an offense other than a capital felony may be sentenced to pay a fine in addition to any punishment described in s. 775.082; when specifically authorized by statute, he or she may be sentenced to pay a fine in lieu of any punishment described in s. 775.082. A person who has been convicted of a noncriminal violation may be sentenced to pay a fine. Fines for designated crimes and for noncriminal violations shall not exceed: ... Fines imposed in this subsection shall be deposited by the clerk of the court in the fine and forfeiture fund established pursuant to s. 142.01. If a defendant is unable to pay a fine, the court may defer payment of the fine to a date certain. As used in this subsection, the term “convicted” or “conviction” means a determination of guilt which is the result of a trial or the entry of a plea of guilty or nolo contendere, regardless of whether adjudication is withheld.

rows.trigger: Fine ceiling of $15,000 when the conviction is of a life felony. The degree is a condition consumed from the charging statute, not assigned here; $15,000 is a fine cap, not a trigger threshold. Note the asymmetry with the lead-in: a life felony is inside this section, a capital felony is excluded from subsection (1) entirely.
rows.quote: $15,000, when the conviction is of a life felony.

rows.trigger: Fine ceiling of $10,000 when the conviction is of a felony of the first degree or of the second degree. Both degrees share one cap; this paragraph does not distinguish them, and the single shared cap is why no one degree can be typed for this row.
rows.quote: $10,000, when the conviction is of a felony of the first or second degree.

rows.trigger: Fine ceiling of $5,000 when the conviction is of a felony of the third degree.
rows.quote: $5,000, when the conviction is of a felony of the third degree.

rows.trigger: Fine ceiling of $1,000 when the conviction is of a misdemeanor of the first degree.
rows.quote: $1,000, when the conviction is of a misdemeanor of the first degree.

rows.trigger: Fine ceiling of $500 when the conviction is of a misdemeanor of the second degree or a noncriminal violation. This paragraph is a cap only; the authority to fine a noncriminal violation comes from the second sentence of the subsection (1) lead-in.
rows.quote: $500, when the conviction is of a misdemeanor of the second degree or a noncriminal violation.

rows.trigger: Override of the (a)-(e) ceilings: the fine may instead be any higher amount up to double the offender's pecuniary gain or double the victim's pecuniary loss. This is a finite, computable ceiling in every case, a multiplier cap, not an absence of a bound; contrast (g), which is the only genuinely open-ended paragraph in this section. A reader who finds their degree tier in (a)-(e) and stops will understate the maximum fine.
rows.quote: Any higher amount equal to double the pecuniary gain derived from the offense by the offender or double the pecuniary loss suffered by the victim.

rows.trigger: Second override, open-ended within this section: any higher amount specifically authorized by any other statute displaces the (a)-(e) ladder, with no ceiling stated here. Never state a maximum fine from (a)-(e) alone without checking the charging statute. Distinguish the lead-in's in-lieu-of clause, which also turns on specific statutory authorization but changes what the fine replaces rather than how high it may go.
rows.quote: Any higher amount specifically authorized by statute.

rows.trigger: Mandatory court costs assessed in addition to subsection (1) fines: $50 for a felony and $20 for any other offense, in each instance of a nolo contendere plea, conviction, or delinquency adjudication for a felony, misdemeanor, criminal traffic offense, or an ordinance violation constituting a misdemeanor under state law. These are cost amounts, not fine caps and not trigger thresholds. This subsection is not governed by the subsection (1) lead-in and contains no capital carve-out, so the $50 felony cost attaches to a capital felony conviction even though the subsection (1) fine authority does not. The back half binds the county: costs are deposited into an appropriate county account, must be accounted for separately as crime prevention funds, and must be expended, in consultation with the sheriff, on crime prevention programs in the county; 'must expend' is mandatory. Contrast subsection (1) fines, which go to the s. 142.01 fine and forfeiture fund instead.
rows.quote: In addition to the fines set forth in subsection (1), court costs shall be assessed and collected in each instance a defendant pleads nolo contendere to, or is convicted of, or adjudicated delinquent for, a felony, a misdemeanor, or a criminal traffic offense under state law, or a violation of any municipal or county ordinance if the violation constitutes a misdemeanor under state law. The court costs imposed by this section shall be $50 for a felony and $20 for any other offense and shall be deposited by the clerk of the court into an appropriate county account for disbursement for the purposes provided in this subsection. A county shall account for the funds separately from other county funds as crime prevention funds. The county, in consultation with the sheriff, must expend such funds for crime prevention programs in the county.

rows.trigger: Procedural only: the clerk of court collects, and the person ordered to pay must immediately contact the clerk to pay in full or apply for a s. 28.246(4) payment plan. No degree, no dollar trigger. Read alongside the closing flush text of subsection (1), which separately allows the court to defer a fine to a date certain for inability to pay.
rows.quote: The clerk of the court of each county is the entity responsible for collecting payment of fines, fees, service charges, and court costs. Unless otherwise designated by the court, a person who has been ordered to pay court obligations under this section shall immediately contact the clerk to pay fines, fees, service charges, and court costs in full or to apply for enrollment in a payment plan pursuant to s. 28.246(4).

rows.trigger: Incorporation-by-reference clause: a bare reference to this section in another statute pulls in the whole fine schedule, including the subsection (1) lead-in limits, so an incorporating statute also inherits the capital-felony exclusion and the in-addition-to default. Confirms 775.083 is a downstream penalty provision, never the source of a degree.
rows.quote: The purpose of this section is to provide uniform penalty authorization for criminal offenses and, to this end, a reference to this section constitutes a general reference under the doctrine of incorporation by reference.

If the property stolen is cargo valued at $50,000 or more that has entered the stream of interstate or intrastate commerce from the shipper’s loading platform to the consignee’s receiving dock; ... the offender commits grand theft in the first degree, punishable as a felony of the first degree, as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: ANY grand theft (no separate dollar threshold beyond whatever made it grand theft) where the offender uses a motor vehicle as an instrumentality, other than merely as a getaway vehicle, and thereby damages the real property of another. NO LOWER BOUND on the value stolen -- min is null.
rows.quote: 3. If the offender commits any grand theft and:a. In the course of committing the offense the offender uses a motor vehicle as an instrumentality, other than merely as a getaway vehicle, to assist in committing the offense and thereby damages the real property of another; ... the offender commits grand theft in the first degree, punishable as a felony of the first degree, as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: ANY grand theft where the offender causes damage to the real or personal property of another in excess of $1,000. The $1,000 figure measures DAMAGE CAUSED to a third party's property, NOT the value of the property stolen, so it is carried here in trigger only and min is null: the value stolen has NO lower bound beyond whatever made the offense grand theft, which includes value-free named items (a stolen firearm worth $200 plus $5,000 of collateral damage qualifies). 'In excess of' is strictly greater than $1,000, so exactly $1,000 of damage does not qualify.
rows.quote: 3. If the offender commits any grand theft and: ... b. In the course of committing the offense the offender causes damage to the real or personal property of another in excess of $1,000,the offender commits grand theft in the first degree, punishable as a felony of the first degree, as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

(b)1. If the property stolen is valued at $20,000 or more, but less than $100,000; ... the offender commits grand theft in the second degree, punishable as a felony of the second degree, as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: CARGO IN THE STREAM OF COMMERCE, ANY VALUE. NO LOWER BOUND -- min is null. Cargo valued at less than $50,000 that has entered the stream of interstate or intrastate commerce from the shipper's loading platform to the consignee's receiving dock is a second degree felony no matter how small the value; there is no floor and no general-ladder minimum imported into this subparagraph.
rows.quote: 2. If the property stolen is cargo valued at less than $50,000 that has entered the stream of interstate or intrastate commerce from the shipper’s loading platform to the consignee’s receiving dock; ... the offender commits grand theft in the second degree, punishable as a felony of the second degree, as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Emergency medical equipment taken from a facility licensed under chapter 395 or from an aircraft or vehicle permitted under chapter 401. No upper bound stated.
rows.quote: 3. rows.trigger: Law enforcement equipment taken from an authorized emergency vehicle as defined in s. 316.003. No upper bound stated.
rows.quote: 4. If the property stolen is law enforcement equipment, valued at $300 or more, that is taken from an authorized emergency vehicle, as defined in s. 316.003,the offender commits grand theft in the second degree, punishable as a felony of the second degree, as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084. ... rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION of ANY theft under paragraph (b) -- including the value-free cargo provision in (b)2 -- when stolen during a riot or aggravated riot under s. 870.01 and facilitated by conditions arising from the riot, OR within a county subject to a Governor-declared state of emergency under chapter 252 where the theft occurs after the declaration and is facilitated by conditions arising from the emergency. fs-817.034.title: Florida Communications Fraud Act

rows.trigger: Organized fraud: engaging in a scheme to defraud and obtaining property thereby. No upper bound stated.
rows.quote: Any person who engages in a scheme to defraud and obtains property thereby commits organized fraud, punishable as follows: 1. If the amount of property obtained has an aggregate value of $50,000 or more, the person commits a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Organized fraud: engaging in a scheme to defraud and obtaining property thereby.
rows.quote: 2. If the amount of property obtained has an aggregate value of $20,000 or more, but less than $50,000, the person commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Organized fraud of ANY aggregate value below $20,000, however small; the statute sets no floor for this tier.
rows.quote: 3. If the amount of property obtained has an aggregate value of less than $20,000, the person commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Communications fraud: a separate offense for EACH act of communication made in furtherance of a scheme to defraud with intent to obtain property from that person. Value counted is property obtained OR endeavored to be obtained by that communication. No upper bound stated.
rows.quote: Any person who engages in a scheme to defraud and, in furtherance of that scheme, communicates with any person with intent to obtain property from that person commits, for each such act of communication, communications fraud, punishable as follows: 1. If the value of property obtained or endeavored to be obtained by the communication is valued at $300 or more, the person commits a third degree felony, punishable as set forth in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Communications fraud (per act of communication) where value obtained or endeavored to be obtained is ANY amount below $300; the statute sets no floor. Note s. 775.084 is omitted from this tier's punishment cross-references.
rows.quote: 2. If the value of the property obtained or endeavored to be obtained by the communication is valued at less than $300, the person commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as set forth in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION (enhancement), value-independent: offense under paragraph (a) or (b) committed against a person age 65 or older, against a minor, or against a person with a mental or physical disability as defined in s. 775.0863(1)(b). A first degree misdemeanor becomes a third degree felony. Degree shown is the OUTPUT of the reclassification, not a standalone offense grade.
rows.quote: The penalty for committing an offense specified in paragraph (a) or paragraph (b) against a person age 65 years or older, against a minor, or against a person with a mental or physical disability, as defined in s. 775.0863(1)(b), shall be reclassified as follows: 1. A misdemeanor of the first degree is reclassified to a felony of the third degree.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION (enhancement), value-independent: victim age 65 or older, a minor, or a person with a mental or physical disability under s. 775.0863(1)(b). A third degree felony becomes a second degree felony. Degree shown is the OUTPUT of the reclassification.
rows.quote: 2. A felony of the third degree is reclassified to a felony of the second degree.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION (enhancement), value-independent: victim age 65 or older, a minor, or a person with a mental or physical disability under s. 775.0863(1)(b). A second degree felony becomes a first degree felony. Degree shown is the OUTPUT of the reclassification.
rows.quote: 3. A felony of the second degree is reclassified to a felony of the first degree.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION (enhancement), value-independent: victim age 65 or older, a minor, or a person with a mental or physical disability under s. 775.0863(1)(b). A first degree felony becomes a life felony. This is the top of the ladder in this section. Degree shown is the OUTPUT of the reclassification.
rows.quote: 4. A felony of the first degree is reclassified to a life felony.

rows.trigger: Cumulative punishment rule: authorizes separate judgments and sentences for organized fraud under (a) AND for each separate communications fraud under (b) arising from the same scheme. Assigns no degree itself but multiplies exposure.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any contrary provisions of law, separate judgments and sentences for organized fraud under paragraph (a) and for each offense of communications fraud under paragraph (b) may be imposed when all such offenses involve the same scheme to defraud.

rows.trigger: Grading rule feeding the (4)(a) dollar tiers: values of separate properties obtained in one scheme are aggregated, whether taken from one person or several. The statute expressly confines this aggregation rule to grading under paragraph (4)(a). Assigns no degree itself.
rows.quote: Amounts of value of separate properties obtained in one scheme to defraud, whether from the same person or from several persons, shall be aggregated in determining the grade of the offense under paragraph (4)(a).

rows.trigger: SECTION-WIDE valuation default: subsection (3) opens 'As used in this section, the term', so this rule defines 'value' everywhere in 817.034, with no limiting language confining it to any paragraph. When value cannot be ascertained and no minimum can be found, value is deemed less than $300. That deemed value governs the per-communication tiers of (4)(b) AND, fed through the (3)(e)3 aggregation rule, the organized fraud tiers of (4)(a), placing an unascertainable-value organized fraud in the (4)(a)3 third degree felony tier. It affects felony grading as well as misdemeanor grading. Assigns no degree itself.
rows.quote: If the value of property cannot be ascertained, the trier of fact may find the value to be not less than a certain amount; if no such minimum value can be ascertained, the value is an amount less than $300.

fs-775.087.title: Possession or use of weapon; aggravated battery; felony reclassification; minimum sentence

rows.trigger: Underlying charge is a first degree felony; defendant carries, displays, uses, threatens to use, or attempts to use any weapon or firearm during the commission of the felony, or commits an aggravated battery during it. Does not apply where use of a weapon or firearm is an essential element of the felony, or where otherwise provided by law. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: Unless otherwise provided by law, whenever a person is charged with a felony, except a felony in which the use of a weapon or firearm is an essential element, and during the commission of such felony the defendant carries, displays, uses, threatens to use, or attempts to use any weapon or firearm, or during the commission of such felony the defendant commits an aggravated battery, the felony for which the person is charged shall be reclassified as follows:(a) In the case of a felony of the first degree, to a life felony.

rows.trigger: Same weapon/firearm or aggravated battery condition as subsection (1); underlying charge is a second degree felony. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: (b) In the case of a felony of the second degree, to a felony of the first degree.

rows.trigger: Same weapon/firearm or aggravated battery condition as subsection (1); underlying charge is a third degree felony. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: (c) In the case of a felony of the third degree, to a felony of the second degree.

rows.trigger: Any felony offense reclassified under this section; enhancement is a one-level bump in offense severity ranking for chapter 921 sentencing and chapter 944 incentive gain-time eligibility. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: For purposes of sentencing under chapter 921 and determining incentive gain-time eligibility under chapter 944, a felony offense which is reclassified under this section is ranked one level above the ranking under s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 of the felony offense committed.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum of 10 years. Conviction of, or attempt to commit, any felony enumerated in sub-subparagraphs 1.a.-r., regardless of whether use of a weapon is an element, where during the commission of the offense the person ACTUALLY POSSESSED a firearm or destructive device as defined in s. 790.001. NO dollar or quantity trigger; qualification is by named offense, and the enumerated list is a list of named items, not a value ladder.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a felony or an attempt to commit a felony, regardless of whether the use of a weapon is an element of the felony, and the conviction was for:a. Murder; b. Sexual battery; c. Robbery; d. Burglary; e. Arson; f. Aggravated battery; g. Kidnapping; h. Escape; i. Aircraft piracy; j. Aggravated child abuse; k. Aggravated abuse of an elderly person or disabled adult; l. Unlawful throwing, placing, or discharging of a destructive device or bomb; m. Carjacking; n. Home-invasion robbery; o. Aggravated stalking; p. Trafficking in cannabis, trafficking in cocaine, capital importation of cocaine, trafficking in illegal drugs, capital importation of illegal drugs, trafficking in phencyclidine, capital importation of phencyclidine, trafficking in methaqualone, capital importation of methaqualone, trafficking in amphetamine, capital importation of amphetamine, trafficking in flunitrazepam, trafficking in gamma-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB), trafficking in 1,4-Butanediol, trafficking in Phenethylamines, or other violation of s. 893.135(1); q. Possession of a firearm by a felon; or r. Human trafficking and during the commission of the offense, such person actually possessed a “firearm” or “destructive device” as those terms are defined in s. 790.001, shall be sentenced to a minimum term of imprisonment of 10 years, ...

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum of 3 years instead of 10. Conviction for possession of a firearm by a felon, or burglary of a conveyance, where the person possessed a firearm or destructive device during the commission of the offense. Note this clause reaches burglary of a conveyance, which is not separately enumerated in 1.a.-r. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: except that a person who is convicted for possession of a firearm by a felon or burglary of a conveyance shall be sentenced to a minimum term of imprisonment of 3 years if such person possessed a “firearm” or “destructive device” during the commission of the offense.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum returns to 10 years. Offender convicted of possession of a firearm by a felon who has a PREVIOUS CONVICTION of committing or attempting to commit a felony listed in s. 775.084(1)(b)1. and who actually possessed a firearm or destructive device during the commission of that prior felony. NO dollar or quantity trigger; criminal-history trigger only.
rows.quote: However, if an offender who is convicted of the offense of possession of a firearm by a felon has a previous conviction of committing or attempting to commit a felony listed in s. 775.084(1)(b)1. and actually possessed a firearm or destructive device during the commission of the prior felony, the offender shall be sentenced to a minimum term of imprisonment of 10 years.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum of 20 years. DISCHARGE of a firearm or destructive device during the course of the commission of a felony (or attempt) listed in sub-subparagraphs 1.a.-p. or 1.r. only. Sub-subparagraph 1.q. (possession of a firearm by a felon) is EXCLUDED from this 20-year provision. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a felony or an attempt to commit a felony listed in sub-subparagraphs 1.a.-p. or sub-subparagraph 1.r., regardless of whether the use of a weapon is an element of the felony, and during the course of the commission of the felony such person discharged a “firearm” or “destructive device” as defined in s. 790.001 shall be sentenced to a minimum term of imprisonment of 20 years.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum of not less than 25 years and up to life. Discharge of a firearm or destructive device during a felony (or attempt) listed in sub-subparagraphs 1.a.-p. or 1.r., and as a result of the discharge death or great bodily harm was inflicted upon any person. Sub-subparagraph 1.q. is EXCLUDED. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a felony or an attempt to commit a felony listed in sub-subparagraphs 1.a.-p. or sub-subparagraph 1.r., regardless of whether the use of a weapon is an element of the felony, and during the course of the commission of the felony such person discharged a “firearm” or “destructive device” as defined in s. 790.001 and, as the result of the discharge, death or great bodily harm was inflicted upon any person, the convicted person shall be sentenced to a minimum term of imprisonment of not less than 25 years and not more than a term of imprisonment of life in prison.

rows.trigger: Applies to any sentence imposed under (2)(a)1., (2)(a)2., or (2)(a)3. Preserves longer sentences and the death penalty, forbids a lesser sentence, and bars suspension, deferral, or withholding of adjudication or sentence, statutory gain-time under s. 944.275, and any discretionary early release other than pardon, executive clemency, or conditional medical release under s. 947.149, prior to serving the minimum sentence. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: Subparagraph (a)1., subparagraph (a)2., or subparagraph (a)3. does not prevent a court from imposing a longer sentence of incarceration as authorized by law in addition to the minimum mandatory sentence, or from imposing a sentence of death pursuant to other applicable law. Subparagraph (a)1., subparagraph (a)2., or subparagraph (a)3. does not authorize a court to impose a lesser sentence than otherwise required by law.Notwithstanding s. 948.01, adjudication of guilt or imposition of sentence shall not be suspended, deferred, or withheld, and the defendant is not eligible for statutory gain-time under s. 944.275 or any form of discretionary early release, other than pardon or executive clemency, or conditional medical release under s. 947.149, prior to serving the minimum sentence.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum must be imposed even where it exceeds the maximum sentence authorized by s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code; where lower, the sentence imposed must still include the mandatory minimum. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: If the minimum mandatory terms of imprisonment imposed pursuant to this section exceed the maximum sentences authorized by s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, then the mandatory minimum sentence must be imposed. If the mandatory minimum terms of imprisonment pursuant to this section are less than the sentences that could be imposed as authorized by s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, then the sentence imposed by the court must include the mandatory minimum term of imprisonment as required in this section.

rows.trigger: Court shall impose the paragraph (a) minimum for EACH qualifying felony offense of conviction, and where there are multiple qualifying felony offenses the terms shall be imposed CONSECUTIVELY. Mandatory. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: It is the intent of the Legislature that offenders who actually possess, carry, display, use, threaten to use, or attempt to use firearms or destructive devices be punished to the fullest extent of the law. The court shall impose the minimum term of imprisonment required under paragraph (a) for each qualifying felony offense for which the person is convicted. If the offender is convicted of multiple felony offenses for which paragraph (a) requires the imposition of a minimum term of imprisonment, the court shall impose any such terms of imprisonment consecutively.

rows.trigger: Discretionary consecutive sentencing. Where an enumerated (a)1. felony is committed in conjunction with any other felony NOT enumerated in (a)1., the court MAY run the paragraph (a) term consecutive to the term for the non-enumerated felony. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: If an offender commits a felony enumerated in subparagraph (a)1. in conjunction with any other felony offense not enumerated in subparagraph (a)1., the court may impose any term of imprisonment provided for in paragraph (a) consecutively to any other term of imprisonment imposed for any other felony offense not enumerated in subparagraph (a)1.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum of 15 years. Conviction of, or attempt to commit, a felony enumerated in sub-subparagraphs 1.a.-r. of THIS subsection, where during the commission the person possessed EITHER (i) a semiautomatic firearm AND its high-capacity detachable box magazine, a prong carrying a quantity element via the (3)(f)1. definition (magazine capable of being loaded with MORE THAN 20 centerfire cartridges; centerfire only), OR (ii) a machine gun as defined in s. 790.001(13), a prong with NO magazine or capacity element of any kind: any machine gun qualifies at any capacity, with any magazine, or with no detachable box magazine at all. Because the machine-gun prong has no floor, no min is typed on this row; the more-than-20-centerfire-cartridge element gates ONLY the semiautomatic prong. The (3) list DIFFERS from the (2) list: it includes 'Sale, manufacture, delivery, or intent to sell, manufacture, or deliver any controlled substance' (1.i.) and does NOT include possession of a firearm by a felon. Requires 'possessed', not 'actually possessed'.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a felony or an attempt to commit a felony, regardless of whether the use of a firearm is an element of the felony, and the conviction was for:a. Murder; b. Sexual battery; c. Robbery; d. Burglary; e. Arson; f. Aggravated battery; g. Kidnapping; h. Escape; i. Sale, manufacture, delivery, or intent to sell, manufacture, or deliver any controlled substance; j. Aircraft piracy; k. Aggravated child abuse; l. Aggravated abuse of an elderly person or disabled adult; m. Unlawful throwing, placing, or discharging of a destructive device or bomb; n. Carjacking; o. Home-invasion robbery; p. Aggravated stalking; q. Trafficking in cannabis, trafficking in cocaine, capital importation of cocaine, trafficking in illegal drugs, capital importation of illegal drugs, trafficking in phencyclidine, capital importation of phencyclidine, trafficking in methaqualone, capital importation of methaqualone, trafficking in amphetamine, capital importation of amphetamine, trafficking in flunitrazepam, trafficking in gamma-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB), trafficking in 1,4-Butanediol, trafficking in Phenethylamines, or other violation of s. 893.135(1); or r. Human trafficking and during the commission of the offense, such person possessed a semiautomatic firearm and its high-capacity detachable box magazine or a machine gun as defined in s. 790.001, shall be sentenced to a minimum term of imprisonment of 15 years.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum of 20 years. During the course of the commission of any felony (or attempt) listed in subparagraph (3)(a)1., the person discharged EITHER (i) a semiautomatic firearm and its high-capacity box magazine -- NOTE the operative text here drops 'detachable': the only term (3)(f)1. defines is 'high-capacity DETACHABLE box magazine', and the section never defines 'high-capacity box magazine' -- OR (ii) a 'machine gun' as defined in s. 790.001(13), a prong with NO magazine or capacity element; any machine gun qualifies at any capacity or with no magazine. No min typed: the machine-gun prong has no quantity floor, and the more-than-20-centerfire-cartridge definition, if it controls the variant term at all, gates only the semiautomatic prong. Unlike (2)(a)2., this provision covers the ENTIRE (3)(a)1. list with no sub-subparagraph carve-out.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a felony or an attempt to commit a felony listed in subparagraph 1., regardless of whether the use of a weapon is an element of the felony, and during the course of the commission of the felony such person discharged a semiautomatic firearm and its high-capacity box magazine or a “machine gun” as defined in s. 790.001 shall be sentenced to a minimum term of imprisonment of 20 years.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum of not less than 25 years and up to life. During a felony (or attempt) listed in subparagraph (3)(a)1., the person discharged EITHER (i) a semiautomatic firearm and its high-capacity box magazine -- NOTE the operative text drops 'detachable'; (3)(f)1. defines only 'high-capacity DETACHABLE box magazine', and 'high-capacity box magazine' is never defined in the section -- OR (ii) a 'machine gun' as defined in s. 790.001(13), a prong with NO magazine or capacity element, and as a result of the discharge death or great bodily harm was inflicted upon any person. No min typed: the machine-gun prong has no quantity floor, and the more-than-20-centerfire-cartridge definition gates only the semiautomatic prong. Covers the ENTIRE (3)(a)1. list with no carve-out.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a felony or an attempt to commit a felony listed in subparagraph 1., regardless of whether the use of a weapon is an element of the felony, and during the course of the commission of the felony such person discharged a semiautomatic firearm and its high-capacity box magazine or a “machine gun” as defined in s. 790.001 and, as the result of the discharge, death or great bodily harm was inflicted upon any person, the convicted person shall be sentenced to a minimum term of imprisonment of not less than 25 years and not more than a term of imprisonment of life in prison.

rows.trigger: Applies to any sentence under (3)(a)1., (3)(a)2., or (3)(a)3. Preserves longer sentences and the death penalty, forbids a lesser sentence, and bars suspension, deferral, or withholding of adjudication or sentence, statutory gain-time under s. 944.275, and any discretionary early release other than pardon, executive clemency, or conditional medical release under s. 947.149, prior to serving the minimum sentence. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: Subparagraph (a)1., subparagraph (a)2., or subparagraph (a)3. does not prevent a court from imposing a longer sentence of incarceration as authorized by law in addition to the minimum mandatory sentence, or from imposing a sentence of death pursuant to other applicable law. Subparagraph (a)1., subparagraph (a)2., or subparagraph (a)3. does not authorize a court to impose a lesser sentence than otherwise required by law.Notwithstanding s. 948.01, adjudication of guilt or imposition of sentence shall not be suspended, deferred, or withheld, and the defendant is not eligible for statutory gain-time under s. 944.275 or any form of discretionary early release, other than pardon or executive clemency, or conditional medical release under s. 947.149, prior to serving the minimum sentence.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum must be imposed even where it exceeds the maximum authorized by s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code; where lower, the sentence imposed must still include the mandatory minimum. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: If the minimum mandatory terms of imprisonment imposed pursuant to this section exceed the maximum sentences authorized by s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, then the mandatory minimum sentence must be imposed. If the mandatory minimum terms of imprisonment pursuant to this section are less than the sentences that could be imposed as authorized by s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, then the sentence imposed by the court must include the mandatory minimum term of imprisonment as required in this section.

rows.trigger: Court shall impose the paragraph (3)(a) minimum for EACH qualifying felony offense of conviction, and where there are multiple qualifying felony offenses the terms shall be imposed CONSECUTIVELY. Mandatory. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: It is the intent of the Legislature that offenders who possess, carry, display, use, threaten to use, or attempt to use a semiautomatic firearm and its high-capacity detachable box magazine or a machine gun as defined in s. 790.001 be punished to the fullest extent of the law. The court shall impose the minimum term of imprisonment required under paragraph (a) for each qualifying felony offense for which the person is convicted. If the offender is convicted of multiple felony offenses for which paragraph (a) requires the imposition of a minimum term of imprisonment, the court shall impose any such terms of imprisonment consecutively.

rows.trigger: Discretionary consecutive sentencing. Where a felony enumerated in (3)(a)1. is committed in conjunction with any other felony NOT enumerated in (3)(a)1., the court MAY run the paragraph (a) term consecutive to the term for the non-enumerated felony. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: If an offender commits a felony enumerated in subparagraph (a)1. in conjunction with any other felony offense not enumerated in subparagraph (a)1., the court may impose any term of imprisonment provided for in paragraph (a) consecutively to any other term of imprisonment imposed for any other felony offense not enumerated in subparagraph (a)1.

rows.trigger: Definition, not a penalty provision. Gates ONLY the semiautomatic-firearm prong of the subsection (3) penalty ladder, NOT the disjunctive machine-gun prong, which carries no magazine or capacity requirement at all. The magazine must be capable of being loaded with MORE THAN 20 CENTERFIRE cartridges; a rimfire magazine of any capacity is outside the definition entirely. No min is typed: 21 would be an attribute of the magazine (the item itself is one magazine), not a count or valuation trigger of the provision, and typing it would falsely project a quantity floor onto machine-gun cases that have none. Also note (3)(a)2. and (3)(a)3. use the variant term 'high-capacity box magazine' (without 'detachable'), which the section never defines; only (3)(a)1. and this definition use the full defined term.
rows.quote: “High-capacity detachable box magazine” means any detachable box magazine, for use in a semiautomatic firearm, which is capable of being loaded with more than 20 centerfire cartridges.

rows.trigger: Definition of 'semiautomatic firearm' used throughout subsection (3). No penalty assigned, no threshold, no degree; scope is not typed because the row measures nothing. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: “Semiautomatic firearm” means a firearm which is capable of firing a series of rounds by separate successive depressions of the trigger and which uses the energy of discharge to perform a portion of the operating cycle.

rows.trigger: Defines 'possession' for all mandatory minimum provisions of this section: carrying the firearm on the person, or having it within immediate physical reach with ready access with intent to use it during the commission of the offense, proven beyond a reasonable doubt. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: For purposes of imposition of minimum mandatory sentencing provisions of this section, with respect to a firearm, the term “possession” is defined as carrying it on the person. Possession may also be proven by demonstrating that the defendant had the firearm within immediate physical reach with ready access with the intent to use the firearm during the commission of the offense, if proven beyond a reasonable doubt.

rows.trigger: Blanket exclusion from the entire section for law enforcement officers and United States military personnel performing lawful duties or traveling to or from their places of employment or assignment to perform those duties. NO dollar or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: This section does not apply to law enforcement officers or to United States military personnel who are performing their lawful duties or who are traveling to or from their places of employment or assignment to perform their lawful duties.

fs-800.04.title: Lewd or lascivious offenses committed upon or in the presence of persons less than 16 years of age

rows.trigger: Lewd or lascivious battery by engaging in sexual activity with a victim 12 years of age or older but less than 16. Offender age is not an element of this branch. Degree assigned by (4)(b) unless the (4)(c) prior-conviction enhancement applies.
rows.quote:
A person commits lewd or lascivious battery by:
1. Engaging in sexual activity with a person 12 years of age or older but less than 16 years of age; or

rows.trigger: Second subparagraph of the same paragraph, different conduct: encouraging, forcing, or enticing a person under 16 into sadomasochistic abuse, sexual bestiality, prostitution, or any other act involving sexual activity. NO LOWER AGE BOUND: min is null; the 12-year floor in (4)(a)1. does NOT carry over, so a victim of any age under 16 qualifies. No sexual activity by the offender is required. Degree assigned by (4)(b) unless (4)(c) applies.
rows.quote:
A person commits lewd or lascivious battery by:
...
2. Encouraging, forcing, or enticing any person less than 16 years of age to engage in sadomasochistic abuse, sexual bestiality, prostitution, or any other act involving sexual activity.

rows.trigger: General penalty for lewd or lascivious battery under (4)(a)1. or (4)(a)2.; offenders of any age; expressly subordinated to paragraph (c).
rows.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (c), an offender who commits lewd or lascivious battery commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Enhancement of lewd or lascivious battery: offender 18 years of age or older with AT LEAST ONE prior conviction of any of the seven enumerated predicates (scope is prior, so min counts prior convictions: 1 required, no upper bound). The predicates have NO MINIMUM SEVERITY: subparagraph 4. reaches all of chapter 794 (excluding s. 794.011(10)) at any degree, and subparagraph 7. reaches ANY prior violation of this section at any degree, including a third degree felony under (5)(d), (6)(c), or (7)(c) and a prior committed while the offender was under 18. Victim-age reach is supplied by (4)(a) and is not typed on this row: 12 to under 16 for sexual activity under (4)(a)1., ANY victim under 16 under (4)(a)2.

Definition of lewd or lascivious molestation. NO LOWER AGE BOUND: any victim less than 16. Covers both the offender touching the victim and forcing or enticing the victim to touch the perpetrator. Degree is assigned by (5)(b), (5)(c), (5)(d), or (5)(e).
rows.quote: A person who intentionally touches in a lewd or lascivious manner the breasts, genitals, genital area, or buttocks, or the clothing covering them, of a person less than 16 years of age, or forces or entices a person under 16 years of age to so touch the perpetrator, commits lewd or lascivious molestation.

rows.trigger: OFFENDER 18 YEARS OF AGE OR OLDER; victim less than 12 (no lower age bound, min null). CAUTION, typed-field collision: this row and (5)(c)1. are identical on scope/min/max and differ only by offender age, which the schema cannot type; offender age here (18 or older) is what makes this a LIFE felony rather than the second degree felony of (5)(c)1. Do not resolve degree from scope/min/max alone in the (5) grid. Punishment is directed specifically to s. 775.082(3)(a)4., not the general s. 775.082/775.083/775.084 string used elsewhere in this section.
rows.quote: An offender 18 years of age or older who commits lewd or lascivious molestation against a victim less than 12 years of age commits a life felony, punishable as provided in s. 775.082(3)(a)4.

rows.trigger: OFFENDER LESS THAN 18 YEARS OF AGE; victim less than 12 (no lower age bound, min null). CAUTION, typed-field collision: identical scope/min/max to (5)(b), which is a LIFE felony; the only differentiator is offender age (here under 18), stated in this trigger because the schema has no typed field for it. Degree supplied by flush closing language shared equally with subparagraph 2.
rows.quote:
1. An offender less than 18 years of age who commits lewd or lascivious molestation against a victim less than 12 years of age; or
...
commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: OFFENDER 18 YEARS OF AGE OR OLDER; victim 12 years of age or older but less than 16. CAUTION, typed-field collision: identical scope/min/max to (5)(d) (third degree, offender under 18) and (5)(e) (first degree, offender 18 or older with a qualifying prior); offender age and criminal history, which the schema cannot type here, are the only differentiators. Subparagraph 2. ends at the words 'less than 16 years of age'; the degree comes from flush closing language that governs subparagraphs 1. and 2. equally, quoted after the line break.
rows.quote:
2. An offender 18 years of age or older who commits lewd or lascivious molestation against a victim 12 years of age or older but less than 16 years of age
commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: OFFENDER LESS THAN 18 YEARS OF AGE; victim 12 years of age or older but less than 16. CAUTION, typed-field collision: identical scope/min/max to (5)(c)2. (second degree) and (5)(e) (first degree); offender age (here under 18) is the differentiator and lives only in this trigger.
rows.quote: An offender less than 18 years of age who commits lewd or lascivious molestation against a victim 12 years of age or older but less than 16 years of age commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Criminal-history enhancement of molestation: offender 18 years of age or older, victim 12 years of age or older but less than 16 (victim ages stated here in prose; min/max on this row count PRIOR CONVICTIONS because scope is prior: at least 1 qualifying prior required, no upper bound), previously convicted of any of the seven enumerated predicates. The predicates have NO MINIMUM SEVERITY: subparagraph 4. reaches all of chapter 794 (excluding s. 794.011(10)) at any degree, and subparagraph 7. reaches ANY prior violation of this section at any degree, including a third degree felony under (5)(d), (6)(c), or (7)(c) and a prior committed while the offender was under 18. This enhancement reaches only the 12-to-under-16 victim band; molestation of a victim under 12 by an offender 18 or older is already a life felony under (5)(b).

First branch of the lewd or lascivious conduct definition: intentional lewd or lascivious touching of a person under 16. NO LOWER AGE BOUND, min null. The words 'commits lewd or lascivious conduct' after the line break are flush closing language governing subparagraphs 1. and 2. equally. Degree assigned by (6)(b) or (6)(c).
rows.quote:
A person who:
1. Intentionally touches a person under 16 years of age in a lewd or lascivious manner; or
...
commits lewd or lascivious conduct.
