A person sentenced pursuant to this subparagraph is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(a).

rows.trigger: Juvenile capital track, non-killer branch: same elements as (1)(b)1. except the person did NOT actually kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill. Permissive ('may be punished'), NO minimum term stated (contrast the 40-year floor in (1)(b)1.). Sentence review under s. 921.1402(2)(c), and only where the term exceeds 15 years.
rows.quote: A person who did not actually kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill the victim and who is convicted under s. 782.04 of a capital felony, or an offense that was reclassified as a capital felony, which was committed before the person attained 18 years of age may be punished by a term of imprisonment for life or by a term of years equal to life if, after a sentencing hearing conducted by the court in accordance with s. 921.1401, the court finds that life imprisonment is an appropriate sentence. A person who is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 15 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(c).

rows.trigger: Operative allocator between the (1)(b)1. and (1)(b)2. tracks: mandatory written finding on sentence-review eligibility under s. 921.1402(2)(a) or (c), based on killing role. The court may find that MULTIPLE defendants killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the same victim, so more than one codefendant can be routed into the harsher (1)(b)1. track for a single death.
rows.quote: The court shall make a written finding as to whether a person is eligible for a sentence review hearing under s. 921.1402(2)(a) or (c). Such a finding shall be based upon whether the person actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim. The court may find that multiple defendants killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim.

rows.trigger: Contingent rule, no offense conduct triggers it: if the death penalty in a capital felony is held unconstitutional by the Florida Supreme Court or the U.S. Supreme Court, a person previously sentenced to death is brought back and resentenced to life as provided in subsection (1). Degree records the offense of conviction the rule operates on (capital felony), not a penalty it assigns.
rows.quote: In the event the death penalty in a capital felony is held to be unconstitutional by the Florida Supreme Court or the United States Supreme Court, the court having jurisdiction over a person previously sentenced to death for a capital felony shall cause such person to be brought before the court, and the court shall sentence such person to life imprisonment as provided in subsection (1).

rows.trigger: Opposite valence from the first sentence: a holding that a METHOD of execution is unconstitutional does NOT reduce any death sentence. Degree tagged 'capital felony' for the same reason as the first sentence and consistently with it: both sentences operate exclusively on death sentences for capital felonies (degree = offense of conviction operated on, not a penalty assigned).
rows.quote: No sentence of death shall be reduced as a result of a determination that a method of execution is held to be unconstitutional under the State Constitution or the Constitution of the United States.

rows.trigger: Unnumbered lead-in scoping paragraphs (3)(a)-(e): reaches any 'other designated felony' (every felony other than capital) and is permissive on its face ('may be punished as follows'); the degree figures that follow are ceilings, not mandates, except where another provision makes a term mandatory.
rows.quote: A person who has been convicted of any other designated felony may be punished as follows:

rows.trigger: Date-of-offense trigger: life felony committed BEFORE October 1, 1983. Life, or a term of at least 30 years. One of two life-felony tiers stating an express minimum term of years; the other is the 25-year split-sentence floor in (3)(a)4.a.(II).
rows.quote: For a life felony committed before October 1, 1983, by a term of imprisonment for life or for a term of at least 30 years.

rows.trigger: Date-of-offense trigger: life felony committed on or after October 1, 1983 (and, by operation of subparagraph 3., before July 1, 1995). The only life-felony tier with a term-of-years cap of 40 years.
rows.quote: For a life felony committed on or after October 1, 1983, by a term of imprisonment for life or by a term of imprisonment not exceeding 40 years.

rows.trigger: Date-of-offense trigger: life felony committed on or after July 1, 1995. Expressly subordinate to subparagraph 4. A term of years may run up to life, so no numeric ceiling below life.
rows.quote: Except as provided in subparagraph 4., for a life felony committed on or after July 1, 1995, by a term of imprisonment for life or by imprisonment for a term of years not exceeding life imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Chapeau only; the two alternative sentences (I) and (II) have their own rows because they differ materially. Trigger: life felony committed on or after September 1, 2005, which is a violation of s. 800.04(5)(b) (lewd or lascivious battery). Subordinate to sub-subparagraph b. Scope null: nothing is taken and no item narrows this; the narrowing is the offense of conviction via statutory cross-reference.
rows.quote: Except as provided in sub-subparagraph b., for a life felony committed on or after September 1, 2005, which is a violation of s. 800.04(5)(b), by:

rows.trigger: First alternative under the 4.a. chapeau: a term of imprisonment for life, full stop. A reader who stops here misses the structurally different alternative at (II).
rows.quote: A term of imprisonment for life; or

rows.trigger: Second alternative under the 4.a. chapeau, materially different from (I): a split sentence with a 25-year prison FLOOR (not exceeding life), followed by probation or community control for the remainder of the person's NATURAL LIFE under s. 948.012(4). The lifetime supervision tail exists only on this branch.
rows.quote: A split sentence that is a term of at least 25 years’ imprisonment and not exceeding life imprisonment, followed by probation or community control for the remainder of the person’s natural life, as provided in s. 948.012(4).

rows.trigger: The only genuinely recidivist provision in subsection (3): a life felony committed on or after July 1, 2008, which is the person's SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT violation of s. 800.04(5)(b). Mandatory life; the 4.a.(II) split-sentence option is unavailable. Scope 'prior' is literal here: prior criminal history is the narrowing element.
rows.quote: For a life felony committed on or after July 1, 2008, which is a person’s second or subsequent violation of s. 800.04(5)(b), by a term of imprisonment for life.

rows.trigger: Overrides subparagraphs 1.-4. Juvenile life-felony track: conviction under s. 782.04 of an offense RECLASSIFIED as a life felony, committed before age 18, after a s. 921.1401 hearing. Permissive ('may be punished'), no minimum term stated. Scope null: age at offense, not criminal history. Sub-subparagraphs a.-c. have their own rows.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding subparagraphs 1.-4., a person who is convicted under s. 782.04 of an offense that was reclassified as a life felony which was committed before the person attained 18 years of age may be punished by a term of imprisonment for life or by a term of years equal to life imprisonment if the judge conducts a sentencing hearing in accordance with s. 921.1401 and finds that life imprisonment or a term of years equal to life imprisonment is an appropriate sentence.

rows.trigger: Sentence-review entitlement on the (3)(a)5. juvenile life-felony track: person actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill AND is sentenced to more than 25 years; review under s. 921.1402(2)(b). Assigns no penalty; confers a right. Scope null: killing role and sentence length are not value, item, place, prior, victim-status, or dwelling narrowings in this schema's sense.
rows.quote: A person who actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim and is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 25 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(b).

rows.trigger: Lower-threshold twin of 5.a. on the same track: a person who did NOT kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill reviews at more than 15 years, ten years earlier than the killer branch. Review under s. 921.1402(2)(c). Scope null.
rows.quote: A person who did not actually kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill the victim and is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 15 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(c).

rows.trigger: Last sub-subparagraph of the paragraph: mandatory written finding allocating between the 5.a. and 5.b. review tracks, with the same multiple-defendants clause as (1)(b)3. -- several codefendants can be routed into the harsher 25-year track for a single death. Scope null.
rows.quote: The court shall make a written finding as to whether a person is eligible for a sentence review hearing under s. 921.1402(2)(b) or (c). Such a finding shall be based upon whether the person actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim. The court may find that multiple defendants killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim.

rows.trigger: Life felony committed on or after October 1, 2014, which is a violation of s. 787.06(3)(g) (human trafficking). MANDATORY life with no term-of-years alternative and no split-sentence option -- harsher than 4.a. Scope null: no item involved; the narrowing is the offense of conviction.
rows.quote: For a life felony committed on or after October 1, 2014, which is a violation of s. 787.06(3)(g), by a term of imprisonment for life.

rows.trigger: General first degree felony ceiling of 30 years -- but the second clause is critical: when another statute specifically so provides, punishable by a term of years NOT EXCEEDING LIFE. Reading only the first clause understates exposure from 30 years to life for every 'first degree felony punishable by life' offense.
rows.quote: For a felony of the first degree, by a term of imprisonment not exceeding 30 years or, when specifically provided by statute, by imprisonment for a term of years not exceeding life imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Overrides subparagraph 1. Juvenile track: conviction under s. 782.04 of a first degree felony punishable by a term of years not exceeding life (or an offense reclassified as such), committed before age 18, after a s. 921.1401 hearing. Scope null: age at offense, not criminal history. Sub-subparagraphs a.-c. have their own rows.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding subparagraph 1., a person convicted under s. 782.04 of a first degree felony punishable by a term of years not exceeding life imprisonment, or an offense that was reclassified as a first degree felony punishable by a term of years not exceeding life, which was committed before the person attained 18 years of age may be punished by a term of years equal to life imprisonment if the judge conducts a sentencing hearing in accordance with s. 921.1401 and finds that a term of years equal to life imprisonment is an appropriate sentence.

rows.trigger: Review entitlement on the juvenile first-degree-punishable-by-life track: killed / intended to kill / attempted to kill AND sentenced to more than 25 years; review under s. 921.1402(2)(b). Textually identical to (3)(a)5.a. but attaches to a different offense class, so both exist as separate rows. Scope null.
rows.quote: A person who actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim and is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 25 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(b).

rows.trigger: Review at more than 15 years where the person did not kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill; review under s. 921.1402(2)(c). Scope null.
rows.quote: A person who did not actually kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill the victim and is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 15 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(c).

rows.trigger: Last sub-subparagraph of the paragraph: mandatory written finding allocating between the 2.a. and 2.b. review tracks, including the multiple-defendants clause. Scope null.
rows.quote: The court shall make a written finding as to whether a person is eligible for a sentence review hearing under s. 921.1402(2)(b) or (c). Such a finding shall be based upon whether the person actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim. The court may find that multiple defendants killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim.

rows.trigger: Juvenile catch-all overriding paragraphs (a) and (b): any offense NOT included in s. 782.04 that is a life felony, or punishable by life or by a term of years not exceeding life, or reclassified as such, committed before age 18. Degree spans multiple degrees deliberately, so none is assigned. Sentence review under s. 921.1402(2)(d) where the term exceeds 20 years -- a third distinct threshold -- and this paragraph has NO written-finding subparagraph. Scope null: age at offense, not criminal history.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding paragraphs (a) and (b), a person convicted of an offense that is not included in s. 782.04 but that is an offense that is a life felony or is punishable by a term of imprisonment for life or by a term of years not exceeding life imprisonment, or an offense that was reclassified as a life felony or an offense punishable by a term of imprisonment for life or by a term of years not exceeding life imprisonment, which was committed before the person attained 18 years of age may be punished by a term of imprisonment for life or a term of years equal to life imprisonment if the judge conducts a sentencing hearing in accordance with s. 921.1401 and finds that life imprisonment or a term of years equal to life imprisonment is an appropriate sentence. A person who is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 20 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(d).

rows.trigger: Applies to any offense a substantive statute grades a second degree felony, whatever the trigger in that statute. A CEILING, not a term: it is the exposure carried by F.S. 812.014(2)(b)2. (cargo) at ANY value including zero, and by every degree-graded second degree felony with no value element. Compare (9)(a)3.c., where 15 years is a flat mandatory term.
rows.quote: For a felony of the second degree, by a term of imprisonment not exceeding 15 years.

rows.trigger: Applies to any offense graded a third degree felony. A ceiling, not a term. Subject to the mandatory nonstate prison sanction in subsection (10) and, in the opposite direction, to the flat 5-year prison releasee reoffender term in (9)(a)3.d.
rows.quote: For a felony of the third degree, by a term of imprisonment not exceeding 5 years.

rows.trigger: Unnumbered lead-in scoping paragraphs (4)(a) and (4)(b): reaches a person convicted of a 'designated misdemeanor' and is permissive ('may be sentenced as follows').
rows.quote: A person who has been convicted of a designated misdemeanor may be sentenced as follows:

rows.trigger: Any offense graded a first degree misdemeanor. The term is a DEFINITE term: subsection (6) preserves indeterminate sentencing generally, but this paragraph forecloses it here.
rows.quote: For a misdemeanor of the first degree, by a definite term of imprisonment not exceeding 1 year;

rows.trigger: Any offense graded a second degree misdemeanor. Source of the familiar '60-day misdemeanor' figure, correct only where the substantive statute actually grades the conduct second degree. Also a definite term.
rows.quote: For a misdemeanor of the second degree, by a definite term of imprisonment not exceeding 60 days.

rows.trigger: The statute names its own class here -- NONCRIMINAL VIOLATION -- which is outside this table's degree enum, so degree is 'no degree assigned' and the class is recorded in this trigger instead (the audited version's 'noncriminal violation' degree value violated the typed field). Ceiling: no imprisonment, nothing more severe than a fine, forfeiture, or other civil penalty. Genuine open-ended carve-out: 'except as provided in chapter 316 or by ordinance of any city or county,' so a local ordinance can in terms exceed this ceiling; chapter 316 and ordinances were not read.
rows.quote: Any person who has been convicted of a noncriminal violation may not be sentenced to a term of imprisonment nor to any other punishment more severe than a fine, forfeiture, or other civil penalty, except as provided in chapter 316 or by ordinance of any city or county.

rows.trigger: Savings clause preserving every Florida statute authorizing an INDETERMINATE sentence within statutory minimum and maximum limits, except as provided in subsection (1). The fixed ceilings in subsection (3) are not the whole picture; only the capital-felony rules in (1) override an indeterminate structure.
rows.quote: Nothing in this section shall be construed to alter the operation of any statute of this state authorizing a trial court, in its discretion, to impose a sentence of imprisonment for an indeterminate period within minimum and maximum limits as provided by law, except as provided in subsection (1).

rows.trigger: Preserves authority to decree forfeiture of property, suspend or cancel a license, remove a person from office, or impose any other civil penalty, and allows such a judgment or order to be included in the sentence. Real exposure sitting outside every term-of-imprisonment row in this table.
rows.quote: This section does not deprive the court of any authority conferred by law to decree a forfeiture of property, suspend or cancel a license, remove a person from office, or impose any other civil penalty. Such a judgment or order may be included in the sentence.

rows.trigger: Applicability by offense date, with degree carve-outs on its face: the October 1, 1983 guidelines apply to all felonies EXCEPT capital felonies committed 10/1/1983 through 12/31/1993, and to felonies committed BEFORE 10/1/1983 except capital AND life felonies, only when the defendant affirmatively elects them -- the only defendant-elective sentencing structure in the section. Scope null: the carve-outs are degree classes, not any enum axis; they are recorded here, not in the typed field.
rows.quote: The sentencing guidelines that were effective October 1, 1983, and any revisions thereto, apply to all felonies, except capital felonies, committed on or after October 1, 1983, and before January 1, 1994, and to all felonies, except capital felonies and life felonies, committed before October 1, 1983, when the defendant affirmatively selects to be sentenced pursuant to such provisions.

rows.trigger: The 1994 sentencing guidelines apply to all felonies except capital felonies committed on or after January 1, 1994, and before October 1, 1995. Scope null; degree carve-out recorded here.
rows.quote: The 1994 sentencing guidelines, that were effective January 1, 1994, and any revisions thereto, apply to all felonies, except capital felonies, committed on or after January 1, 1994, and before October 1, 1995.

rows.trigger: The 1995 sentencing guidelines apply to all felonies except capital felonies committed on or after October 1, 1995, and before October 1, 1998. Scope null; degree carve-out recorded here.
rows.quote: The 1995 sentencing guidelines that were effective October 1, 1995, and any revisions thereto, apply to all felonies, except capital felonies, committed on or after October 1, 1995, and before October 1, 1998.

rows.trigger: The foundation of the `level` column: the Criminal Punishment Code applies to all felonies except capital felonies committed on or after October 1, 1998, switching on the s. 921.0022 ranking chart and s. 921.0023 defaults that every `level` field depends on. Second sentence is its own rule: any revision to the Code applies to felonies committed on or after the revision's effective date, so the applicable version floats with the offense date. Scope null.
rows.quote: The Criminal Punishment Code applies to all felonies, except capital felonies, committed on or after October 1, 1998. Any revision to the Criminal Punishment Code applies to sentencing for all felonies, except capital felonies, committed on or after the effective date of the revision.

rows.trigger: Last paragraph of subsection (8): continuing-enterprise felonies (except capital felonies) are sentenced under the guidelines or Criminal Punishment Code in effect on the BEGINNING date of the criminal activity, not the ending date and not the date of any individual act. For a scheme spanning a structural change this can move the entire sentencing regime backward by years. Scope null.
rows.quote: Felonies, except capital felonies, with continuing dates of enterprise shall be sentenced under the sentencing guidelines or the Criminal Punishment Code in effect on the beginning date of the criminal activity.

rows.trigger: Sixteen ENUMERATED NAMED OFFENSES qualifying a defendant as a prison releasee reoffender, reaching attempts as well ('commits, or attempts to commit'). This row covers only the named entries; sub-subparagraphs o. and r. are structurally different and have their own rows -- the quote is elided at o. and before r., marked with ellipses. Scope 'prior' because this row is part of the recidivist 'prison releasee reoffender' status definition, whose narrowing axis is criminal history (prior incarceration and release supplied by the closing flush text); tagged uniformly with o., r., the closing text, and (9)(a)2. so the one predicate list carries one field type throughout.
rows.quote: “Prison releasee reoffender” means any defendant who commits, or attempts to commit: a. Treason; b. Murder; c. Manslaughter; d. Sexual battery; e. Carjacking; f. Home-invasion robbery; g. Robbery; h. Arson; i. Kidnapping; j. Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; k. Aggravated battery; l. Aggravated stalking; m. Aircraft piracy; n. Unlawful throwing, placing, or discharging of a destructive device or bomb; ... p. Armed burglary; q. Burglary of a dwelling or burglary of an occupied structure; or ...

rows.trigger: THE STRUCTURAL TRAP THIS REPAIR EXISTS TO SURFACE, same shape as F.S. 812.014(2)(b)2. and F.S. 817.568(2)(b): a list whose neighbors are named offenses and whose middle entry is an OPEN-ENDED CATEGORY with no floor. 'Any felony that involves the use or threat of physical force or violence against an individual' -- no enumerated floor, NO DEGREE FLOOR, reaches a felony of ANY degree including third degree, satisfied by mere THREAT with no force used, no weapon, no injury. Consequence: the (9)(a)3. mandatory minimums attach to ANY violent felony whatsoever, not merely the sixteen named crimes; a third degree felony involving a threat draws a flat 5 years at 100 percent under (9)(a)3.d. and (9)(b). Degree null because this sub-subparagraph assigns none -- read that as EVERY felony degree, never as no exposure. Scope 'prior': part of the recidivist PRR status definition, tagged uniformly with the rest of the a.-r. list.
rows.quote: Any felony that involves the use or threat of physical force or violence against an individual;

rows.trigger: Third structurally different entry in the same list, and the LAST sub-subparagraph -- the terminal position a reader who found an answer earlier never reaches. A statutory cross-reference list: ANY felony violation of s. 790.07 (weapons during a felony), s. 800.04 (lewd or lascivious offenses on a person under 16), s. 827.03 (child abuse), s. 827.071 (sexual performance by a child), or s. 847.0135(5) (lewd computer solicitation). 'Any felony violation' means every felony degree under each cited section qualifies, with no violence element required. The five cited sections were not read, so the full qualifying set is unverified. Scope 'prior': part of the recidivist PRR status definition, tagged uniformly with the rest of the list.

Unnumbered flush text following r. supplying the TIMING ELEMENT for every entry a.-r.: the qualifying offense must be committed within 3 YEARS after release. Three release sources count: a state correctional facility (DOC or private vendor); a COUNTY detention facility following incarceration for an offense for which the sentence pronounced was a prison sentence; and a correctional institution of another state, D.C., the United States, any U.S. possession or territory, or ANY FOREIGN JURISDICTION, following incarceration for an offense punishable by more than 1 year IN THIS STATE -- equivalence measured by Florida's punishment, not the sentencing jurisdiction's. The 3-year figure is a temporal gate, not a value element, so min/max stay null.
rows.quote: within 3 years after being released from a state correctional facility operated by the Department of Corrections or a private vendor, a county detention facility following incarceration for an offense for which the sentence pronounced was a prison sentence, or a correctional institution of another state, the District of Columbia, the United States, any possession or territory of the United States, or any foreign jurisdiction, following incarceration for an offense for which the sentence is punishable by more than 1 year in this state.

rows.trigger: A second definitional PRR pathway with no release-date trigger and no 3-year window: any offense listed in (a)1.a.-r. committed WHILE SERVING a prison sentence or on ESCAPE STATUS (state, out-of-state, federal, territorial, or foreign institution). Incorporates the whole a.-r. list, so it carries the open-ended (9)(a)1.o. catch-all with it. CAVEAT ON THE FACE OF THE TEXT: the election clause in (9)(a)3.'s first sentence authorizes the state attorney to seek PRR sentencing only for a defendant 'as defined in subparagraph 1.' -- it does not cite this subparagraph -- while (9)(a)3.'s second sentence broadens to 'as defined in this section.' Whether the election mechanism reaches subparagraph-2 reoffenders is an asymmetry the statutory text does not resolve; this row therefore does not claim the pathway is fully independent of subparagraph 1. for election purposes, only that the definition is.
rows.quote: “Prison releasee reoffender” also means any defendant who commits or attempts to commit any offense listed in sub-subparagraphs (a)1.a.-r. while the defendant was serving a prison sentence or on escape status from a state correctional facility operated by the Department of Corrections or a private vendor or while the defendant was on escape status from a correctional institution of another state, the District of Columbia, the United States, any possession or territory of the United States, or any foreign jurisdiction, following incarceration for an offense for which the sentence is punishable by more than 1 year in this state.

rows.trigger: PRR sentencing is ELECTIVE with the state attorney ('may seek'), the burden is PREPONDERANCE of the evidence, and a proven PRR defendant is NOT eligible for guidelines sentencing. TEXTUAL ASYMMETRY, flagged rather than glossed: the first sentence's election clause reaches only a reoffender 'as defined in subparagraph 1.', while the second sentence's mandatory-sentencing clause reaches one 'as defined in this section' (which includes subparagraph 2.). How a subparagraph-2 reoffender enters the election mechanism is not resolved by this text.
rows.quote: If the state attorney determines that a defendant is a prison releasee reoffender as defined in subparagraph 1., the state attorney may seek to have the court sentence the defendant as a prison releasee reoffender. Upon proof from the state attorney that establishes by a preponderance of the evidence that a defendant is a prison releasee reoffender as defined in this section, such defendant is not eligible for sentencing under the sentencing guidelines and must be sentenced as follows:

rows.trigger: PRR term for 'a felony punishable by life' -- the statute names no degree, only a punishment class, so degree is not guessed. MANDATORY LIFE. The predicate is any offense in (9)(a)1.a.-r., which includes the open-ended violent-felony category at o. and the cross-reference list at r., not a closed list of sixteen named crimes. Under (9)(b), release only by expiration of sentence; under (9)(c) a court may go higher; under (9)(d)1. the state attorney may decline for extenuating circumstances.
rows.quote: For a felony punishable by life, by a term of imprisonment for life;

rows.trigger: PRR: a FLAT MANDATORY 30 years, not a maximum -- contrast (3)(b)1., where 30 years is a ceiling. Predicate includes the open-ended (9)(a)1.o. category and the r. cross-references. Served at 100 percent with no early release under (9)(b); may be exceeded under (9)(c), including under s. 775.084.
rows.quote: For a felony of the first degree, by a term of imprisonment of 30 years;

rows.trigger: PRR: a FLAT MANDATORY 15 years, not a maximum. Compare (3)(d), where 15 years is the CEILING for the same degree -- a PRR second degree felony is sentenced at the statutory maximum with no discretion below it. Predicate includes the unbounded (9)(a)1.o. category and the r. cross-references. Served at 100 percent under (9)(b); may be exceeded under (9)(c).
rows.quote: For a felony of the second degree, by a term of imprisonment of 15 years; and

rows.trigger: PRR: a FLAT MANDATORY 5 years, which is also the statutory maximum for the degree under (3)(e), so there is no room below it. THE PREDICATE IS NOT A CLOSED LIST: via (9)(a)1.o., any felony involving the use or THREAT of physical force or violence against an individual qualifies, at any degree. A defendant whose new offense is an ordinary third degree felony involving nothing more than a threat, committed within 3 years of release under (9)(a)1. or while serving a sentence or on escape status under (9)(a)2., draws a flat 5 years served at 100 percent under (9)(b), and the court may impose more under (9)(c). Also reachable via (9)(a)1.r. through any felony violation of ss. 790.07, 800.04, 827.03, 827.071, or 847.0135(5).
rows.quote: For a felony of the third degree, by a term of imprisonment of 5 years.

rows.trigger: What converts all four (9)(a)3. terms from nominal sentences into true mandatory minimums: release ONLY by expiration of sentence, no eligibility for parole, control release, or ANY form of early release, and 100 PERCENT of the court-imposed sentence must be served. Applies to every tier -- life, 30, 15, and 5 years. Scope null (corrected from 'prior'): this is a service-of-sentence rule conditioned on having been sentenced under paragraph (a), not a criminal-history narrowing.
rows.quote: A person sentenced under paragraph (a) shall be released only by expiration of sentence and shall not be eligible for parole, control release, or any form of early release. Any person sentenced under paragraph (a) must serve 100 percent of the court-imposed sentence.

rows.trigger: The PRR terms in (9)(a)3. are FLOORS, not ceilings: nothing in subsection (9) prevents a court from imposing a GREATER sentence as authorized by law, expressly including under s. 775.084 or any other provision. Applies to all four tiers. Scope null (corrected from 'prior'): a savings clause with no criminal-history element of its own.
rows.quote: Nothing in this subsection shall prevent a court from imposing a greater sentence of incarceration as authorized by law, pursuant to s. 775.084 or any other provision of law.

rows.trigger: The discretion valve on an otherwise mandatory scheme: qualifying offenders are to be punished to the fullest extent UNLESS the state attorney determines extenuating circumstances exist which preclude just prosecution, expressly including whether the VICTIM recommends against PRR sentencing. Read with the (9)(a)3. lead-in, PRR is prosecutorially elective, not automatic. Scope 'prior' is literal here: the provision is expressly keyed to 'offenders previously released from prison or a county detention facility following incarceration.'
rows.quote: It is the intent of the Legislature that offenders previously released from prison or a county detention facility following incarceration for an offense for which the sentence pronounced was a prison sentence who meet the criteria in paragraph (a) be punished to the fullest extent of the law and as provided in this subsection, unless the state attorney determines that extenuating circumstances exist which preclude the just prosecution of the offender, including whether the victim recommends that the offender not be sentenced as provided in this subsection.

rows.trigger: Accountability mechanism for the (9)(d)1. valve, and the last subparagraph of the last paragraph of subsection (9): for every case where the offender meets the paragraph (a) criteria and does not receive the mandatory minimum, the state attorney must explain the deviation IN WRITING in the case file. Scope null (corrected from 'prior'): a recordkeeping mandate on the state attorney, not a criminal-history narrowing.
rows.quote: For every case in which the offender meets the criteria in paragraph (a) and does not receive the mandatory minimum prison sentence, the state attorney must explain the sentencing deviation in writing and place such explanation in the case file maintained by the state attorney.

rows.trigger: Mandatory NONSTATE PRISON SANCTION -- the only mitigating mandate in the section. Requires ALL of: offense on or after July 1, 2009; third degree felony; NOT a forcible felony under s. 776.08; NOT any third degree felony violation under chapter 810; and total sentence points under s. 921.0024 are 22 OR FEWER. The 22-point gate is a numeric sentence-points threshold, not a dollar or property-value element, so min/max stay null. Escape hatch: state prison on written findings of danger to the public. Tension with (9)(a)3.d.: a PRR-qualified third degree felon is ineligible for guidelines sentencing and faces a flat 5 years, and the forcible-felony exclusion here is often triggered by the same conduct that satisfies (9)(a)1.o.
rows.quote: If a defendant is sentenced for an offense committed on or after July 1, 2009, which is a third degree felony but not a forcible felony as defined in s. 776.08, and excluding any third degree felony violation under chapter 810, and if the total sentence points pursuant to s. 921.0024 are 22 points or fewer, the court must sentence the offender to a nonstate prison sanction. However, if the court makes written findings that a nonstate prison sanction could present a danger to the public, the court may sentence the offender to a state correctional facility pursuant to this section.

rows.trigger: Final subsection: a reference to this section constitutes a GENERAL reference under the doctrine of incorporation by reference, so every substantive statute saying 'punishable as provided in s. 775.082' absorbs later amendments to this section automatically rather than freezing the version in force at its own enactment.
rows.quote: The purpose of this section is to provide uniform punishment for those crimes made punishable under this section and, to this end, a reference to this section constitutes a general reference under the doctrine of incorporation by reference.

rows.trigger: CRITICAL FRAMING. This entire section assigns NO degree of offense to anything and contains NO dollar amounts anywhere (verified by scanning the full operative text, subsection (1)(a) through the History note: zero dollar figures). It is the sentencing-computation statute: scoresheet points, multipliers, and the lowest permissible sentence. Degrees come from the substantive offense statutes; severity levels come from s. 921.0022 and s. 921.0023. Every row below therefore carries degree 'no degree assigned' and null min/max, and no row here may be read as grading any crime.

rows.quote: WORKSHEET KEY: Legal status points are assessed when any form of legal status existed at the time the offender committed an offense before the court for sentencing. Four (4) sentence points are assessed for an offender’s legal status.

rows.trigger: Community sanction violation before the court: 6 points for each violation and each successive violation. The 6-point figure is the DEFAULT ONLY: the sentence ends in 'unless any of the following apply' and is followed by subparagraphs 1. and 2., which raise it to 12 or 24. Do not quote the 6-point figure without reading both subparagraphs and sub-subparagraphs 2.a. and 2.b.
rows.quote: Community sanction violation points are assessed when a community sanction violation is before the court for sentencing. Six (6) sentence points are assessed for each community sanction violation and each successive community sanction violation, unless any of the following apply:

rows.quote: 1. If the community sanction violation includes a new felony conviction before the sentencing court, twelve (12) community sanction violation points are assessed for the violation, and for each successive community sanction violation involving a new felony conviction.

Requires that the violation of felony probation or community control does NOT include a new felony conviction (sub-sub I.) AND is not based solely on failure to pay costs, fines, or restitution (sub-sub II.); conditions I. and II. are conjunctive ('and'). Result is 12 points per violation and each successive violation. The violation does not include a new felony conviction; and II. The community sanction violation is not based solely on the probationer or offender’s failure to pay costs or fines or make restitution payments.

Under the same s. 948.06 gateway in subparagraph 2., a violation of felony probation or community control that DOES include a new felony conviction: 24 points, per violation and each successive violation. This sub-subparagraph sits after 2.a. and its two sub-subs; a reader who answers the question at 2.a.I. and stops will miss it. rows.quote: b. Twenty-four (24) community sanction violation points are assessed for the violation and for each successive violation of felony probation or community control where the violation includes a new felony conviction.

rows.trigger: Anti-stacking rule closing the community sanction violation key. Multiple counts of community sanction violations before the sentencing court cannot multiply the assessment. Note the tension with the 'each successive violation' language in the tiers above: successive violations multiply, multiple counts of one violation do not.
rows.quote: Multiple counts of community sanction violations before the sentencing court shall not be a basis for multiplying the assessment of community sanction violation points.

rows.trigger: Prior serious felony points. Requires BOTH a primary or additional offense ranked level 8, 9, or 10 AND one or more prior serious felonies. A SINGLE 30-point assessment, not per prior. Definition sentence adds a recency requirement: the prior must be one the offender is still serving, or whose later of release-from-confinement/supervision/sanction date falls within 3 years before the date the primary or any additional offense was committed. Carrier line on the worksheet face is 'PRIOR SERIOUS FELONY'.
rows.quote: Prior serious felony points: If the offender has a primary offense or any additional offense ranked in level 8, level 9, or level 10, and one or more prior serious felonies, a single assessment of thirty (30) points shall be added. For purposes of this section, a prior serious felony is an offense in the offender’s prior record that is ranked in level 8, level 9, or level 10 under s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 and for which the offender is serving a sentence of confinement, supervision, or other sanction or for which the offender’s date of release from confinement, supervision, or other sanction, whichever is later, is within 3 years before the date the primary offense or any additional offense was committed.

rows.trigger: Prior capital felony points. Not a flat figure: one or more prior capital felonies adds points equal to TWICE the points received for the primary offense and any additional offense, added to the subtotal. Definition sweeps in pleas of nolo contendere or guilty as well as findings of guilt, and out-of-state felonies that are capital there or would be capital if committed in Florida. Carrier line on the worksheet face is 'PRIOR CAPITAL FELONY'.
rows.quote: Prior capital felony points: If the offender has one or more prior capital felonies in the offender’s criminal record, points shall be added to the subtotal sentence points of the offender equal to twice the number of points the offender receives for the primary offense and any additional offense. A prior capital felony in the offender’s criminal record is a previous capital felony offense for which the offender has entered a plea of nolo contendere or guilty or has been found guilty; or a felony in another jurisdiction which is a capital felony in that jurisdiction, or would be a capital felony if the offense were committed in this state.

Note the carve-out cross-reference differs from tier one: s. 775.087(3) here versus s. 775.087(2) for the 18-point tier. Applies to attempts and to mere possession without use. Same carrier line on the worksheet face, 'FIREARM OR SEMIAUTOMATIC WEAPON'.
rows.quote: ... or if the offender is convicted of committing or attempting to commit any felony other than those enumerated in s. 775.087(3) while having in his or her possession a semiautomatic firearm as defined in s. 775.087(3) or a machine gun as defined in s. 790.001, an additional twenty-five (25) sentence points are assessed.

rows.trigger: Organizing heading that separates the additive point provisions above from the multiplicative provisions below. EIGHT multiplier paragraphs follow this line: aggravated animal cruelty (1.25x), drug trafficking (1.5x, discretionary), justice system personnel (three tiers, 2.5x / 2.0x / 1.5x, one row each below), grand theft of a motor vehicle (1.5x), fleeing or eluding (1.5x), criminal gang (1.5x), domestic violence in the presence of a child (1.5x), adult-on-minor sex offense (2.0x). Every one of them multiplies the SUBTOTAL sentence points, not the total. Only seven have a checkbox on the (1)(a) worksheet face; fleeing or eluding does not.
rows.quote: Sentencing multipliers:

rows.trigger: Multiplier, aggravated animal cruelty, 1.25x on the subtotal. Turns on the primary offense being a violation of s. 828.12(2) plus a conduct element (knowing and intentional torture or torment that injured, mutilated, or killed the animal); not graded by any item taken, possessed, or valued. The s. 379.303 language defines what counts as an 'animal' and carves out agricultural animals and permitted captive wildlife, a definitional exclusion, not an item-based grading tier. Lowest multiplier in the section.
rows.quote: Aggravated Animal Cruelty: If the primary offense is aggravated animal cruelty under s. 828.12(2), which included the knowing and intentional torture or torment of an animal that injured, mutilated, or killed the animal, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.25. As used in this paragraph, the term “animal” does not include an animal used for agricultural purposes or permitted as captive wildlife as authorized under s. 379.303.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, drug trafficking, 1.5x on the subtotal. Two limits that are easy to skip: the multiplier applies only to a level 7 or level 8 offense, and it is DISCRETIONARY ('at the discretion of the court'), unlike every other multiplier in this key, which are all mandatory in form. Second sentence adds a downward mechanism: the state attorney may move to reduce or suspend for substantial assistance under s. 893.135(4).
rows.quote: Drug trafficking: If the primary offense is drug trafficking under s. 893.135, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied, at the discretion of the court, for a level 7 or level 8 offense, by 1.5. The state attorney may move the sentencing court to reduce or suspend the sentence of a person convicted of a level 7 or level 8 offense, if the offender provides substantial assistance as described in s. 893.135(4).

rows.trigger: Multiplier, violent offenses against specified justice system personnel, TIER ONE of three packed one-per-sentence into a single paragraph: 2.5x on the subtotal where the primary offense is a violation of s. 775.0823(2), (3), or (4). This is the largest multiplier anywhere in this section, larger than the 2.0x adult-on-minor multiplier. STOPPING AT THIS SENTENCE LOSES TWO THIRDS OF THE RULE: the same paragraph continues into a 2.0x tier and a 1.5x tier, carried in the next two rows. No statutory-maximum cap is attached to any of the three tiers, unlike the gang and adult-on-minor multipliers. Worksheet face carrier is 'LAW ENF. PROTECT.'.
rows.quote: Violent offenses committed against specified justice system personnel: If the primary offense is a violation of s. 775.0823(2), (3), or (4), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 2.5. ...

rows.trigger: Multiplier, justice system personnel, TIER TWO, second sentence of the same paragraph: 2.0x on the subtotal where the primary offense is a violation of s. 775.0823(5), (6), (7), (8), or (9). Distinct subsection list from the 2.5x tier; no statutory-maximum cap. Same worksheet face carrier, 'LAW ENF. PROTECT.'.
rows.quote: ... If the primary offense is a violation of s. 775.0823(5), (6), (7), (8), or (9), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 2.0. ...

rows.trigger: Multiplier, justice system personnel, TIER THREE, third and last sentence of the same paragraph: 1.5x on the subtotal where the primary offense is a violation of s. 784.07(3) or s. 775.0875(1), or s. 775.0823(10) or (11). The only tier of the three reaching outside s. 775.0823. No statutory-maximum cap. Same worksheet face carrier, 'LAW ENF. PROTECT.'.
rows.quote: ... If the primary offense is a violation of s. 784.07(3) or s. 775.0875(1), or s. 775.0823(10) or (11), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, grand theft of a motor vehicle, 1.5x on the subtotal. Conjunctive: the primary offense must be grand theft of the THIRD DEGREE involving a motor vehicle AND the prior record must contain THREE OR MORE third-degree grand thefts involving a motor vehicle. The degree label 'third degree' is imported from the theft statute; nothing here assigns it. No dollar threshold appears in this provision even though the underlying theft grading is value-based; the multiplier keys off the degree and the count of priors only.
rows.quote: Grand theft of a motor vehicle: If the primary offense is grand theft of the third degree involving a motor vehicle and in the offender’s prior record, there are three or more grand thefts of the third degree involving a motor vehicle, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, fleeing or attempting to elude, 1.5x on the subtotal. Primary offense must be fleeing or attempting to elude a law enforcement officer, or aggravated fleeing or eluding, under s. 316.1935, plus ONE OR MORE prior s. 316.1935 violations in the record. Only one prior is required, in contrast to the three required by the motor vehicle theft multiplier immediately above. CONFIRMED BY AUDIT: this is the one multiplier in (1)(b) with NO corresponding checkbox on the (1)(a) worksheet face.
rows.quote: Fleeing or attempting to elude a law enforcement officer: If the primary offense is fleeing or attempting to elude a law enforcement officer or aggravated fleeing or eluding in violation of s. 316.1935, and in the offender’s prior record, there is one or more violation of s. 316.1935, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, offense related to a criminal gang, 1.5x on the subtotal, where the offense was committed for the purpose of benefiting, promoting, or furthering a criminal gang as defined in s. 874.03. SECOND SENTENCE IS A CAP AND IS EASY TO MISS: if applying the multiplier would push the lowest permissible sentence above the chapter 775 statutory maximum for the primary offense, the court may NOT apply the multiplier and must impose the statutory maximum. This runs in the opposite direction from the override in subsection (2), which says a code sentence exceeding the statutory maximum must be imposed; the cap here is specific to this multiplier.
rows.quote: Offense related to a criminal gang: If the offender is convicted of the primary offense and committed that offense for the purpose of benefiting, promoting, or furthering the interests of a criminal gang as defined in s. 874.03, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5. If applying the multiplier results in the lowest permissible sentence exceeding the statutory maximum sentence for the primary offense under chapter 775, the court may not apply the multiplier and must sentence the defendant to the statutory maximum sentence.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, domestic violence in the presence of a child, 1.5x on the subtotal. Requires the primary offense to be a crime of domestic violence as defined in s. 741.28, committed in the presence of a child UNDER 16 who is a family or household member as defined in s. 741.28(3) with the victim or perpetrator. NO statutory-maximum cap is attached to this multiplier, unlike the gang and adult-on-minor multipliers. Worksheet face carrier reads 'DOMESTIC VIOLENCE IN THE PRESENCE OF RELATED CHILD'.
rows.quote: Domestic violence in the presence of a child: If the offender is convicted of the primary offense and the primary offense is a crime of domestic violence, as defined in s. 741.28, which was committed in the presence of a child under 16 years of age who is a family or household member as defined in s. 741.28(3) with the victim or perpetrator, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, adult-on-minor sex offense, 2.0x on the subtotal, and the last multiplier in the key. Gateway conditions: offender 18 or older, victim under 18 at the time of the primary offense, and the primary offense committed on or after October 1, 2014. The predicate list is a semicolon-separated series with SIX branches, only the first of which carries the extra 'in the course of committing that violation' requirement: (i) s. 787.01(2) or s. 787.02(2) where the victim was a minor and the defendant committed a sexual battery under ch. 794 or a lewd act under s. 800.04 or s. 847.0135(5) against the minor; (ii) s. 787.01(3)(a)2. or 3.; (iii) s. 787.02(3)(a)2. or 3.; (iv) s. 794.011 excluding s. 794.011(10); (v) s. 800.04; (vi) s. 847.0135(5). Branches (ii) through (vi) carry no in-the-course-of element. Final sentence is the same statutory-maximum cap as the gang multiplier.
rows.quote: Adult-on-minor sex offense: If the offender was 18 years of age or older and the victim was younger than 18 years of age at the time the offender committed the primary offense, and if the primary offense was an offense committed on or after October 1, 2014, and is a violation of s. 787.01(2) or s. 787.02(2), if the violation involved a victim who was a minor and, in the course of committing that violation, the defendant committed a sexual battery under chapter 794 or a lewd act under s. 800.04 or s. 847.0135(5) against the minor; s. 787.01(3)(a)2. or 3.; s. 787.02(3)(a)2. or 3.; s. 794.011, excluding s. 794.011(10); s. 800.04; or s. 847.0135(5), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 2.0. If applying the multiplier results in the lowest permissible sentence exceeding the statutory maximum sentence for the primary offense under chapter 775, the court may not apply the multiplier and must sentence the defendant to the statutory maximum sentence.

rows.trigger: Total sentence points equal to or less than 44. Prescribes the sanction directly by point score, not by offense degree. Note the discretionary escape hatch in the same sentence: the court may still impose a prison sentence up to the statutory maximum notwithstanding the sub-44 score.
rows.quote: The lowest permissible sentence is the minimum sentence that may be imposed by the trial court, absent a valid reason for departure. The lowest permissible sentence is any nonstate prison sanction in which the total sentence points equals or is less than 44 points, unless the court determines within its discretion that a prison sentence, which may be up to the statutory maximums for the offenses committed, is appropriate.

rows.trigger: Total sentence points exceed 44. Prescribes a term directly by arithmetic formula: subtract 28 from the total points, then reduce the remainder by 25 percent; the result is the lowest permissible sentence expressed in prison months.
rows.quote: When the total sentence points exceeds 44 points, the lowest permissible sentence in prison months shall be calculated by subtracting 28 points from the total sentence points and decreasing the remaining total by 25 percent.

rows.trigger: Defines the top of the permissible range as the statutory maximum under s. 775.082 for the primary offense and any additional offenses before the court, and authorizes concurrent or consecutive sentences. The maximum is imported from s. 775.082, not assigned here. First sentence also limits the role of the point total: it exists only to fix the floor.
rows.quote: The total sentence points shall be calculated only as a means of determining the lowest permissible sentence. The permissible range for sentencing shall be the lowest permissible sentence up to and including the statutory maximum, as defined in s. 775.082, for the primary offense and any additional offenses before the court for sentencing. The sentencing court may impose such sentences concurrently or consecutively.

rows.trigger: MANDATORY FLOOR on any state prison sentence: it must EXCEED 1 year, unconditionally, regardless of point score and regardless of offense degree. AUDIT FINDING ADDRESSED, min deliberately kept null: under this programme's field rules min/max carry TRIGGER thresholds only, the dollar or quantity element of a provision, and are never a penalty term. The 1-year figure here is the penalty floor itself, not a trigger element; typing it into min would be the same class of defect as writing a penalty cap into max. The floor is therefore stated here in words, as a hard rule: every state prison sentence under the code exceeds 1 year.
rows.quote: However, any sentence to state prison must exceed 1 year.

rows.trigger: OVERRIDE PROVISION, sitting mid-paragraph and easy to miss. When the scoresheet's lowest permissible sentence exceeds the s. 775.082 statutory maximum for the offense, the code sentence controls and must be imposed. The degree of the offense does not cap exposure in that situation. Contrast the multiplier-specific caps in the gang and adult-on-minor paragraphs of (1)(b), which resolve the same conflict the opposite way.
rows.quote: If the lowest permissible sentence under the code exceeds the statutory maximum sentence as provided in s. 775.082, the sentence required by the code must be imposed.

rows.trigger: Total sentence points greater than or equal to 363. Authorizes life imprisonment by point score alone, with no degree named and no lower bound tied to the offense's own grading. Second sentence strips discretionary early release for anyone so sentenced, except executive clemency or conditional medical release under s. 947.149. Last substantive rule in subsection (2).
rows.quote: If the total sentence points are greater than or equal to 363, the court may sentence the offender to life imprisonment. An offender sentenced to life imprisonment under this section is not eligible for any form of discretionary early release, except executive clemency or conditional medical release under s. 947.149.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full and recorded for completeness. One digitized scoresheet per defendant, except separate scoresheets when the felonies were committed under more than one version or revision of the guidelines or the code. State attorney prepares; defense counsel reviews for accuracy unless the judge directs otherwise; sentencing judge must approve and sign. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: A single digitized scoresheet shall be prepared for each defendant to determine the permissible range for the sentence that the court may impose, except that if the defendant is before the court for sentencing for more than one felony and the felonies were committed under more than one version or revision of the guidelines or the code, separate digitized scoresheets must be prepared. The scoresheet or scoresheets must cover all the defendant’s offenses pending before the court for sentencing. The state attorney shall prepare the digitized scoresheet or scoresheets, which must be presented to the defense counsel for review for accuracy in all cases unless the judge directs otherwise. The defendant’s scoresheet or scoresheets must be approved and signed by the sentencing judge.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full. Department of Corrections, in consultation with OSCA, state attorneys, and public defenders, submits the revised digitized scoresheet to the Supreme Court by June 15 each year as necessary, and produces approved scoresheets by September 30. Scoresheets must have individual structured data cells per field, plus cells flagging any mandatory minimum imposed and any downward departure. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: The Department of Corrections, in consultation with the Office of the State Courts Administrator, state attorneys, and public defenders, must develop and submit the revised digitized Criminal Punishment Code scoresheet to the Supreme Court for approval by June 15 of each year, as necessary. The digitized scoresheet shall have individual, structured data cells for each data field on the scoresheet. Upon the Supreme Court’s approval of the revised digitized scoresheet, the Department of Corrections shall produce and provide the revised digitized scoresheets by September 30 of each year, as necessary. Digitized scoresheets must include individual data cells to indicate whether any prison sentence imposed includes a mandatory minimum sentence or the sentence imposed was a downward departure from the lowest permissible sentence under the Criminal Punishment Code.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full. DOC must make the digitized scoresheets available to those responsible for preparing them. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: The Department of Corrections shall make available the digitized Criminal Punishment Code scoresheets to those persons charged with the responsibility for preparing scoresheets.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full. Clerk of the circuit court transmits a complete and accurate digitized copy of each sentencing scoresheet to DOC, electronically, no less than monthly by the first of each month, and may send them collectively. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: The clerk of the circuit court shall transmit a complete and accurate digitized copy of the Criminal Punishment Code scoresheet used in each sentencing proceeding to the Department of Corrections. Scoresheets must be electronically transmitted no less frequently than monthly, by the first of each month, and may be sent collectively.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full, and the last operative subsection. A digitized sentencing scoresheet must be prepared for EVERY defendant sentenced for a felony offense, and it plus any attachments prepared under Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.701, 3.702, 3.703, or any other applicable rule, must accompany the uniform judgment and sentence form provided to DOC. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: A digitized sentencing scoresheet must be prepared for every defendant who is sentenced for a felony offense. The individual offender’s digitized Criminal Punishment Code scoresheet and any attachments thereto prepared pursuant to Rule 3.701, Rule 3.702, or Rule 3.703, Florida Rules of Criminal Procedure, or any other rule pertaining to the preparation and submission of felony sentencing scoresheets, must be included with the uniform judgment and sentence form provided to the Department of Corrections.

rows.trigger: History note, recorded rather than merely asserted as read. Not degree-assigning and not operative text. Twenty-four amendments from 1997 to 2025. Currency check: the two most recent are s. 3, ch. 2025-75 and s. 3, ch. 2025-102, which confirms this is the 2025 version and that the section was amended twice in the 2025 session. Anything relying on a pre-2025 copy of this worksheet is stale.

fs-943.0435.title: Sexual offenders required to register with the department; penalty.

rows.trigger: Offender reported intent to vacate a permanent, temporary, or transient residence under paragraph (4)(b), then remained at the residence and failed to report in person within 48 hours after the date he or she indicated he or she would or did vacate. No value or quantity trigger. This paragraph is one of the two 'otherwise specifically provided' carve-outs from the (9)(a) third degree catch-all; the other is subsection (8).
rows.quote: A sexual offender who makes a report as required under paragraph (b) but fails to make a report as required under this paragraph commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Sexual offender maintaining a transient residence fails to report in person to the sheriff's office every 30 days as required by subparagraph (4)(b)2. This paragraph assigns no degree in its own words; it cross-references subsection (9), and the only degree assignment in subsection (9) is (9)(a)'s third degree felony, so the cross-reference resolves determinately: this failure is a third degree felony via (9)(a). No value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: The failure of a sexual offender who maintains a transient residence to report in person to the sheriff's office every 30 days as required in subparagraph (b)2. is punishable as provided in subsection (9).

rows.trigger: Categorical carve-out, not an offense. The entire section, and therefore EVERY degree recorded in this table, does not reach a sexual offender who is also a sexual predator as defined in s. 775.21; a sexual predator registers under s. 775.21 instead, and noncompliance by a predator is prosecuted under that section, not this one. Any consumer of this table must gate on predator status before applying any row. No value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: This section does not apply to a sexual offender who is also a sexual predator, as defined in s. 775.21. A sexual predator must register as required under s. 775.21.

rows.trigger: Failure to provide intended place of residence in another state or jurisdiction, or intended international travel, to the sheriff (in person at least 48 hours before leaving to establish out-of-state residence, at least 21 days before travel outside the United States, or as soon as possible before departure for travel not known within those windows). This subsection assigns no degree in its own words; it cross-references subsection (9), and the only degree assignment in subsection (9) is (9)(a)'s third degree felony, so the cross-reference resolves determinately: this failure is a third degree felony via (9)(a). No value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: The failure of a sexual offender to provide his or her intended place of residence or intended travel is punishable as provided in subsection (9).

rows.trigger: Offender reported intent to establish residence in another state or jurisdiction, or intent to travel to another country, then remained in this state without reporting in person within 48 hours after the date he or she indicated he or she would leave. No value or quantity trigger. This subsection is one of the two 'otherwise specifically provided' carve-outs from the (9)(a) third degree catch-all; the other is paragraph (4)(c).
rows.quote: A sexual offender who reports his or her intent to establish a permanent, temporary, or transient residence in another state, a jurisdiction other than the State of Florida, or intent to travel to another country, but who remains in this state without reporting to the sheriff in the manner required by this subsection commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Catch-all registration violation. Any of: failure to register; failure after registration to maintain, acquire, or renew a driver license or identification card; failure to provide required location or change-of-name information; failure to provide electronic mail addresses or Internet identifiers and each identifier's corresponding website homepage or application software name; failure to provide all home and cellular telephone numbers; failure to report changes to employment information; failure to report changes in status at an institution of higher education; failure to report changes to vehicles owned; failure to make a required report in connection with vacating a permanent residence; failure to reregister as required; failure to respond to address verification correspondence within 3 weeks; knowingly providing false registration information by act or omission; OR otherwise failing, by act or omission, to comply with any requirement of this section. The opening limiter 'Except as otherwise specifically provided' carves out exactly two provisions that provide otherwise: (4)(c) and (8), each a SECOND degree felony, so those two failures are punished one degree higher and are not swallowed by this catch-all. Each instance is a separate offense. NO LOWER BOUND of any kind: no value, quantity, prior-offense, or victim-age threshold. This is also the degree assignment that (4)(d), (7), and the (9)(d) subsequent-charge mechanism resolve to.
rows.quote: Except as otherwise specifically provided, a sexual offender who fails to register; who fails, after registration, to maintain, acquire, or renew a driver license or an identification card; who fails to provide required location information or change-of-name information; who fails to provide electronic mail addresses, Internet identifiers, and each Internet identifier's corresponding website homepage or application software name; who fails to provide all home telephone numbers and cellular telephone numbers; who fails to report any changes to employment information, including the addition of new employment, termination of existing employment, and changes to the occupation, business name, employment address, and telephone number of previously reported employment; who fails to report any changes in status at an institution of higher education; who fails to report any changes to vehicles owned, including the addition of new vehicles and changes to the make, model, color, vehicle identification number (VIN), and license tag numbers of previously reported vehicles; who fails to make a required report in connection with vacating a permanent residence; who fails to reregister as required; who fails to respond to any address verification correspondence from the department or from county or local law enforcement agencies within 3 weeks after the date of the correspondence; who knowingly provides false registration information by act or omission; or who otherwise fails, by act or omission, to comply with the requirements of this section commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084. Each instance of a failure to register or report changes to the required information specified in this paragraph constitutes a separate offense.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum flush/introductory clause. Applies to ANY felony violation of this section, EXCLUDING subsection (13), committed on or after July 1, 2018, and only where the court does not impose a prison sentence. It does not itself set a term; the tiers are in subparagraphs 1.-3. No value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: For a felony violation of this section, excluding subsection (13), committed on or after July 1, 2018, if the court does not impose a prison sentence, the court shall impose a mandatory minimum term of community control, as defined in s. 948.001, as follows:

rows.trigger: First offense on the criminal-history ladder of (9)(b): mandatory minimum term of community control of 6 MONTHS with electronic monitoring, imposed only where the court does not impose a prison sentence for a felony violation of this section (excluding subsection (13)) committed on or after July 1, 2018. min/max are null because the tier condition is an offense ordinal (criminal history, recorded by scope), not a dollar or quantity element, and the 6-month term is a penalty, which is never typed into min/max.
rows.quote: For a first offense, a mandatory minimum term of 6 months with electronic monitoring.

rows.trigger: Second offense on the criminal-history ladder of (9)(b): mandatory minimum term of community control of 1 YEAR with electronic monitoring, imposed only where the court does not impose a prison sentence for a felony violation of this section (excluding subsection (13)) committed on or after July 1, 2018. min/max are null because the tier condition is an offense ordinal (criminal history, recorded by scope), not a dollar or quantity element, and the 1-year term is a penalty, which is never typed into min/max.
rows.quote: For a second offense, a mandatory minimum term of 1 year with electronic monitoring.

rows.trigger: Third or subsequent offense on the criminal-history ladder of (9)(b): mandatory minimum term of community control of 2 YEARS with electronic monitoring, imposed only where the court does not impose a prison sentence for a felony violation of this section (excluding subsection (13)) committed on or after July 1, 2018. 'Or subsequent' is open-ended: the tier has no upper bound. min/max are null because the tier condition is an offense ordinal (criminal history, recorded by scope), not a dollar or quantity element, and the 2-year term is a penalty, which is never typed into min/max.
rows.quote: For a third or subsequent offense, a mandatory minimum term of 2 years with electronic monitoring.

rows.trigger: Venue/prosecutorial-reach provision, not a degree assignment. ANY act or omission in violation of this section may be prosecuted in any of five counties: where the act or omission was committed, the county of the offender's last registered address, the county of the conviction that made the person a sexual offender, the county of release from incarceration, or the county of the intended address reported before release. No value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: A sexual offender who commits any act or omission in violation of this section may be prosecuted for the act or omission in the county in which the act or omission was committed, in the county of the last registered address of the sexual offender, in the county in which the conviction occurred for the offense or offenses that meet the criteria for designating a person as a sexual offender, in the county where the sexual offender was released from incarceration, or in the county of the intended address of the sexual offender as reported by the offender prior to his or her release from incarceration.

rows.trigger: Actual-notice / subsequent-charge / defense-stripping enhancement. A prior arrest on failure-to-register charges (where the offender was provided and advised of the subsection (2) obligations), service of an information or complaint for a violation of this section, or an arraignment on charges under this section constitutes actual notice of the duty to register; failure to immediately register after that event is grounds for a SUBSEQUENT charge of failure to register, which is the (9)(a) offense, a third degree felony (degree resolved via (9)(a)). The offender charged with the subsequent failure may not assert lack of notice, and registering after the arrest, service, or arraignment is not a defense. This is the mechanism that generates the second and third-or-subsequent offense inputs to the (9)(b) ladder. NO LOWER BOUND: applies to any registrant, at any point, on any qualifying arrest, service, or arraignment; no value, quantity, or victim-age threshold.
rows.quote: An arrest on charges of failure to register when the offender has been provided and advised of his or her statutory obligations to register under subsection (2), the service of an information or a complaint for a violation of this section, or an arraignment on charges for a violation of this section constitutes actual notice of the duty to register. A sexual offender's failure to immediately register as required by this section following such arrest, service, or arraignment constitutes grounds for a subsequent charge of failure to register. A sexual offender charged with the crime of failure to register who asserts, or intends to assert, a lack of notice of the duty to register as a defense to a charge of failure to register shall immediately register as required by this section. A sexual offender who is charged with a subsequent failure to register may not assert the defense of a lack of notice of the duty to register. Registration following such arrest, service, or arraignment is not a defense and does not relieve the sexual offender of criminal liability for the failure to register.

rows.trigger: Third-party offense. Any person who has reason to believe a sexual offender is not complying, or has not complied, with this section and who acts with the intent to assist the offender in eluding a law enforcement agency seeking to find the offender to question or arrest him or her for noncompliance, and who commits any one of the four acts in paragraphs (a)-(d). The degree is assigned by the flush language following paragraph (d) and applies to every one of paragraphs (a) through (d). NO LOWER BOUND: no value, quantity, or prior-offense threshold. This subsection is expressly excluded from the (9)(b) mandatory minimum community control provision.
rows.quote: Any person who has reason to believe that a sexual offender is not complying, or has not complied, with the requirements of this section and who, with the intent to assist the sexual offender in eluding a law enforcement agency that is seeking to find the sexual offender to question the sexual offender about, or to arrest the sexual offender for, his or her noncompliance with the requirements of this section: ... commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: First of four alternative acts under subsection (13): withholding information from, or not notifying, law enforcement about the offender's noncompliance and, if known, the offender's whereabouts. Degree supplied by the flush clause after paragraph (d). No value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: Withholds information from, or does not notify, the law enforcement agency about the sexual offender's noncompliance with the requirements of this section, and, if known, the whereabouts of the sexual offender;

rows.trigger: Second of four alternative acts under subsection (13): harboring, attempting to harbor, or assisting another in harboring or attempting to harbor the offender. Degree supplied by the flush clause after paragraph (d). No value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: Harbors, or attempts to harbor, or assists another person in harboring or attempting to harbor, the sexual offender;

rows.trigger: Third of four alternative acts under subsection (13): concealing, attempting to conceal, or assisting another in concealing or attempting to conceal the offender. Degree supplied by the flush clause after paragraph (d). No value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: Conceals or attempts to conceal, or assists another person in concealing or attempting to conceal, the sexual offender; or

rows.trigger: Fourth of four alternative acts under subsection (13): providing information to law enforcement about the offender that the person knows to be false. Degree supplied by the flush clause immediately following paragraph (d); the quote joins the paragraph text to the flush clause, which begins at 'commits' in the source. No value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: Provides information to the law enforcement agency regarding the sexual offender that the person knows to be false information, commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

fs-316-193-2025.title: Driving under the influence; penalties.

rows.trigger: Defines the offense only. Assigns NO degree and NO term of its own; it routes all punishment to subsection (2), which is itself subject to the exceptions in (2)(b), (3), and (4). Reading (1) alone tells a reader nothing about exposure. NOTE: no provision anywhere in 316.193 is graded by a dollar amount, so min/max are null on every row in this table; every dollar figure that appears is a fine (a penalty), never a grading trigger.
rows.quote: A person is guilty of the offense of driving under the influence and is subject to punishment as provided in subsection (2) if the person is driving or in actual physical control of a vehicle within this state and:(a) The person is under the influence of alcoholic beverages, any chemical substance set forth in s. 877.111, or any substance controlled under chapter 893, when affected to the extent that the person’s normal faculties are impaired;(b) The person has a blood-alcohol level of 0.08 or more grams of alcohol per 100 milliliters of blood; or (c) The person has a breath-alcohol level of 0.08 or more grams of alcohol per 210 liters of breath.

rows.trigger: First conviction. Fine range is the penalty, not a grading trigger. The whole of (2)(a) applies only 'Except as provided in paragraph (b), subsection (3), or subsection (4)' -- a reader who stops at (2)(a) will miss the felony provisions entirely. Scope is 'prior' because the tier is selected by conviction count, i.e. by criminal history; every conviction-count tier in this table carries scope 'prior', including first-conviction tiers.
rows.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (b), subsection (3), or subsection (4), any person who is convicted of a violation of subsection (1) shall be punished:1. By a fine of:a. Not less than $500 or more than $1,000 for a first conviction.

rows.trigger: Second conviction, with no time limit stated on how old the prior is. Fine range is the penalty, not a grading trigger.
rows.quote: b. Not less than $1,000 or more than $2,000 for a second conviction; and

rows.trigger: First conviction. The statute prescribes a term directly (not more than 6 months) and names no degree. This row records only what s. 316.193 says. TRIGGER CORRECTED ON REPAIR: an earlier version asserted how s. 775.082 would classify a 6-month maximum while this table lists 775.082 as unread; that assertion is withdrawn, and this table makes no claim about the contents of 775.082.
rows.quote: 2. By imprisonment for:a. Not more than 6 months for a first conviction.

rows.trigger: Second conviction. Term prescribed directly (not more than 9 months), no degree named; this row records only what s. 316.193 says.
