Each of the findings required as the basis for such sentence shall be found to exist by a preponderance of the evidence and shall be appealable to the extent normally applicable to similar findings. 5. For the purpose of identification of a three-time violent felony offender, the court shall fingerprint the defendant pursuant to s. 921.241.

rows.trigger: The three-time violent felony offender analogue of (3)(a)6., and the critical contrast with it: this subparagraph contains NO protection-of-the-public escape clause, and (4)(e) likewise routes only to paragraph (3)(a) and paragraph (3)(c), never to (3)(b). Once the state attorney pursues the sanction and the court finds the (1)(c) criteria met, the (4)(c)1. mandatory minimums must be imposed. Governs the four rows at (4)(c)1.a.-d. Unlike (3)(a)6. and (3)(c)5., this subparagraph is a single sentence; the quote is complete, not truncated. Its effective-date trigger is "on or after the effective date of this act" rather than a stated calendar date.
rows.quote: For an offense committed on or after the effective date of this act, if the state attorney pursues a three-time violent felony offender sanction against the defendant and the court, in a separate proceeding pursuant to this paragraph, determines that the defendant meets the criteria under subsection (1) for imposing such sanction, the court must sentence the defendant as a three-time violent felony offender, subject to imprisonment pursuant to this section as provided in paragraph (4)(c).

rows.trigger: REPAIR: added; previously disclosed in unread with no row, and the chapeau carries a SUBSTANTIVE date limit that appeared in no row: the violent career criminal determination is made only with respect to a primary offense committed on or after October 1, 1995. The procedure at 1.-4. differs from (3)(a) and (3)(b) in two load-bearing ways: there is NO presentence-investigation requirement, and under 3. the findings are appealable ONLY as provided in paragraph (d), a narrower review right than the (3)(a)4. and (3)(b)4. findings, which are appealable to the extent normally applicable.
rows.quote: In a separate proceeding, the court shall determine whether the defendant is a violent career criminal with respect to a primary offense committed on or after October 1, 1995. The procedure shall be as follows: 1. Written notice shall be served on the defendant and the defendant’s attorney a sufficient time prior to the entry of a plea or prior to the imposition of sentence in order to allow the preparation of a submission on behalf of the defendant. 2. All evidence presented shall be presented in open court with full rights of confrontation, cross-examination, and representation by counsel. 3. Each of the findings required as the basis for such sentence shall be found to exist by a preponderance of the evidence and shall be appealable only as provided in paragraph (d). 4. For the purpose of identification, the court shall fingerprint the defendant pursuant to s. 921.241.

rows.trigger: REPAIR (quote defect fixed): the prior quote stopped at "...not necessary for the protection of the public" with no ellipsis, omitting two of the subparagraph's three sentences while the trigger asserted their content. The full subparagraph is now quoted. The violent career criminal analogue of (3)(a)6. Mandatory once the state attorney pursues the sanction and the (1)(d) criteria are found, subject to the same protection-of-the-public escape with written reasons, 7-day transcript option, and monthly reporting to the Office of Economic and Demographic Research. Governs the three rows at (4)(d)1.-3. Works in tandem with (4)(e), which supplies the consequence of the escape finding.
rows.quote: For an offense committed on or after October 1, 1995, if the state attorney pursues a violent career criminal sanction against the defendant and the court, in a separate proceeding pursuant to this paragraph, determines that the defendant meets the criteria under subsection (1) for imposing such sanction, the court must sentence the defendant as a violent career criminal, subject to imprisonment pursuant to this section unless the court finds that such sentence is not necessary for the protection of the public. If the court finds that it is not necessary for the protection of the public to sentence the defendant as a violent career criminal, the court shall provide written reasons; a written transcript of orally stated reasons is permissible, if filed by the court within 7 days after the date of sentencing. Each month, the court shall submit to the Office of Economic and Demographic Research of the Legislature the written reasons or transcripts in each case in which the court determines not to sentence a defendant as a violent career criminal as provided in this subparagraph.

rows.trigger: Post-sentencing review limitation unique to the violent career criminal rows at (4)(d)1.-3. Preserves direct appeal and an any-time illegal-sentence motion by either party, then removes the substance: the trial court's decision to impose OR to decline to impose a violent career criminal sentence is presumed appropriate, and no collateral or postconviction motion may be considered on a claim that the sentence is inappropriate, inadequate, or excessive. The presumption runs both directions, so the state is barred from collaterally attacking a declination under (4)(e) just as the defendant is barred from attacking an imposition. Also note (3)(c)3.: violent career criminal findings are appealable only as provided in paragraph (d), a narrower review right than the (3)(a)4. and (3)(b)4. findings.
rows.quote: A person sentenced under paragraph (4)(d) as a violent career criminal has the right of direct appeal, and either the state or the defendant may petition the trial court to vacate an illegal sentence at any time. However, the determination of the trial court to impose or not to impose a violent career criminal sentence is presumed appropriate and no petition or motion for collateral or other postconviction relief may be considered based on an allegation either by the state or the defendant that such sentence is inappropriate, inadequate, or excessive.

rows.trigger: Second limitation on review of violent career criminal sentences, and a separate rule from (3)(d)1. Imposes a 2-year outside limit measured from finality of judgment and sentence on ALL claims of error or illegality, on direct appeal and collateral review alike, unless the basis could not have been ascertained by due diligence. Separately bars appeal by either party of technical violations and mistakes at trial and sentencing that do not affect due process or fundamental fairness. Framed as legislative intent rather than flat prohibition, which is preserved here rather than resolved.
rows.quote: It is the intent of the Legislature that, with respect to both direct appeal and collateral review of violent career criminal sentences, all claims of error or illegality be raised at the first opportunity and that no claim should be filed more than 2 years after the judgment and sentence became final, unless it is established that the basis for the claim could not have been ascertained at the time by the exercise of due diligence. Technical violations and mistakes at trials and sentencing proceedings involving violent career criminals that do not affect due process or fundamental fairness are not appealable by either the state or the defendant.

rows.trigger: Third and last of the (3)(d) restrictions, a funding bar rather than a procedural one. Directs that no state or political-subdivision funds, resources, or employees be used, directly or indirectly, in appellate or collateral proceedings based on violent career criminal sentencing, except where constitutionally or statutorily mandated. The mandate exception is what preserves appointed appellate counsel in practice.
rows.quote: It is the intent of the Legislature that no funds, resources, or employees of the state or its political subdivisions be used, directly or indirectly, in appellate or collateral proceedings based on violent career criminal sentencing, except when such use is constitutionally or statutorily mandated.

rows.trigger: REPAIR: added; the chapeau carrying the operative verb for the habitual felony offender penalty block previously survived only inside trigger prose. "MAY sentence": the block is permissive on its face, made mandatory only by (3)(a)6. for offenses on or after October 1, 1995 when the state attorney pursues the sanction, and even then subject to the protection-of-the-public escape whose consequence is supplied by (4)(e). Routes through the (3)(a) procedure. Governs the three rows at (4)(a)1.-3.
rows.quote: The court, in conformity with the procedure established in paragraph (3)(a), may sentence the habitual felony offender as follows:

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null): this row's operative discriminator is the degree of the CURRENT offense, not a prior conviction; the priors gate the category via (1)(a), which now has its own scoped row. No permitted scope value describes current-offense degree, so null. Habitual felony offender whose current offense is a life felony or a felony of the first degree. This section assigns NO degree of offense at all; it prescribes a term directly for an already-graded felony. There is no dollar value anywhere in s. 775.084, so min and max are null on every row, not merely unstated. Eligibility requires the (1)(a) findings (see that row), counted per (2) and (5). Permissive per the (4)(a) chapeau ("may"), but mandatory under (3)(a)6. subject to the protection-of-the-public finding at (4)(e). The term is a ceiling, not a floor. Gain-time eligible under (4)(k)1.; conditional release under (4)(j) applies; not subject to the Criminal Punishment Code per (4)(h); may not be increased after imposition per (4)(g).
rows.quote: In the case of a life felony or a felony of the first degree, for life.

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null, same ground as (4)(a)1.). Habitual felony offender whose current offense is a felony of the second degree. Term prescribed directly; the underlying offense keeps its own degree. No value trigger. Same (1)(a) predicate findings, counted per (2) and (5), and the same (3)(a)6. must-impose rule with the (4)(e) protection-of-the-public escape. The 30 years is a CEILING against an ordinary second degree maximum of 15 years; there is no mandatory minimum in this row. Gain-time eligible under (4)(k)1.; (4)(j) conditional release applies; (4)(g) and (4)(h) apply.
rows.quote: In the case of a felony of the second degree, for a term of years not exceeding 30.

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null, same ground as (4)(a)1.). Habitual felony offender whose current offense is a felony of the third degree. Term prescribed directly. No value trigger. The 10 years is a CEILING against an ordinary third degree maximum of 5 years; no mandatory minimum. Same (1)(a) predicate counted per (2) and (5), same (3)(a)6. mandate and (4)(e) escape, same (4)(g), (4)(h), (4)(j), and (4)(k)1. consequences.
rows.quote: In the case of a felony of the third degree, for a term of years not exceeding 10.

rows.trigger: REPAIR: added; the chapeau carrying the operative verb for the habitual violent felony offender penalty block. "MAY sentence", permissive on its face, made mandatory by (3)(a)6. subject to the (4)(e) escape. Note it routes through the procedure of paragraph (3)(a), the same paragraph as habitual felony offenders; there is no separate (3) paragraph for this category. Governs the three rows at (4)(b)1.-3.
rows.quote: The court, in conformity with the procedure established in paragraph (3)(a), may sentence the habitual violent felony offender as follows:

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null; the row's discriminator is the current offense degree, and the (1)(b) predicate now has its own scoped row). Habitual violent felony offender whose current offense is a life felony or a felony of the first degree. Requires the (1)(b) findings: one or more prior convictions, or an attempt or conspiracy, for an offense on the closed list at (1)(b)1.a.-o. (see the (1)(b) row for the full list), plus the (1)(b)2. timing, (1)(b)3. no pardon on the ground of innocence, and (1)(b)4. no conviction set aside. Predicate counting governed by (2) and (5). Mandatory under (3)(a)6. subject to the (4)(e) escape. Adds a 15-year release ineligibility on top of the life term. Gain-time eligible under (4)(k)1., and s. 947.1405 conditional release applies under (4)(j).
rows.quote: In the case of a life felony or a felony of the first degree, for life, and such offender shall not be eligible for release for 15 years.

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null, same ground as (4)(b)1.). Habitual violent felony offender whose current offense is a felony of the second degree. Same (1)(b) enumerated-prior predicate as (4)(b)1., counted per (2) and (5). Dual-bound in substance: a 30-year CEILING plus a 10-year release ineligibility, which functions as a floor on time served though it is not phrased as a mandatory minimum term. Mandatory under (3)(a)6. subject to the (4)(e) escape. Gain-time eligible under (4)(k)1.; (4)(j) applies.
rows.quote: In the case of a felony of the second degree, for a term of years not exceeding 30, and such offender shall not be eligible for release for 10 years.

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null, same ground as (4)(b)1.). Habitual violent felony offender whose current offense is a felony of the third degree. Same (1)(b) enumerated-prior predicate, counted per (2) and (5). A 10-year CEILING plus a 5-year release ineligibility. Mandatory under (3)(a)6. subject to the (4)(e) escape. Gain-time eligible under (4)(k)1.; (4)(j) applies.
rows.quote: In the case of a felony of the third degree, for a term of years not exceeding 10, and such offender shall not be eligible for release for 5 years.

rows.trigger: REPAIR: added; the chapeau carrying the operative verb for the three-time violent felony offender penalty block. "MUST sentence ... to a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment": mandatory in the chapeau itself, the only one of the four blocks whose chapeau says must, and the figures it introduces at a.-d. are FLOORS. Routes through the (3)(b) procedure. No protection-of-the-public escape exists for this block: (3)(b)6. omits it and (4)(e) routes only to (3)(a) and (3)(c). Governs the four rows at (4)(c)1.a.-d.
rows.quote: The court, in conformity with the procedure established in paragraph (3)(b), must sentence the three-time violent felony offender to a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment, as follows:

rows.trigger: REPAIR, twice: scope corrected from "prior" to null (the discriminator is the current offense class; the (1)(c) predicate has its own scoped row), and a FACTUAL ERROR removed: the prior trigger said (4)(k)3. "displaces the general gain-time eligibility of (4)(k)1. for this category," but (4)(k)1. names only habitual felony offenders, habitual violent felony offenders, and violent career criminals; three-time violent felony offenders were never granted gain-time eligibility by it, so there is nothing to displace. (4)(k)3. adds the expiration-of-sentence rule to a category (4)(k)1. never reached. Three-time violent felony offender where the current felony is punishable by life. MANDATORY MINIMUM, not a ceiling, and the court "must" impose it per the (4)(c)1. chapeau. No protection-of-the-public escape: (3)(b)6. omits it and (4)(e) routes only to (3)(a) and (3)(c). Requires the (1)(c) findings (see that row), counted per (2) and (5); the CURRENT felony must itself be enumerated in (1)(c)1.a.-q. Under (4)(k)3., for offenses on or after July 1, 1999, release only by expiration of sentence, with no parole, control release, or any form of early release. The wording "a felony punishable by life" is broader than "life felony" as used in (4)(a), (4)(b), and (4)(d); that ambiguity is preserved here rather than resolved, and it stops short of capital felonies by force of (4)(i). Not capped by the figure stated: see (4)(c)2.
rows.quote: In the case of a felony punishable by life, to a term of imprisonment for life;

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null, same ground as (4)(c)1.a.). Three-time violent felony offender whose current offense is a felony of the first degree. Mandatory minimum of 30 years, a FLOOR and not a maximum; the (4)(c)2. savings clause preserves a greater sentence. Same (1)(c) predicate counted per (2) and (5), and the current offense must itself be an enumerated violent felony under (1)(c)2. No protection-of-the-public escape. Release only by expiration of sentence under (4)(k)3. for offenses on or after July 1, 1999; three-time violent felony offenders are not named in the (4)(k)1. gain-time grant.
rows.quote: In the case of a felony of the first degree, to a term of imprisonment of 30 years;

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null, same ground as (4)(c)1.a.). Three-time violent felony offender whose current offense is a felony of the second degree. Mandatory minimum of 15 years, which equals the ordinary statutory maximum for a second degree felony, so it converts that maximum into a floor. A FLOOR, not a ceiling; (4)(c)2. preserves a greater sentence as authorized by law. Same (1)(c) predicate counted per (2) and (5). No protection-of-the-public escape. (4)(k)3. release restriction applies; no (4)(k)1. gain-time.
rows.quote: In the case of a felony of the second degree, to a term of imprisonment of 15 years; or

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null, same ground as (4)(c)1.a.). Three-time violent felony offender whose current offense is a felony of the third degree. Mandatory minimum of 5 years, which equals the ordinary third degree maximum, so it converts that maximum into a floor. A FLOOR, not a ceiling; (4)(c)2. preserves a greater sentence. Same (1)(c) predicate counted per (2) and (5). No protection-of-the-public escape. (4)(k)3. release restriction applies; no (4)(k)1. gain-time.
rows.quote: In the case of a felony of the third degree, to a term of imprisonment of 5 years.

rows.trigger: Not a penalty assignment but a savings clause on sentencing authority: nothing prevents a court from imposing a greater sentence of incarceration as authorized by law. SCOPE OF THE CLAUSE, presented per the auditor's instruction as an OPEN QUESTION rather than settled: the text says "Nothing in this SUBSECTION," and in Florida statutory hierarchy the subsection is (4) while the paragraph is (c), so the literal reading reaches all of subsection (4), including the (4)(a), (4)(b), and (4)(d) blocks and their stated ceilings (the 30 and 10 of (4)(a), the 30 and 10 of (4)(b), the 40 and 15 of (4)(d)). But the clause is PLACED as subparagraph 2. under paragraph (c), and placement supports a narrower paragraph-only reading confined to the (4)(c)1. floors. The two readings materially diverge on six rows, and this table does not resolve the conflict; a downstream consumer must not treat the subsection-wide reading as settled law. Under either reading the clause permits a greater sentence at the time of imposition only; (4)(g) bars any increase after imposition. Scope field is null: this provision is not keyed to prior convictions or to any listed scope value.
rows.quote: Nothing in this subsection shall prevent a court from imposing a greater sentence of incarceration as authorized by law.

rows.trigger: REPAIR: added; the chapeau carrying the operative verb for the violent career criminal penalty block. "SHALL sentence": mandatory in form, stronger than the "may" of (4)(a) and (4)(b), but still subject to the (3)(c)5. protection-of-the-public escape whose consequence is supplied by (4)(e). Routes through the (3)(c) procedure, which has no presentence-investigation requirement and whose findings are appealable only as provided in (3)(d). Governs the three rows at (4)(d)1.-3.
rows.quote: The court, in conformity with the procedure established in paragraph (3)(c), shall sentence the violent career criminal as follows:

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null; the discriminator is the current offense degree, and the (1)(d) predicate now has its own scoped rows). Violent career criminal whose current offense is a life felony or a felony of the first degree. Mandatory per the (4)(d) chapeau ("shall"), but under (3)(c)5. and (4)(e) the court may decline if it finds in writing that the sentence is not necessary for the protection of the public. Requires the (1)(d) findings (see that row): three or more prior adult convictions from the (1)(d)1.a.-g. list, prior state or federal incarceration, an enumerated primary offense on or after October 1, 1995 with the timing predicates, no pardon, no conviction set aside, counted per (2) and (5). The predicate list has NO lower bound at its first item: (1)(d)1.a. incorporates the s. 776.08 forcible felony class, whose residual clause reaches any felony involving the use or threat of physical force or violence against any individual at any degree, and (1)(d)1.g. admits bare firearm possession felonies; see those rows. Under (4)(k)2. no discretionary early release other than pardon, executive clemency, or conditional medical release under s. 947.149, though (4)(k)1.gain-time eligibility applies. Review restricted by (3)(c)3. and (3)(d)1.-3. Note (4)(j) does NOT extend s. 947.1405 conditional release to this category; it names only habitual felony offenders and habitual violent felony offenders.
rows.quote: In the case of a life felony or a felony of the first degree, for life.

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null, same ground as (4)(d)1.). Violent career criminal whose current offense is a felony of the second degree. This provision carries BOTH bounds: a 40-year ceiling AND a 30-year mandatory minimum, against an ordinary second degree maximum of 15 years. Because min and max in this schema carry dollar-value semantics and this section states no dollar values, that dual-bound structure lives only in the quote and this trigger; see the unread field, where the schema gap is named. Same (1)(d) three-prior-plus-prior-imprisonment predicate as (4)(d)1., counted per (2) and (5), and reaching the unbounded (1)(d)1.a. forcible felony class. Mandatory under (3)(c)5. subject to the (4)(e) escape. (4)(k)2. release restriction and the (3)(d)1.-3. review restrictions apply.
rows.quote: In the case of a felony of the second degree, for a term of years not exceeding 40, with a mandatory minimum term of 30 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected from "prior" to null, same ground as (4)(d)1.). Violent career criminal whose current offense is a felony of the third degree. Dual-bound: a 15-year ceiling AND a 10-year mandatory minimum, against an ordinary third degree maximum of 5 years. Same (1)(d) predicate counted per (2) and (5), reaching the unbounded (1)(d)1.a. forcible felony class and the (1)(d)1.g. possession item. Mandatory under (3)(c)5. subject to the (4)(e) escape. (4)(k)2. release restriction and the (3)(d)1.-3. review restrictions apply.
rows.quote: In the case of a felony of the third degree, for a term of years not exceeding 15, with a mandatory minimum term of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: The protection-of-the-public override, and the provision that supplies the CONSEQUENCE of the finding described in (3)(a)6. and (3)(c)5.: the sentence is imposed without regard to this section entirely, meaning the defendant is sentenced under the ordinary guidelines and statutory maximums with no enhancement, not merely at a lower enhanced figure. Reaches habitual felony offenders, habitual violent felony offenders, AND violent career criminals, so it governs the nine rows at (4)(a)1.-3., (4)(b)1.-3., and (4)(d)1.-3. It does NOT reach three-time violent felony offenders: it routes only to paragraph (3)(a) and paragraph (3)(c), never (3)(b), which is why the four (4)(c)1. rows have no escape. Limited to offenses committed on or after October 1, 1995.
rows.quote: If the court finds, pursuant to paragraph (3)(a) or paragraph (3)(c), that it is not necessary for the protection of the public to sentence a defendant who meets the criteria for sentencing as a habitual felony offender, a habitual violent felony offender, or a violent career criminal, with respect to an offense committed on or after October 1, 1995, sentence shall be imposed without regard to this section.

rows.trigger: Duty-to-determine provision governing all thirteen penalty rows. Whenever it APPEARS to the court that the defendant is eligible under this section, the court shall make the determination through the separate proceeding at (3)(a), (3)(b), or (3)(c) as applicable. Phrased as a court obligation triggered by apparent eligibility, and it is not conditioned on the state attorney pursuing the sanction, unlike the must-impose rules at (3)(a)6., (3)(b)6., and (3)(c)5., which are. The tension between the two is preserved here rather than resolved.
rows.quote: At any time when it appears to the court that the defendant is eligible for sentencing under this section, the court shall make that determination as provided in paragraph (3)(a), paragraph (3)(b), or paragraph (3)(c).

rows.trigger: One-way ratchet limiting all thirteen penalty rows: a sentence imposed under this section shall not be increased after imposition. Bars upward correction on resentencing or on state appeal. Read against (4)(c)2., which permits a greater sentence at the time of imposition but not after it, and against (3)(d)1., which lets either party move to vacate an ILLEGAL sentence at any time.
rows.quote: A sentence imposed under this section shall not be increased after such imposition.

rows.trigger: This is the provision that actually controls the null "level" field on every row in this table. A sentence imposed under s. 775.084 is not subject to s. 921.002, the Criminal Punishment Code, so the offense-severity-level machinery, the lowest permissible sentence computation, and the departure rules do not apply to these sentences. Any severity level would attach to the underlying felony, not to these provisions. Governs all thirteen penalty rows.
rows.quote: A sentence imposed under this section is not subject to s. 921.002.

rows.trigger: REPAIR (scope corrected a second time, from "current" to null: "current" is not a value the scope vocabulary permits; the keying to the current offense is recorded here in the trigger instead). Not a penalty assignment but an offense-class exclusion keyed to the CURRENT offense, not to any prior conviction: none of the s. 775.084 enhancements reach capital felonies, and being sentenced under this section does not preclude imposition of the death penalty for a capital felony. Bounds every penalty row above. Recorded because a table of the subsection (4) penalties alone would wrongly imply the section covers the top of the felony ladder. Note the interaction with (4)(c)1.a., which reaches "a felony punishable by life": that phrase stops short of capital felonies by force of this paragraph.
rows.quote: The provisions of this section do not apply to capital felonies, and a sentence authorized under this section does not preclude the imposition of the death penalty for a capital felony.

rows.trigger: Attaches s. 947.1405 conditional release supervision to persons sentenced as habitual felony offenders and as habitual violent felony offenders, that is, to the six rows at (4)(a)1.-3. and (4)(b)1.-3. It does NOT name three-time violent felony offenders or violent career criminals, and that omission is load-bearing: it aligns with the (4)(k)2. and (4)(k)3. release restrictions, which foreclose discretionary early release for those two categories. A downstream consumer reading only the (4)(a) and (4)(b) terms would miss that release from those terms carries a post-release supervision tail.
rows.quote: The provisions of s. 947.1405 shall apply to persons sentenced as habitual felony offenders and persons sentenced as habitual violent felony offenders.

rows.trigger: The affirmative release-side grant: a defendant sentenced under this section as a habitual felony offender, a habitual violent felony offender, OR a violent career criminal is ELIGIBLE for gain-time under s. 944.275(4)(b). It reaches those three categories, so it applies to the nine rows at (4)(a)1.-3., (4)(b)1.-3., and (4)(d)1.-3., and it materially changes actual time served on every one of them. For violent career criminals it must be read against (4)(k)2., which forecloses discretionary early release but does not by its terms strip the (4)(k)1. gain-time eligibility; that tension is preserved rather than resolved. Three-time violent felony offenders are the one category NOT named in this subparagraph, consistent with the absolute expiration-of-sentence rule in (4)(k)3.; the (4)(c)1.a. row's earlier contrary claim that (4)(k)3. "displaces" a (4)(k)1. eligibility has been removed, since no such eligibility ever existed for that category.
rows.quote: A defendant sentenced under this section as a habitual felony offender, a habitual violent felony offender, or a violent career criminal is eligible for gain-time granted by the Department of Corrections as provided in s. 944.275(4)(b).

rows.trigger: Release restriction specific to violent career criminals, governing the three rows at (4)(d)1.-3. For offenses committed on or after October 1, 1995, no form of discretionary early release, with three carve-outs: pardon, executive clemency, and conditional medical release granted pursuant to s. 947.149. Narrower than the (4)(k)3. three-time offender rule, which admits no carve-outs at all.
rows.quote: For an offense committed on or after October 1, 1995, a defendant sentenced under this section as a violent career criminal is not eligible for any form of discretionary early release, other than pardon or executive clemency, or conditional medical release granted pursuant to s. 947.149.

rows.trigger: The most absolute release restriction in the section, governing the four rows at (4)(c)1.a.-d. For offenses committed on or after July 1, 1999, a three-time violent felony offender is released ONLY by expiration of sentence: no parole, no control release, no form of early release, and no pardon or clemency carve-out of the kind (4)(k)2. gives violent career criminals. Consistent with the omission of three-time violent felony offenders from the (4)(k)1. gain-time grant and from the (4)(j) conditional release provision; it does not displace a (4)(k)1. eligibility, because (4)(k)1. never named this category.
rows.quote: For an offense committed on or after July 1, 1999, a defendant sentenced under this section as a three-time violent felony offender shall be released only by expiration of sentence and shall not be eligible for parole, control release, or any form of early release.

rows.trigger: The sequential-conviction requirement, a hard predicate limit on all thirteen penalty rows and the most heavily litigated eligibility rule in the section. To be counted as a prior felony under this section the felony must have (a) resulted in a conviction, (b) been sentenced separately PRIOR to the current offense, and (c) been sentenced separately from any other felony conviction being counted as a prior. Its practical effect is that multiple felonies disposed of at a single sentencing hearing collapse into one countable prior, and priors sentenced after the commission of the current offense do not count at all. It governs the (1)(a) two-or-more count, the (1)(b) one-or-more count, the (1)(c) two-or-more count, and the (1)(d) three-or-more count alike. Cuts against (2), which expands the prior-conviction pool to withheld adjudications; (5) then subtracts from that pool by requiring separate sequential sentencing.
rows.quote: In order to be counted as a prior felony for purposes of sentencing under this section, the felony must have resulted in a conviction sentenced separately prior to the current offense and sentenced separately from any other felony conviction that is to be counted as a prior felony.

rows.trigger: Purpose and construction clause, and it is operative rather than hortatory: it declares that a reference to this section constitutes a GENERAL reference under the doctrine of incorporation by reference, which means statutes elsewhere that cross-reference s. 775.084 pick up its later amendments automatically rather than freezing the text as of the referencing statute's enactment. Recorded because a table of the penalty rows alone gives a downstream consumer no signal that this section's amendments propagate outward through every statute that cites it.
rows.quote: The purpose of this section is to provide uniform punishment for those crimes made punishable under this section, and to this end, a reference to this section constitutes a general reference under the doctrine of incorporation by reference.

unread: READING METHOD, stated so the coverage claim can be checked: raw HTML fetched by curl from https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/775.084 for this repair, stripped to text locally, and read line by line start to finish. Every subsection, paragraph, subparagraph, and sub-subparagraph of the section was read: (1)(a)1.-5. including 2.a.-b., (1)(b)1.a.-o. and 2.a.-b., 3., 4., (1)(c)1.a.-r. and 2.a.-b., 3., 4., (1)(d)1.a.-g. and 2., 3.a.-b., 4., 5., (1)(e), (2), (3)(a) chapeau and 1.-6., (3)(b) chapeau and 1.-6., (3)(c) chapeau and 1.-5., (3)(d)1.-3., (4)(a)-(4)(k)3. including all four block chapeaux, (5), (6), and the History note. Every quote in this table was checked verbatim against that fetched text.

s. 776.08 (forcible felony), incorporated at (1)(d)1.a. -- OPENED AND READ IN FULL for this repair, correcting the prior table's failure to open it. Its full text, including the residual clause reaching any other felony which involves the use or threat of physical force or violence against any individual, is captured at the (1)(d)1.a. row. This resolves the auditor's headline no-lower-bound finding.

STRUCTURAL CHOICES, named so read-but-unrecorded is distinguishable from unread: the (1)(a)-(1)(d) category definitions now each have their own row with the operative text quoted in full, including the complete (1)(c)1.a.-r. list that the prior table never recited; the prior justification for omitting them as rows was found dishonest by the audit and is withdrawn. (1)(d)1.a. and (1)(d)1.g. additionally have dedicated rows because each supplies an unbounded or degree-floorless predicate class that a consumer of the (4)(d) rows must see. The (3)(a), (3)(b), and (3)(c) procedural paragraphs now have rows quoting their chapeaux and procedural subparagraphs, including the substantive October 1, 1995 date limit in the (3)(c) chapeau. The (4)(a), (4)(b), (4)(c)1., and (4)(d) chapeaux now have rows carrying the may/must/shall verbs.

SCHEMA GAP, flagged so it is known rather than silent: min and max are null on all 46 rows of this table. Those fields carry trigger-threshold semantics (dollar or quantity elements) and s. 775.084 states no dollar or quantity trigger anywhere; the year figures in subsection (4) are penalty terms, never trigger thresholds, and the field rules forbid recording penalty bounds there. The cost is that the YEAR bounds are legible only in the quote and trigger text: the dual-bound structure of (4)(d)2. (40-year ceiling WITH a 30-year floor) and (4)(d)3. (15-year ceiling WITH a 10-year floor), the floor-not-ceiling character of all four (4)(c)1. rows, the ceiling-only character of the (4)(a) rows, and the ceiling-plus-release-ineligibility structure of the (4)(b) rows are invisible to a structured consumer that reads only min and max. Any consumer computing exposure from this table must parse the quote.

SCOPE VOCABULARY GAP: thirteen penalty rows discriminate on the degree of the CURRENT offense, and (4)(i) is keyed to the current offense class, but the scope vocabulary (dwelling, item, prior, victim, place) has no value for current-offense keying, so those rows carry scope null with the keying stated in trigger text. The prior table's scope 'prior' on the penalty rows and invented value 'current' on (4)(i) are both corrected.

OPEN QUESTION carried in the (4)(c)2. row per the audit: whether 'Nothing in this subsection' reaches all of subsection (4) or only paragraph (c). The literal hierarchy reading and the placement-based reading materially diverge on six rows, and this table records both without resolving them.

s. 921.0022 offense severity ranking chart -- NOT opened. Every level is null rather than guessed, and this is independently justified by operative text: (4)(h) provides that a sentence imposed under this section is not subject to s. 921.002, so the severity-level machinery does not reach these sentences; any level would attach to the underlying felony.

The violent career criminal predicate statutes enumerated at (1)(d)1.b.-g. -- s. 784.048(3) and (4), s. 827.03(2)(a), s. 825.102(2), s. 800.04, s. 847.0135(5), s. 944.40, and chapter 790 -- NOT opened. Unlike s. 776.08 these are bounded named offenses whose identity is stated in 775.084 itself; their internal gradations are not captured here.

s. 893.13 (purchase or possession of a controlled substance), which at (1)(a)3. disqualifies both the current offense and one of the two priors from counting toward habitual felony offender status -- NOT opened. It bounds all three (4)(a) rows.

Cross-referenced procedural, release, and sentencing statutes, all NOT opened: s. 921.241 (fingerprinting, cited at (3)(a)5., (3)(b)5., (3)(c)4.), s. 947.1405 (conditional release, cited at (4)(j)), s. 944.275(4)(b) (gain-time, cited at (4)(k)1.), s. 947.149 (conditional medical release, cited at (4)(k)2.), and s. 921.002 (Criminal Punishment Code, cited at (4)(h)). Each is recorded in this table only to the extent 775.084 itself describes its effect.

The session laws in the History note (s. 5, ch. 71-136 through s. 8, ch. 2019-98) were not pulled, so the calendar date behind the (3)(b)6. phrase 'the effective date of this act' (ch. 99-188) is not resolved here. No check was made for amendments enacted after the 2025 compilation; today is 2026-08-14, so the 2026 regular session may have amended this section; the 2025 text was read as the assigned source.

usc-18-924.title: Penalties (federal firearms offenses, Chapter 44)

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Catch-all for the four enumerated acts in (A) false statement in required records or license/exemption/relief application; (B) knowing violation of 922(a)(4),(f),(k),(q); (C) knowing import in violation of 922(l); (D) willful violation of any other provision of the chapter. Federal statute assigns no Florida-style degree.
rows.quote: (a)(1) Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, subsection (b), (c), (f), or (p) of this section, or in section 929, whoever- (A) knowingly makes any false statement or representation with respect to the information required by this chapter to be kept in the records of a person licensed under this chapter or in applying for any license or exemption or relief from disability under the provisions of this chapter; (B) knowingly violates subsection (a)(4), (f), (k), or (q) of section 922; (C) knowingly imports or brings into the United States or any possession thereof any firearm or ammunition in violation of section 922(l); or (D) willfully violates any other provision of this chapter, shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than five years, or both.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Knowing violation of 922(a)(6) (false statement to licensee), 922(h), (i), (j), or (o) (machinegun possession/transfer).
rows.quote: (2) Whoever knowingly violates subsection (a)(6), (h), (i), (j), or (o) of section 922 shall be fined as provided in this title, imprisoned not more than 10 years, or both.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Offender status trigger: only a licensed dealer, importer, manufacturer, or collector; conduct is (A) false statement in required records or (B) violation of 922(m).
rows.quote: (3) Any licensed dealer, licensed importer, licensed manufacturer, or licensed collector who knowingly- (A) makes any false statement or representation with respect to the information required by the provisions of this chapter to be kept in the records of a person licensed under this chapter, or (B) violates subsection (m) of section 922, shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than one year, or both.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Violation of 922(q), the school-zone firearm provision (place-based). Sentence must run consecutively; offense is deemed a misdemeanor for all other purposes despite the 5-year maximum.
rows.quote: (4) Whoever violates section 922(q) shall be fined under this title, imprisoned for not more than 5 years, or both. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the term of imprisonment imposed under this paragraph shall not run concurrently with any other term of imprisonment imposed under any other provision of law. Except for the authorization of a term of imprisonment of not more than 5 years made in this paragraph, for the purpose of any other law a violation of section 922(q) shall be deemed to be a misdemeanor.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Knowing violation of 922(s) or (t) (background check requirements).
rows.quote: (5) Whoever knowingly violates subsection (s) or (t) of section 922 shall be fined under this title, imprisoned for not more than 1 year, or both.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Offender is a juvenile violating 922(x). Mandatory probation-only, no incarceration, if the juvenile is described in clause (ii), unless the juvenile fails a probation condition.
rows.quote: (6)(A)(i) A juvenile who violates section 922(x) shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than 1 year, or both, except that a juvenile described in clause (ii) shall be sentenced to probation on appropriate conditions and shall not be incarcerated unless the juvenile fails to comply with a condition of probation.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Defines the juvenile who gets probation-only under clause (i): BOTH conditions required -- (I) the charge is possession of a handgun or ammunition under 922(x)(2), AND (II) the juvenile has no prior qualifying conviction or delinquency adjudication. Scope left null deliberately: the provision is a combined charge-type and criminal-history definition, not a pure prior-record enhancement.
rows.quote: (ii) A juvenile is described in this clause if- (I) the offense of which the juvenile is charged is possession of a handgun or ammunition in violation of section 922(x)(2); and (II) the juvenile has not been convicted in any court of an offense (including an offense under section 922(x) or a similar State law, but not including any other offense consisting of conduct that if engaged in by an adult would not constitute an offense) or adjudicated as a juvenile delinquent for conduct that if engaged in by an adult would constitute an offense.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Offender is a person other than a juvenile who knowingly violates 922(x).
rows.quote: (B) A person other than a juvenile who knowingly violates section 922(x)- (i) shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than 1 year, or both

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. ENHANCEMENT from 1 year to 10 years: the person sold, delivered, or transferred a handgun or ammunition to a juvenile knowing or having reasonable cause to know the juvenile intended to use it in a crime of violence.
rows.quote: (ii) if the person sold, delivered, or otherwise transferred a handgun or ammunition to a juvenile knowing or having reasonable cause to know that the juvenile intended to carry or otherwise possess or discharge or otherwise use the handgun or ammunition in the commission of a crime of violence, shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than 10 years, or both.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Knowing violation of section 931 (body armor possession by violent felons).
rows.quote: (7) Whoever knowingly violates section 931 shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than 3 years, or both.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Knowing violation of 922(d) (transfer to prohibited person) or 922(g) (prohibited person in possession).
rows.quote: (8) Whoever knowingly violates subsection (d) or (g) of section 922 shall be fined under this title, imprisoned for not more than 15 years, or both.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Shipping, transporting, or receiving a firearm or ammunition in interstate or foreign commerce with intent that, or knowledge or reasonable cause to believe that, an offense punishable by more than one year will be committed with it.
rows.quote: (b) Whoever, with intent to commit therewith an offense punishable by imprisonment for a term exceeding one year, or with knowledge or reasonable cause to believe that an offense punishable by imprisonment for a term exceeding one year is to be committed therewith, ships, transports, or receives a firearm or any ammunition in interstate or foreign commerce shall be fined under this title, or imprisoned not more than ten years, or both.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. MANDATORY MINIMUM 5 years, consecutive to and in addition to the underlying crime: using or carrying a firearm during and in relation to any federal crime of violence or drug trafficking crime, or possessing a firearm in furtherance of such a crime. Baseline tier -- applies unless a greater minimum applies.
rows.quote: (c)(1)(A) Except to the extent that a greater minimum sentence is otherwise provided by this subsection or by any other provision of law, any person who, during and in relation to any crime of violence or drug trafficking crime (including a crime of violence or drug trafficking crime that provides for an enhanced punishment if committed by the use of a deadly or dangerous weapon or device) for which the person may be prosecuted in a court of the United States, uses or carries a firearm, or who, in furtherance of any such crime, possesses a firearm, shall, in addition to the punishment provided for such crime of violence or drug trafficking crime- (i) be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than 5 years;

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. MANDATORY MINIMUM 7 years: the firearm is brandished (defined in (c)(4)).
rows.quote: (ii) if the firearm is brandished, be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than 7 years; and

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. MANDATORY MINIMUM 10 years: the firearm is discharged.
rows.quote: (iii) if the firearm is discharged, be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than 10 years.

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. MANDATORY MINIMUM 10 years based on the type of firearm possessed: short-barreled rifle, short-barreled shotgun, or semiautomatic assault weapon.
rows.quote: (B) If the firearm possessed by a person convicted of a violation of this subsection- (i) is a short-barreled rifle, short-barreled shotgun, or semiautomatic assault weapon, the person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than 10 years; or

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. MANDATORY MINIMUM 30 years based on the type of firearm possessed: machinegun, destructive device, or firearm equipped with a silencer or muffler.
rows.quote: (ii) is a machinegun or a destructive device, or is equipped with a firearm silencer or firearm muffler, the person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than 30 years.

rows.trigger: MANDATORY MINIMUM 25 years. Criminal-history trigger: the violation occurs after a prior conviction under subsection (c) has become final. One or more priors; NO UPPER BOUND on number of priors.
rows.quote: (C) In the case of a violation of this subsection that occurs after a prior conviction under this subsection has become final, the person shall- (i) be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than 25 years; and

A fentanyl derivative, as described in s. 893.03(1)(a)63.; f. A controlled substance analog, as described in s. 893.0356, of any substance described in sub-subparagraphs a.-e.; or g. The substance or mixture listed in subparagraph 1. is in a form that resembles, or is mixed, granulated, absorbed, spray-dried, or aerosolized as or onto, coated on, in whole or in part, or solubilized with or into, a product, when such product or its packaging further has at least one of the following attributes: a. Resembles the trade dress of a branded food product, consumer food product, or logo food product; b. Incorporates an actual or fake registered copyright, service mark, or trademark; c. rows.trigger: Purchase, or possession with intent to purchase, a substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(a), (1)(b), (1)(d), (2)(a), (2)(b), or (2)(c)5. NO quantity threshold.
rows.quote: A controlled substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(a), (1)(b), (1)(d), (2)(a), (2)(b), or (2)(c)5. commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Purchase or possession with intent to purchase a substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(c), (2)(c)1., (2)(c)2., (2)(c)3., (2)(c)6.-(2)(c)10., (3), or (4). NO quantity threshold.
rows.quote: A controlled substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(c), (2)(c)1., (2)(c)2., (2)(c)3., (2)(c)6., (2)(c)7., (2)(c)8., (2)(c)9., (2)(c)10., (3), or (4) commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Purchase or possession with intent to purchase a Schedule V substance named or described in s. 893.03(5). NO quantity threshold.
rows.quote: A controlled substance named or described in s. 893.03(5) commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: UNITS: GRAMS. Purchase of 'more than 10 grams' of a s. 893.03(1)(a) or (1)(b) substance, any combination thereof, or any mixture containing any such substance. The statutory lower bound is strictly EXCLUSIVE at 10: exactly 10.0 grams is NOT covered. Typed min 11 (inclusive) encodes that exclusion at the statute's whole-gram granularity; fractional weights above 10 and below 11 grams ARE covered by the operative words even though they fall below the typed min, so apply the statutory words 'more than 10 grams' at fractional weights. No upper bound stated in this paragraph.
rows.quote: Except as provided in this chapter, a person may not purchase more than 10 grams of any substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(a) or (1)(b), or any combination thereof, or any mixture containing any such substance. A person who violates this paragraph commits a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: UNITS: GRAMS. Delivery of cannabis WITHOUT consideration. NO lower bound. The statutory upper bound is INCLUSIVE at 20 ('20 grams or less'): exactly 20.0 grams IS covered. Typed max 21 (exclusive) encodes that inclusion at the statute's whole-gram granularity; fractional weights above 20 and below 21 grams are NOT covered by the operative words even though they fall inside the typed range, so apply the statutory words '20 grams or less' at fractional weights (delivery of more than 20 grams falls under (1)(a) instead). 'Cannabis' here excludes the resin extracted from plants of the genus Cannabis and any compound manufacture, salt, derivative, mixture, or preparation of such resin.
rows.quote: A person who delivers, without consideration, 20 grams or less of cannabis, as defined in this chapter, commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: Person 18 or older delivers a controlled substance to a person younger than 18, uses or hires a person younger than 18 as an agent or employee in the sale or delivery of such substance, or uses such person to assist in avoiding detection or apprehension, as to a s. 893.03(1)(a), (1)(b), (1)(d), (2)(a), (2)(b), or (2)(c)5. substance. NO quantity threshold.
rows.quote: A controlled substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(a), (1)(b), (1)(d), (2)(a), (2)(b), or (2)(c)5. commits a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Same conduct involving a person younger than 18, as to a s. 893.03(1)(c), (2)(c)1., (2)(c)2., (2)(c)3., (2)(c)6.-(2)(c)10., (3), or (4) substance. NO quantity threshold.
rows.quote: A controlled substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(c), (2)(c)1., (2)(c)2., (2)(c)3., (2)(c)6., (2)(c)7., (2)(c)8., (2)(c)9., (2)(c)10., (3), or (4) commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: CATCH-ALL: 'any other controlled substance' in the same conduct involving a person younger than 18. NO substance limit and NO quantity threshold. Unlike the parallel catch-alls in (1)(c)-(f) and (1)(h), this one DOES assign a felony degree.
rows.quote: Any other controlled substance, except as lawfully sold, manufactured, or delivered, commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Applies to every conviction under subsection (4), i.e. all of paragraphs (a), (b), and (c). Bars suspension or deferral of sentence and bars probation. NO quantity or substance threshold.
rows.quote: Imposition of sentence may not be suspended or deferred, and the person so convicted may not be placed on probation.

rows.trigger: Bringing into this state a substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(a), (1)(b), (1)(d), (2)(a), (2)(b), or (2)(c)5., unless possession is authorized by the chapter or the person is federally licensed. NO quantity threshold.
rows.quote: A controlled substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(a), (1)(b), (1)(d), (2)(a), (2)(b), or (2)(c)5. commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Bringing into this state a substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(c), (2)(c)1., (2)(c)2., (2)(c)3., (2)(c)6.-(2)(c)10., (3), or (4). NO quantity threshold.
rows.quote: A controlled substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(c), (2)(c)1., (2)(c)2., (2)(c)3., (2)(c)6., (2)(c)7., (2)(c)8., (2)(c)9., (2)(c)10., (3), or (4) commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Bringing into this state a Schedule V substance named or described in s. 893.03(5). NO quantity threshold.
rows.quote: A controlled substance named or described in s. 893.03(5) commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: Actual or constructive possession of ANY controlled substance not lawfully obtained from a practitioner or pursuant to a valid prescription or order. NO lower bound of any kind: no quantity threshold and no schedule limitation. This is the residual possession offense. Paragraph (b) reclassifies possession of 20 grams or less of cannabis DOWN to a first degree misdemeanor and paragraph (d) reclassifies Schedule V possession DOWN to a second degree misdemeanor; paragraph (c) is NOT a carve-out or exception from (6)(a) -- it is an independent first degree felony prohibition that AGGRAVATES possession of more than 10 grams of the s. 893.03(1)(a), (1)(b), or (2)(b) substances.
rows.quote: A person may not be in actual or constructive possession of a controlled substance unless such controlled substance was lawfully obtained from a practitioner or pursuant to a valid prescription or order of a practitioner while acting in the course of his or her professional practice or to be in actual or constructive possession of a controlled substance except as otherwise authorized by this chapter. A person who violates this provision commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: UNITS: GRAMS. Possession of cannabis. NO lower bound. The statutory upper bound is INCLUSIVE at 20 ('20 grams or less'): exactly 20.0 grams IS covered as the misdemeanor, the single most consequential boundary point in the subsection. Typed max 21 (exclusive) encodes that inclusion at the statute's whole-gram granularity; fractional weights above 20 and below 21 grams are NOT covered by the operative words even though they fall inside the typed range, so apply the statutory words '20 grams or less' at fractional weights (possession above 20 grams is the (6)(a) third degree felony). 'Cannabis' here excludes the resin extracted from plants of the genus Cannabis and any compound manufacture, salt, derivative, mixture, or preparation of such resin.
rows.quote: If the offense is the possession of 20 grams or less of cannabis, as defined in this chapter, the person commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: UNITS: GRAMS. Possession of 'more than 10 grams' of a substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(a), (1)(b), or (2)(b), any combination thereof, or any mixture containing any such substance. The statutory lower bound is strictly EXCLUSIVE at 10: exactly 10.0 grams is NOT covered. Typed min 11 (inclusive) encodes that exclusion at the statute's whole-gram granularity; fractional weights above 10 and below 11 grams ARE covered by the operative words even though they fall below the typed min, so apply the statutory words 'more than 10 grams' at fractional weights. No upper bound stated. Note the schedule list here differs from (1)(b) and (2)(b): it includes s. 893.03(2)(b).
rows.quote: Except as provided in this chapter, a person may not possess more than 10 grams of any substance named or described in s. 893.03(1)(a), (1)(b), or (2)(b), or any combination thereof, or any mixture containing any such substance. rows.quote: except that, upon a second or subsequent violation, the person commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

(doctor shopping: obtaining or attempting to obtain from a practitioner, with intent to obtain a medically unnecessary controlled substance or amount, by misrepresentation, fraud, forgery, deception, subterfuge, or concealment of a material fact) OR of paragraph (7)(b) (health care practitioner providing a medically unnecessary controlled substance or prescription by the same means). Degree applies only if any controlled substance that is the subject of the offense is listed in Schedule II, III, or IV. NO quantity or value threshold.

rows.trigger: Prescribing practitioner violates paragraph (8)(a): knowingly assisting a patient, other person, or animal owner to obtain a controlled substance through deceptive, untrue, or fraudulent representations; employing a trick or scheme to do so; knowingly writing a prescription for a fictitious person; or writing a prescription whose sole purpose is to provide or obtain a monetary benefit for the prescribing practitioner. NO dollar or quantity threshold.
rows.quote: A person who violates paragraph (a) commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: UNITS: DOLLARS, not grams (the only dollar-denominated min/max in this table; every other populated min/max is grams). First prong of a DISJUNCTIVE reclassification of the (8)(c) offense: the prescribing practitioner violated paragraph (8)(a) AND received $1,000 or more in payment for writing one or more prescriptions. Min 1000 is inclusive ('$1,000 or more'); the statute states no upper bound. This prong alone does NOT exhaust (8)(d): the companion row for the s. 893.135 trafficking-quantity prong reclassifies with NO dollar bound at all, so a consumer filtering on this row's min loses that prong. Level 4 is stated expressly in the quoted statutory text ('ranked in level 4 of the Criminal Punishment Code'), not taken from the s. 921.0022 chart.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding paragraph (c), if a prescribing practitioner has violated paragraph (a) and received $1,000 or more in payment for writing one or more prescriptions ... the violation is reclassified as a felony of the second degree and ranked in level 4 of the Criminal Punishment Code.

rows.trigger: Second prong of the DISJUNCTIVE (8)(d) reclassification, with NO dollar bound and NO payment element of any kind: the prescribing practitioner violated paragraph (8)(a) and, in the case of a prescription written for a controlled substance described in s. 893.135, wrote one or more prescriptions for a quantity that, individually or in the aggregate, meets the s. 893.135 trafficking threshold. A practitioner who wrote a trafficking-quantity prescription and was paid $0 commits this reclassified second degree felony. min is null because the operative quantity thresholds live in s. 893.135, vary by substance, and s. 893.135 was not fetched; no single number in this section states them. Scope 'item': the trigger conditions on the identity (a s. 893.135 substance) and quantity of the substance prescribed. Level 4 is stated expressly in the quoted statutory text, not taken from the s. 921.0022 chart.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding paragraph (c), if a prescribing practitioner has violated paragraph (a) and ... in the case of a prescription written for a controlled substance described in s. 893.135, has written one or more prescriptions for a quantity of a controlled substance which, individually or in the aggregate, meets the threshold for the offense of trafficking in a controlled substance under s. 893.135, the violation is reclassified as a felony of the second degree and ranked in level 4 of the Criminal Punishment Code.

rows.trigger: Violation of ANY provision of chapter 893 that results in serious injury to a state or local law enforcement officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, paramedic, employee of a public utility or electric utility, animal control officer, volunteer firefighter engaged by state or local government, federal law enforcement officer, or any other local, state, or federal government employee injured during the course and scope of employment. NO quantity or value threshold, and no limitation to any particular substance or subsection.
rows.quote: If a person violates any provision of this chapter and the violation results in a serious injury to a state or local law enforcement officer as defined in s. 943.10, firefighter as defined in s. 633.102, emergency medical technician as defined in s. 401.23, paramedic as defined in s. 401.23, employee of a public utility or an electric utility as defined in s. 366.02, animal control officer as defined in s. 828.27, volunteer firefighter engaged by state or local government, law enforcement officer employed by the Federal Government, or any other local, state, or Federal Government employee injured during the course and scope of his or her employment, the person commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Same class of protected persons as the first sentence of subsection (10), where the injury sustained results in death or great bodily harm. NO quantity or value threshold.
rows.quote: If the injury sustained results in death or great bodily harm, the person commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.
