rows.trigger: Definition. 'Access device' is incorporated into the definition of personal identification information at (1)(f)5., so every offense row below can be committed with a card number, PIN, or other account-access identifier.
rows.quote: “Access device” means any card, plate, code, account number, electronic serial number, mobile identification number, personal identification number, or other telecommunications service, equipment, or instrument identifier, or other means of account access that can be used, alone or in conjunction with another access device, to obtain money, goods, services, or any other thing of value, or that can be used to initiate a transfer of funds, other than a transfer originated solely by paper instrument.

rows.trigger: Definition. Sets the meaning of the 'without authorization' element in (2), (4), (6), and (11).
rows.quote: “Authorization” means empowerment, permission, or competence to act.

rows.trigger: Definition that NARROWS subsection (4). 'Harass' requires intent to cause substantial emotional distress and no legitimate purpose, and expressly excludes accepted commercial purposes and constitutionally protected conduct such as organized protests. This exclusion is what keeps the (4) misdemeanor off protected speech.
rows.quote: “Harass” means to engage in conduct directed at a specific person that is intended to cause substantial emotional distress to such person and serves no legitimate purpose. “Harass” does not mean to use personal identification information for accepted commercial purposes. The term does not include constitutionally protected conduct such as organized protests or the use of personal identification information for accepted commercial purposes.

rows.trigger: Definition. 'Individual' is a single human being and expressly excludes firms, associations, corporations, partnerships, joint ventures, sole proprietorships, and any other entity. This confines (6), (7), and (11), and the deceased-individual branch of (8), to natural persons. Contrast (1)(e), which makes 'person' far broader.
rows.quote: “Individual” means a single human being and does not mean a firm, association of individuals, corporation, partnership, joint venture, sole proprietorship, or any other entity.

rows.trigger: THE DEFINITION THAT SETS THE REACH OF SUBSECTION (2). 'Person' takes the s. 1.01(3) definition, which I fetched and read this pass: 'The word person includes individuals, children, firms, associations, joint adventures, partnerships, estates, trusts, business trusts, syndicates, fiduciaries, corporations, and all other groups or combinations.' Consequences recorded in the affected rows: existing corporations and partnerships are victims under (2)(a), (2)(b), (2)(c), (4), and (9), and entities COUNT toward the 10, 20, and 30 person thresholds in (2)(b) and (2)(c). Subsection (8) is the only route to DECEASED individuals and DISSOLVED entities, not to entity victims generally.
rows.quote: “Person” means a “person” as defined in s. 1.01(3).

rows.trigger: Definition of the object element of every offense in the section. Six illustrative categories, including biometric data, medical records, access devices, and any other number or information usable to access a person's financial resources.
rows.quote: “Personal identification information” means any name or number that may be used, alone or in conjunction with any other information, to identify a specific person, including any: 1. Name, postal or electronic mail address, telephone number, social security number, date of birth, mother’s maiden name, official state-issued or United States-issued driver license or identification number, alien registration number, government passport number, employer or taxpayer identification number, Medicaid or food assistance account number, bank account number, credit or debit card number, or personal identification number or code assigned to the holder of a debit card by the issuer to permit authorized electronic use of such card; 2. Unique biometric data, such as fingerprint, voice print, retina or iris image, or other unique physical representation; 3. Unique electronic identification number, address, or routing code; 4. Medical records; 5. Telecommunication identifying information or access device; or 6. Other number or information that can be used to access a person’s financial resources.

rows.trigger: Definition that makes subsection (9) chargeable. Counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information is fabricated data in the similitude of (1)(f) that would lead a reasonably prudent person to credit its truthfulness and accuracy.
rows.quote: “Counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information” means any counterfeit, fictitious, or fabricated information in the similitude of the data outlined in paragraph (f) that, although not truthful or accurate, would in context lead a reasonably prudent person to credit its truthfulness and accuracy.

rows.trigger: BASE OFFENSE WITH NO DOLLAR FLOOR AND NO VICTIM-COUNT FLOOR. min is null because value is not an element at all, not because the range starts at zero. Violated by mere POSSESSION WITH INTENT to fraudulently use -- no completed use and no loss of any amount required, so a $0 case is a third degree felony. 'Person' includes existing corporations, partnerships, trusts, and estates per (1)(e) and s. 1.01(3). Level 4 verified this pass in the s. 921.0022 chart entry for 817.568(2)(a).
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, personal identification information concerning another person without first obtaining that person’s consent, commits the offense of fraudulent use of personal identification information, which is a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: DOLLAR prong of paragraph (2)(b), one of two independent prongs. min/max are DOLLARS. Pecuniary benefit, value of services received, payment sought to be avoided, or amount of injury or fraud of $5,000 or more. max is null because the paragraph states NO upper dollar bound; the $50,000 figure in (2)(c) is a floor for a higher paragraph, not a ceiling here, and any ceiling would be fabricated. Requires actual fraudulent USE; possession with intent does not reach this paragraph. Level 5 verified this pass in the s. 921.0022 chart, whose (2)(b) entry describes both prongs.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more persons, but fewer than 20 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: INDEPENDENT COUNT PRONG WITH NO DOLLAR ELEMENT. min/max are a PERSON COUNT, not dollars: 10 or more but fewer than 20 persons. Second degree felony at ANY dollar value including zero, and the 3-year mandatory minimum in the next sentence attaches. A $0 twelve-person case read against a $5,000 floor lands two degrees low and misses three years of mandatory prison. CRITICAL under (1)(e) and s. 1.01(3): 'persons' includes corporations, partnerships, trusts, and estates, so entities count toward this threshold; counting only natural persons undercounts it. Level 5 verified this pass; the chart's (2)(b) description expressly includes the 10-or-more-persons prong.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more persons, but fewer than 20 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: Trailing sentence prescribing a term directly without naming a degree. A 3-year MANDATORY MINIMUM attaches to EVERY (2)(b) conviction, including one resting purely on the 10-to-19-person count prong with no dollar loss, so both bounds are null. Subsection (3) forces it past the Criminal Punishment Code maximum; subsection (13) is the only route to relief.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 3 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: DOLLAR prong of paragraph (2)(c). min/max are DOLLARS: $50,000 or more with NO upper bound stated. Level is null because the s. 921.0022 chart, searched this pass, contains NO entry for (2)(c); its default ranking would come from s. 921.0023, which was not read.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent commits a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more persons, but fewer than 30 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: INDEPENDENT COUNT PRONG WITH NO DOLLAR ELEMENT. min/max are a PERSON COUNT: 20 or more but fewer than 30 persons. First degree felony at ANY dollar value including zero, carrying the 5-year mandatory minimum in the next sentence. A guard that only reaches (2)(c) above $50,000 makes a 25-person, $0 case invisible. 'Persons' includes entities per (1)(e) and s. 1.01(3), so corporations and trusts count toward the threshold.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent commits a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more persons, but fewer than 30 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: Prescribes a term directly without naming a degree. A 5-year mandatory minimum attaches to EVERY (2)(c) conviction, including one resting solely on the 20-to-29-person count prong with no dollar loss, so both bounds are null. Only subsection (13) can reduce or suspend it.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 5 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: A SECOND, HIGHER THRESHOLD BURIED IN THE LAST SENTENCE OF PARAGRAPH (2)(c), numbered by nothing. min/max are DOLLARS: $100,000 or more, NO upper bound, raises the mandatory minimum from 5 to 10 years. The degree remains first degree felony under (2)(c); this sentence names no degree, it prescribes a term, so a reader tracking only degrees records the $50,000 tier and stops. See the companion count-prong row.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more persons without their consent, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: THE 10-YEAR MANDATORY MINIMUM IS ALSO TRIGGERED, WHOLLY INDEPENDENTLY OF MONEY, BY 30 OR MORE PERSONS. min/max are a PERSON COUNT; max is null because no upper count exists. Thirty persons and $0 of proven loss is a first degree felony with a 10-year mandatory minimum. TEXTUAL NOTE, recorded not inferred: the degree-assigning clause of (2)(c) stops at 'fewer than 30 persons', so 30-or-more is expressly named only in this mandatory-minimum sentence, which reaches back to 'the offense described in this paragraph'. Entities count toward the 30 per (1)(e) and s. 1.01(3). Easiest provision in the section to miss: it sits in the third sentence of a paragraph whose first sentence already answered the degree question.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more persons without their consent, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree but governs how the (2)(b) and (2)(c) mandatory minimums interact with the Criminal Punishment Code. THE MANDATORY MINIMUM MUST BE IMPOSED EVEN IF IT EXCEEDS THE MAXIMUM otherwise authorized under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or chapter 921, and the court's power to go higher is preserved. Note it names only (2)(b) and (2)(c); it says nothing about the parallel (8)(b) and (8)(c) mandatory minimums.
rows.quote: Neither paragraph (2)(b) nor paragraph (2)(c) prevents a court from imposing a greater sentence of incarceration as authorized by law. If the minimum mandatory terms of imprisonment imposed under paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c) exceed the maximum sentences authorized under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, the mandatory minimum sentence must be imposed. If the mandatory minimum terms of imprisonment under paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c) are less than the sentence that could be imposed under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, the sentence imposed by the court must include the mandatory minimum term of imprisonment as required by paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c).

rows.trigger: Harassment purpose, not fraud purpose. No dollar amount or count is an element, so both bounds are null. Reaches POSSESSES, USES, OR ATTEMPTS TO USE -- an attempt alone completes the offense. 'Harass' is narrowed by (1)(c), which excludes accepted commercial purposes and constitutionally protected conduct. The only base misdemeanor in the section; punishable under s. 775.082 or s. 775.083 only, with no s. 775.084 reference. Subsections (5)(a) and (10)(a) can each convert it to a third degree felony.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization possesses, uses, or attempts to use personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent, and who does so for the purpose of harassing that person, commits the offense of harassment by use of personal identification information, which is a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION, NOT A STANDALONE OFFENSE. Applies when any offense under this section was facilitated or furthered by use of a public record as defined in s. 119.011 (an instrumentality trigger, so no scope value applies). Converts the (4) first degree misdemeanor into a third degree felony. Level 2 is stated IN THE STATUTE ITSELF, in the flush-left sentence closing subsection (5): a reclassified misdemeanor is ranked in level 2 of the s. 921.0022 chart. Quote is the chapeau and paragraph (a), which are adjacent in the text.
rows.quote: If an offense prohibited under this section was facilitated or furthered by the use of a public record, as defined in s. 119.011, the offense is reclassified to the next higher degree as follows: (a) A misdemeanor of the first degree is reclassified as a felony of the third degree.

rows.trigger: Public-record reclassification. Any third degree felony under this section -- (2)(a), (8)(a), or (9) -- becomes a second degree felony. Level is null because the closing sentence of (5) ranks a reclassified felony one level above its base s. 921.0022 ranking, and the possible base offenses do not share a single ranking.
rows.quote: (b) A felony of the third degree is reclassified as a felony of the second degree.

rows.trigger: Public-record reclassification. Any second degree felony under this section -- (2)(b) on either prong, (6), (7), (8)(b) on either prong, or (11) -- becomes a first degree felony. NOTE THE GAP: subsection (5) stops at (c) and provides NO reclassification for an offense already a first degree felony, unlike subsection (10), which continues to a life felony.
rows.quote: (c) A felony of the second degree is reclassified as a felony of the first degree.

rows.trigger: Sentencing-level rule accompanying the public-record reclassification, governing ALL of (5)(a) through (5)(c). The typed level 2 is supplied by this text itself and applies ONLY to a reclassified MISDEMEANOR; a reclassified FELONY is ranked one level above its base s. 921.0022 ranking, which is not a single number, so do not read this row's level onto felony reclassifications. Expressly reaches incentive gain-time eligibility under chapter 944 as well as sentencing under chapter 921 (the parallel closing sentence of (10) omits chapter 944).
rows.quote: For purposes of sentencing under chapter 921 and incentive gain-time eligibility under chapter 944, a felony offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked one level above the ranking under s. 921.0022 of the felony offense committed, and a misdemeanor offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked in level 2 of the offense severity ranking chart in s. 921.0022.

rows.trigger: VICTIM-STATUS OFFENSE WITH NO DOLLAR ELEMENT. A single fraudulent use of an under-18 individual's personal identification information is a second degree felony regardless of amount; a $1 case carries the same degree as a $5,000 case under (2)(b). 'Individual' is confined to natural persons by (1)(d). Level 8 VERIFIED THIS PASS in the s. 921.0022 chart, whose entry for 817.568(6) reads 'Fraudulent use of personal identification information of an individual under the age of 18' -- the chart description covers ONLY this branch, which is why (6) is split into two rows.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning an individual who is younger than 18 years of age or 60 years of age or older without first obtaining the consent of that individual or of his or her legal guardian commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: SAME OFFENSE SENTENCE, ELDER-VICTIM BRANCH, SPLIT OUT BECAUSE THE RANKING CHART DOES NOT COVER IT. The s. 921.0022 entry for (6) is confined to victims under 18; the 60-or-older branch, added by later amendment, has NO chart entry, so its ranking would fall to the s. 921.0023 default for an unranked second degree felony (not read). Level is null; scoring this branch at level 8 off the chart is unsupported. Degree and all elements are otherwise identical to the under-18 branch. Overlaps subsection (11)'s 60-or-older class.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning an individual who is younger than 18 years of age or 60 years of age or older without first obtaining the consent of that individual or of his or her legal guardian commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: No dollar element. Aggravated by the defendant's custodial relationship to the victim: parent, legal guardian, or anyone otherwise exercising custodial authority. The mens rea omits 'without authorization' and any lack-of-consent element -- only willful and fraudulent use is required. Level 9 VERIFIED THIS PASS in the s. 921.0022 chart, whose entry for 817.568(7) reads 'Fraudulent use of personal identification information of an individual under the age of 18 by his or her parent, legal guardian, or person exercising custodial authority' and lists the offense as '2nd, PBL'. The chart description covers ONLY the under-18 branch.
rows.quote: Any person who is in the relationship of parent or legal guardian, or who otherwise exercises custodial authority over an individual who is younger than 18 years of age or 60 years of age or older, who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information of that individual commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: SAME OFFENSE SENTENCE, ELDER-VICTIM BRANCH, SPLIT OUT BECAUSE THE RANKING CHART DOES NOT COVER IT. The s. 921.0022 entry for (7) is confined to victims under 18; custodial use against an individual 60 or older has NO chart entry, so level is null and its ranking would fall to the s. 921.0023 default (not read). Scoring this branch at level 9 off the chart is unsupported. Degree and elements otherwise identical to the under-18 branch.
rows.quote: Any person who is in the relationship of parent or legal guardian, or who otherwise exercises custodial authority over an individual who is younger than 18 years of age or 60 years of age or older, who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information of that individual commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: NO DOLLAR FLOOR. Parallel base offense for the personal identification information of a DECEASED INDIVIDUAL or a DISSOLVED BUSINESS ENTITY. Reaches possession with intent to fraudulently use, so no completed use and no loss is required; no consent element, since there is no one to consent. CORRECTED SCOPE STATEMENT: (8) is the only route to deceased individuals and DISSOLVED entities; it is NOT the only route to entity victims generally, because 'person' in subsection (2) includes existing corporations, partnerships, trusts, and estates per (1)(e) and s. 1.01(3). Not in the s. 921.0022 chart (verified absent this pass), so level is null.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits the offense of fraudulent use or possession with intent to use personal identification information of a deceased individual or dissolved business entity, a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: DOLLAR prong only. min/max are DOLLARS: $5,000 or more, with max null because the paragraph states no upper bound; the $50,000 figure in (8)(c) is a floor for a higher paragraph, not a ceiling here. Requires actual fraudulent use, not possession. No s. 921.0022 entry exists for (8) (verified absent this pass). See the separate (8)(b) count-prong row.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more but fewer than 20 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: INDEPENDENT COUNT PRONG, NO DOLLAR ELEMENT. min/max are a COUNT of deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, not dollars: 10 or more but fewer than 20. Second degree felony at ANY value including zero, carrying the 3-year mandatory minimum in the next sentence. The deceased-victim twin of the (2)(b) count-prong trap.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more but fewer than 20 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: Trailing sentence prescribing a term without naming a degree: a 3-year MANDATORY MINIMUM on every (8)(b) conviction, including one resting solely on the 10-to-19 count prong with no dollar loss, so both bounds are null. Note that subsection (3), which forces mandatory minimums past the Criminal Punishment Code maximum, names only (2)(b) and (2)(c) and does not mention this one.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 3 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: DOLLAR prong only. min/max are DOLLARS: $50,000 or more with NO upper bound. Named offense: aggravated fraudulent use of the personal identification information of multiple deceased individuals or dissolved business entities. No s. 921.0022 entry (verified absent this pass). See the separate (8)(c) count-prong row.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits the offense of aggravated fraudulent use of the personal identification information of multiple deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more but fewer than 30 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: INDEPENDENT COUNT PRONG, NO DOLLAR ELEMENT. min/max are a COUNT of deceased individuals or dissolved business entities: 20 or more but fewer than 30. First degree felony at any value including zero, carrying the 5-year minimum mandatory in the next sentence.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits the offense of aggravated fraudulent use of the personal identification information of multiple deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more but fewer than 30 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: Prescribes a term without naming a degree: a 5-year minimum mandatory on every (8)(c) conviction, including a zero-dollar count-prong conviction, so both bounds are null. The statute says 'minimum mandatory' here where the parallel (2)(c) says 'mandatory minimum'; the wording differs and is recorded verbatim.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of the offense described in this paragraph to a minimum mandatory sentence of 5 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: SECOND HIDDEN THRESHOLD IN THE LAST SENTENCE OF (8)(c), the deceased-victim twin of the (2)(c) trap. min/max are DOLLARS: $100,000 or more, NO upper bound, raises the mandatory minimum to 10 years. No degree is named; the degree remains first degree felony under (8)(c). Stopping at the $50,000 sentence understates exposure by five years of mandatory time.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of an offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: The 10-year mandatory minimum is ALSO triggered, independently of money, by 30 OR MORE deceased individuals or dissolved business entities. min/max are a COUNT; max is null because no upper count exists. Thirty dissolved-entity identities and $0 of proven loss carries a 10-year mandatory minimum. The degree clause of (8)(c) stops at 'fewer than 30', so 30-or-more appears expressly only in this sentence.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of an offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NO DOLLAR ELEMENT AND NO REAL VICTIM REQUIRED. Reaches counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information concerning a FICTITIOUS PERSON as well as a real person, so synthetic-identity conduct is a third degree felony even though no actual human is harmed. Reaches CREATES or USES or POSSESSES WITH INTENT TO USE. Defined subject matter in (1)(g) by a reasonably-prudent-person standard; requires intent to commit or facilitate a fraud on another person, and 'person' includes entities per (1)(e). No s. 921.0022 entry (verified absent this pass).
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently creates or uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information concerning a fictitious person, or concerning a real person without first obtaining that real person’s consent, with intent to use such counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information for the purpose of committing or facilitating the commission of a fraud on another person, commits the offense of fraudulent creation or use, or possession with intent to fraudulently use, counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information, a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION, NOT A STANDALONE OFFENSE. Triggered when the defendant, for the purpose of obtaining or using personal identification information, misrepresents himself or herself as a law enforcement officer; an employee or representative of a bank, credit card company, credit counseling company, or credit reporting agency; or wrongfully represents that he or she is seeking to help the victim with a credit-history problem. Reaches ANY misdemeanor, not just first degree as in (5)(a). Level 2 is stated in the statute's own closing sentence of (10): a reclassified misdemeanor is ranked in level 2. Quote is the chapeau and paragraph (a), adjacent in the text.
rows.quote: Any person who commits an offense described in this section and for the purpose of obtaining or using personal identification information misrepresents himself or herself to be a law enforcement officer; an employee or representative of a bank, credit card company, credit counseling company, or credit reporting agency; or any person who wrongfully represents that he or she is seeking to assist the victim with a problem with the victim’s credit history shall have the offense reclassified as follows: (a) In the case of a misdemeanor, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the third degree.

rows.trigger: Impersonation reclassification. Any third degree felony under this section becomes a second degree felony. Level null: the closing sentence of (10) ranks it one level above the base offense's s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 ranking, and the possible base offenses do not share one ranking.
rows.quote: (b) In the case of a felony of the third degree, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the second degree.

rows.trigger: Impersonation reclassification. Any second degree felony under this section -- (2)(b) on either prong, (6), (7), (8)(b) on either prong, or (11) -- becomes a first degree felony.
rows.quote: (c) In the case of a felony of the second degree, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the first degree.

rows.trigger: THE HIGHEST DEGREE NAMED ANYWHERE IN THIS SECTION, sitting in the last subparagraph of the subsection, exactly where a reader who found the answer at (a), (b), or (c) stops. A first degree felony under this section, or a first degree felony punishable by life, becomes a LIFE FELONY on the impersonation trigger. A (2)(c) or (8)(c) case in which the defendant posed as a bank representative or a police officer is not a 30-year first degree felony but a life felony, and because the (2)(c) and (8)(c) count prongs carry no dollar element, this exposure is reachable at $0 with 20 or more victims. Subsection (5) has no equivalent rung. Whether an offense can be walked up the (5) ladder and then the (10) ladder in one case is unresolved; see the (5)/(10) interaction row.
rows.quote: (d) In the case of a felony of the first degree or a felony of the first degree punishable by a term of imprisonment not exceeding life, the offense is reclassified as a life felony.

rows.trigger: Sentencing-level rule accompanying the impersonation reclassification, governing ALL of (10)(a) through (10)(d). The typed level 2 is supplied by this text itself and applies ONLY to a reclassified MISDEMEANOR; a reclassified FELONY is ranked one level above its ranking under s. 921.0022 OR s. 921.0023, which is not a single number, so do not read this row's level onto felony reclassifications. Differs from the (5) closing sentence in citing s. 921.0023 as well and in omitting any chapter 944 gain-time reference.
rows.quote: For purposes of sentencing under chapter 921, a felony offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked one level above the ranking under s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 of the felony offense committed, and a misdemeanor offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked in level 2 of the offense severity ranking chart.

rows.trigger: RECORDED AS AMBIGUITY, NOT RESOLVED. Subsections (5) and (10) are both reclassification provisions keyed to DIFFERENT facts -- public-record facilitation versus impersonation -- and NEITHER states that it is exclusive of the other. On a stacking reading, a (2)(a) third degree felony furthered by a public record AND committed while posing as a bank representative reaches a FIRST degree felony (and a stacked first degree felony would then face (10)(d)'s life-felony rung), degrees no single subsection produces from that base. On a non-stacking reading each ladder applies alone. The operative text does not answer the question and no case law was read. Any consumer of the (5) and (10) rows above must know this question is open. Quote joins the chapeau of (5) to the chapeau of (10) with marked elisions; the two passages are not adjacent.
rows.quote: If an offense prohibited under this section was facilitated or furthered by the use of a public record, as defined in s. 119.011, the offense is reclassified to the next higher degree as follows: ... Any person who commits an offense described in this section and for the purpose of obtaining or using personal identification information misrepresents himself or herself to be a law enforcement officer ... shall have the offense reclassified as follows:

rows.trigger: NO DOLLAR ELEMENT WHATSOEVER -- a single unauthorized fraudulent use of one protected individual's information is a second degree felony no matter how small the amount. Seven disjunctive protected classes: an individual 60 or older; a disabled adult as defined in s. 825.101; a public servant as defined in s. 838.014; a veteran as defined in s. 1.01; a first responder as defined in s. 125.01045; an individual employed by the State of Florida; and an individual employed by the Federal Government. 'Individual' confines every class to natural persons per (1)(d). The 60-or-older branch overlaps subsection (6). The four incorporated definitions were not read, so each class's outer boundary is unverified. No s. 921.0022 entry (verified absent this pass).
rows.quote: A person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning an individual who is 60 years of age or older; a disabled adult as defined in s. 825.101; a public servant as defined in s. 838.014; a veteran as defined in s. 1.01; a first responder as defined in s. 125.01045; an individual who is employed by the State of Florida; or an individual who is employed by the Federal Government without first obtaining the consent of that individual commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree but imposes a monetary consequence on EVERY conviction under this section, including a withhold of adjudication and a nolo contendere plea: a mandatory $1,001 surcharge, on top of any fine under s. 775.083 and any restitution. It attaches to every offense row in this table, including the (4) misdemeanor. The $1,001 is a PENALTY and is therefore not typed into min/max, which record trigger thresholds only. Distribution is in (12)(a) through (12)(c); non-waivability is in (12)(d); each has its own row below.
rows.quote: In addition to any sanction imposed when a person pleads guilty or nolo contendere to, or is found guilty of, regardless of adjudication, a violation of this section, the court shall impose a surcharge of $1,001.

rows.trigger: Surcharge distribution: $500 of the $1,001 goes to the Department of Law Enforcement Operating Trust Fund for grants to local law enforcement to investigate criminal-use-of-identity offenses under s. 943.0412 (not read). A distribution rule, not exposure; recorded for paragraph-level completeness.
rows.quote: The sum of $500 of the surcharge shall be deposited into the Department of Law Enforcement Operating Trust Fund for the department to provide grants to local law enforcement agencies to investigate offenses related to the criminal use of personal identification information as provided in s. 943.0412.

rows.trigger: Surcharge distribution: $250 to the State Attorneys Revenue Trust Fund for prosecutions and $250 to the Indigent Criminal Defense Trust Fund. A distribution rule, not exposure.
rows.quote: The sum of $250 of the surcharge shall be deposited into the State Attorneys Revenue Trust Fund for the purpose of funding prosecutions of offenses relating to the criminal use of personal identification information. The sum of $250 of the surcharge shall be deposited into the Indigent Criminal Defense Trust Fund for the purposes of indigent criminal defense related to the criminal use of personal identification information.

rows.trigger: Surcharge distribution: the clerk of court retains $1 of each $1,001 surcharge as a service charge. A distribution rule, not exposure.
rows.quote: The clerk of the court shall retain $1 of each $1,001 surcharge that he or she collects as a service charge of the clerk’s office.

rows.trigger: THE SURCHARGE MAY NOT BE WAIVED BY THE COURT, and where restitution is ordered under s. 775.089 the surcharge is included in a judgment. This is what makes the $1,001 in the (12) chapeau unavoidable on every conviction.
rows.quote: The surcharge may not be waived by the court. In the event that the person has been ordered to pay restitution in accordance with s. 775.089, the surcharge shall be included in a judgment.

rows.trigger: SUBSTANTIAL ASSISTANCE. The ONLY provision in this section capable of defeating the 3-, 5-, and 10-year mandatory minimums in (2)(b), (2)(c), (8)(b), and (8)(c), which subsection (3) otherwise makes unavoidable for (2)(b) and (2)(c). Structural limits: the motion is the PROSECUTOR'S to make, not the defendant's; the judge MAY but need not grant it; the arresting agency gets a hearing in aggravation or mitigation; on good cause the motion may be filed and heard in camera. Applies to every row in this table at any dollar value and any count. Quote is the complete subsection, unspliced.
rows.quote: The prosecutor may move the sentencing court to reduce or suspend the sentence of any person who is convicted of a violation of this section and who provides substantial assistance in the identification, arrest, or conviction of any of that person’s accomplices, accessories, coconspirators, or principals or of any other person engaged in fraudulent possession or use of personal identification information. The arresting agency shall be given an opportunity to be heard in aggravation or mitigation in reference to any such motion. Upon good cause shown, the motion may be filed and heard in camera. The judge hearing the motion may reduce or suspend the sentence if the judge finds that the defendant rendered such substantial assistance.

rows.trigger: COMPLETE EXEMPTION FROM THE ENTIRE SECTION, not a defense to one subsection. Every offense row above must be read subject to it. Lawfully authorized investigative, protective, or intelligence activity of a law enforcement agency of this state, of any other state, or of the Federal Government, or their political subdivisions, is outside the section entirely. The exemption runs to the agency activity and requires that the activity be lawfully authorized.
rows.quote: This section does not prohibit any lawfully authorized investigative, protective, or intelligence activity of a law enforcement agency of this state or any of its political subdivisions, of any other state or its political subdivisions, or of the Federal Government or its political subdivisions.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree but expands monetary exposure beyond the $1,001 surcharge and beyond ordinary out-of-pocket loss: restitution under s. 775.089 may include the victim's ATTORNEY'S FEES for clearing a credit history or credit rating and the costs of civil or administrative proceedings to undo debts, liens, or obligations created by the defendant. Because the restitution measure is not the pecuniary-benefit element that sets the degree, a low-dollar or zero-dollar count-prong conviction can still carry substantial restitution.
rows.quote: In sentencing a defendant convicted of an offense under this section, the court may order that the defendant make restitution under s. 775.089 to any victim of the offense. In addition to the victim’s out-of-pocket costs, restitution may include payment of any other costs, including attorney’s fees incurred by the victim in clearing the victim’s credit history or credit rating, or any costs incurred in connection with any civil or administrative proceeding to satisfy any debt, lien, or other obligation of the victim arising as the result of the actions of the defendant.

rows.trigger: Companion remedial power: the sentencing court may issue orders correcting any public record containing false information given in violation of the section.
rows.quote: The sentencing court may issue such orders as are necessary to correct any public record that contains false information given in violation of this section.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree. Charging authority is not limited to the local state attorney; the statewide prosecutor may bring a multi-circuit case. Relevant in practice to the multi-victim count prongs, which typically span circuits.
rows.quote: Prosecutions for violations of this section may be brought on behalf of the state by any state attorney or by the statewide prosecutor.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree. Legislative finding that fixes, absent contrary evidence, the situs of consent or non-consent at the county where the victim generally resides. Feeds the venue rule in (18).
rows.quote: The Legislature finds that, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, the location where a victim gives or fails to give consent to the use of personal identification information is the county where the victim generally resides.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree. Venue lies in ANY county in which an element occurred, expressly including the county where the victim generally resides.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, venue for the prosecution and trial of violations of this section may be commenced and maintained in any county in which an element of the offense occurred, including the county where the victim generally resides.

rows.trigger: Statute of limitations, a limit on exposure rather than a source of it, and PARTIAL in a way easily misread: the 3-year period with the 1-year-after-discovery extension (capped at 5 years) applies ONLY to prosecutions under subsection (2), subsection (6), or subsection (7). Subsections (4), (8), (9), (10), and (11) are NOT named, so their limitation periods come from the general law, which was not read. Ambiguity noted rather than resolved.
rows.quote: A prosecution of an offense prohibited under subsection (2), subsection (6), or subsection (7) must be commenced within 3 years after the offense occurred. However, a prosecution may be commenced within 1 year after discovery of the offense by an aggrieved party, or by a person who has a legal duty to represent the aggrieved party and who is not a party to the offense, if such prosecution is commenced within 5 years after the violation occurred.
