rows.trigger: Defines the prohibited act; no quantity trigger and NO LOWER BOUND of any kind, any quantity of a controlled substance. Penalty is assigned by subsection (b).
rows.quote: Except as authorized by this subchapter, it shall be unlawful for any person knowingly or intentionally— (1) to manufacture, distribute, or dispense, or possess with intent to manufacture, distribute, or dispense, a controlled substance

rows.trigger: Counterfeit substance. NO LOWER BOUND, any quantity. Penalty assigned by subsection (b).
rows.quote: (2) to create, distribute, or dispense, or possess with intent to distribute or dispense, a counterfeit substance.

rows.trigger: Sentencing ladder applies to any violation of subsection (a), subject to displacement by §§849, 859, 860, 861.
rows.quote: Except as otherwise provided in section 849, 859, 860, or 861 of this title, any person who violates subsection (a) of this section shall be sentenced as follows:

rows.trigger: Heroin. Values in GRAMS (1 kilogram). No upper bound in the text, this is the top tier. Mandatory minimum 10 years, maximum life.
rows.quote: (i) 1 kilogram or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of heroin; ... such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment which may not be less than 10 years or more than life

rows.trigger: Coca leaves, cocaine, ecgonine, and any compound/mixture/preparation containing any quantity of them. Values in GRAMS (5 kilograms). Note subclause (IV) reaches any compound containing ANY quantity of subclauses (I)-(III), so the 5-kilogram figure attaches to the mixture, not the pure drug.
rows.quote: (ii) 5 kilograms or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of— (I) coca leaves, except coca leaves and extracts of coca leaves from which cocaine, ecgonine, and derivatives of ecgonine or their salts have been removed; (II) cocaine, its salts, optical and geometric isomers, and salts of isomers; (III) ecgonine, its derivatives, their salts, isomers, and salts of isomers; or (IV) any compound, mixture, or preparation which contains any quantity of any of the substances referred to in subclauses (I) through (III);

rows.trigger: Cocaine base. Values in GRAMS. Top tier, no upper bound.
rows.quote: (iii) 280 grams or more of a mixture or substance described in clause (ii) which contains cocaine base;

rows.trigger: Phencyclidine (PCP). TWO alternative thresholds in GRAMS: 100 grams of PCP itself, OR 1,000 grams (1 kilogram) of a mixture containing a detectable amount of PCP. min recorded is the lower (pure) figure.
rows.quote: (iv) 100 grams or more of phencyclidine (PCP) or 1 kilogram or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of phencyclidine (PCP);

rows.trigger: Lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD). Values in GRAMS. Top tier, no upper bound.
rows.quote: (v) 10 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD);

rows.trigger: Fentanyl. TWO alternative thresholds in GRAMS: 400 grams of a fentanyl mixture, OR 100 grams of any analogue of fentanyl or a fentanyl-related substance. min recorded is the lower (100 g analogue/fentanyl-related substance) figure.
rows.quote: (vi) 400 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of N-phenyl-N- [ 1- ( 2-phenylethyl ) -4-piperidinyl ] propanamide or 100 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of any analogue of N-phenyl-N-[1-(2-phenylethyl)-4-piperidinyl] propanamide or a fentanyl-related substance;

rows.trigger: Marihuana. Weight threshold recorded in GRAMS (1,000 kilograms). SECOND, INDEPENDENT trigger with no weight element at all: 1,000 or more marihuana plants regardless of weight.
rows.quote: (vii) 1000 kilograms or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of marihuana, or 1,000 or more marihuana plants regardless of weight; or

rows.trigger: Methamphetamine. TWO alternative thresholds in GRAMS: 50 grams of methamphetamine, its salts, isomers, and salts of its isomers, OR 500 grams of a mixture containing a detectable amount. min recorded is the lower (pure) figure.
rows.quote: (viii) 50 grams or more of methamphetamine, its salts, isomers, and salts of its isomers or 500 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of methamphetamine, its salts, isomers, or salts of its isomers;

rows.trigger: Death or serious bodily injury results from use of the substance; raises the mandatory minimum from 10 years to 20 years, maximum life. Quantity trigger is whichever clause (i)-(viii) applies. NOTE: the fine ceiling ($10,000,000 individual / $50,000,000 non-individual) governs the ENTIRE first sentence, including the base 10-year branch, not only the death/SBI branch.
rows.quote: ... such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment which may not be less than 10 years or more than life and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be not less than 20 years or more than life, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $10,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $50,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: One prior final conviction for a serious drug felony or serious violent felony; mandatory minimum rises to 15 years, and to mandatory LIFE if death or serious bodily injury results.
rows.quote: If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a serious drug felony or serious violent felony has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than 15 years and not more than life imprisonment and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to life imprisonment, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $20,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $75,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Two or more prior final convictions for a serious drug felony or serious violent felony; mandatory minimum 25 years. Note this enhancement also attaches to violations of §§849, 859, 860, or 861, not just this subparagraph.
rows.quote: If any person commits a violation of this subparagraph or of section 849, 859, 860, or 861 of this title after 2 or more prior convictions for a serious drug felony or serious violent felony have become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than 25 years and fined in accordance with the preceding sentence.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum supervised release: at least 5 years with no prior conviction, at least 10 years with such a prior conviction.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding section 3583 of title 18, any sentence under this subparagraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 5 years in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 10 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: No probation, no suspended sentence, no parole for anyone sentenced under this subparagraph.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall not place on probation or suspend the sentence of any person sentenced under this subparagraph. No person sentenced under this subparagraph shall be eligible for parole during the term of imprisonment imposed therein.

rows.trigger: Heroin. Values in GRAMS. The text reads "100 grams or more" with NO upper bound; subparagraph (A) does not textually displace (B) at the 1-kilogram (A)(i) floor, and a quantity above it still satisfies this element (a charging observation only, not a statutory ceiling). Mandatory minimum 5 years, maximum 40 years.
rows.quote: (i) 100 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of heroin; ... such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment which may not be less than 5 years and not more than 40 years

rows.trigger: Coca leaves, cocaine, ecgonine, and any compound containing any quantity of them. Values in GRAMS. "Or more" with NO upper bound; the (A)(ii) 5-kilogram figure is a separate tier's floor, not a ceiling on this one.
rows.quote: (ii) 500 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of— (I) coca leaves, except coca leaves and extracts of coca leaves from which cocaine, ecgonine, and derivatives of ecgonine or their salts have been removed; (II) cocaine, its salts, optical and geometric isomers, and salts of isomers; (III) ecgonine, its derivatives, their salts, isomers, and salts of isomers; or (IV) any compound, mixture, or preparation which contains any quantity of any of the substances referred to in subclauses (I) through (III);

rows.trigger: Cocaine base. Values in GRAMS. "Or more" with NO upper bound; the (A)(iii) 280-gram figure is a separate tier's floor, not a ceiling on this one.
rows.quote: (iii) 28 grams or more of a mixture or substance described in clause (ii) which contains cocaine base;

rows.trigger: Phencyclidine (PCP). TWO alternative thresholds in GRAMS: 10 grams of PCP itself, OR 100 grams of a mixture containing a detectable amount of PCP. min recorded on the lower (pure) figure. NO upper bound stated on either alternative; the (A)(iv) figures are a separate tier's floors, not ceilings on this one.
rows.quote: (iv) 10 grams or more of phencyclidine (PCP) or 100 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of phencyclidine (PCP);

rows.trigger: LSD. Values in GRAMS. "Or more" with NO upper bound; the (A)(v) 10-gram figure is a separate tier's floor, not a ceiling on this one.
rows.quote: (v) 1 gram or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD);

rows.trigger: Fentanyl. TWO alternative thresholds in GRAMS: 40 grams of a fentanyl mixture, OR 10 grams of any analogue or a fentanyl-related substance. min recorded on the lower (10 g analogue/fentanyl-related) figure. NO upper bound stated on either alternative; the (A)(vi) figures are a separate tier's floors, not ceilings on this one.
rows.quote: (vi) 40 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of N-phenyl-N- [ 1- ( 2-phenylethyl ) -4-piperidinyl ] propanamide or 10 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of any analogue of N-phenyl-N-[1-(2-phenylethyl)-4-piperidinyl] propanamide or a fentanyl-related substance;

rows.trigger: Marihuana. Weight in GRAMS (100 kilograms). SECOND, INDEPENDENT trigger with no weight element: 100 or more marihuana plants regardless of weight. "Or more" with NO upper bound on either the weight or the plant count; the (A)(vii) figures are a separate tier's floors, not ceilings on this one.
rows.quote: (vii) 100 kilograms or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of marihuana, or 100 or more marihuana plants regardless of weight; or

rows.trigger: Methamphetamine. TWO alternative thresholds in GRAMS: 5 grams pure, OR 50 grams of a mixture. min recorded on the pure figure. NO upper bound stated on either alternative; the (A)(viii) figures are a separate tier's floors, not ceilings on this one.
rows.quote: (viii) 5 grams or more of methamphetamine, its salts, isomers, and salts of its isomers or 50 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of methamphetamine, its salts, isomers, or salts of its isomers;

rows.trigger: Death or serious bodily injury results from use of the substance; mandatory minimum rises from 5 years to 20 years and the maximum rises from 40 years to life. NOTE: the fine ceiling ($5,000,000 individual / $25,000,000 non-individual) governs the ENTIRE first sentence, including the base 5-year branch, not only the death/SBI branch.
rows.quote: ... such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment which may not be less than 5 years and not more than 40 years and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be not less than 20 years or more than life, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $5,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $25,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: One prior final conviction for a serious drug felony or serious violent felony; mandatory minimum 10 years, maximum life, and mandatory LIFE if death or serious bodily injury results.
rows.quote: If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a serious drug felony or serious violent felony has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment which may not be less than 10 years and not more than life imprisonment and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to life imprisonment, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $8,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $50,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum supervised release: at least 4 years with no prior conviction, at least 8 years with such a prior conviction.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding section 3583 of title 18, any sentence imposed under this subparagraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, include a term of supervised release of at least 4 years in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, include a term of supervised release of at least 8 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: No probation, no suspended sentence, no parole for anyone sentenced under this subparagraph.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall not place on probation or suspend the sentence of any person sentenced under this subparagraph. No person sentenced under this subparagraph shall be eligible for parole during the term of imprisonment imposed therein.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Any schedule I or II controlled substance in ANY quantity that is not covered by subparagraphs (A), (B), or (D); also gamma hydroxybutyric acid (including when scheduled as an approved drug product) and 1 gram of flunitrazepam. Maximum 20 years, no mandatory minimum in the base case.
rows.quote: (C) In the case of a controlled substance in schedule I or II, gamma hydroxybutyric acid (including when scheduled as an approved drug product for purposes of section 3(a)(1)(B) of the Hillory J. Farias and Samantha Reid Date-Rape Drug Prohibition Act of 2000), or 1 gram of flunitrazepam, except as provided in subparagraphs (A), (B), and (D), such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 20 years

rows.trigger: Death or serious bodily injury results from use of the substance. This converts a no-minimum, 20-year-max offense into a 20-year MANDATORY MINIMUM with a maximum of life, with NO LOWER BOUND on quantity.
rows.quote: and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than twenty years or more than life, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $1,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $5,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Prior final conviction for a felony drug offense (note: a different and broader predicate than the "serious drug felony or serious violent felony" used in (A) and (B)); maximum rises to 30 years, and to mandatory LIFE if death or serious bodily injury results.
rows.quote: If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a felony drug offense has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 30 years and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to life imprisonment, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $2,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $10,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum supervised release: at least 3 years with no prior conviction, at least 6 years with such a prior conviction.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding section 3583 of title 18, any sentence imposing a term of imprisonment under this paragraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 3 years in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 6 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Probation/suspension and parole are barred only for the death-or-serious-bodily-injury mandatory-minimum branch of this subparagraph, not for the whole subparagraph.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall not place on probation or suspend the sentence of any person sentenced under the provisions of this subparagraph which provide for a mandatory term of imprisonment if death or serious bodily injury results, nor shall a person so sentenced be eligible for parole during the term of such a sentence.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Marihuana under 50 kilograms (max recorded in GRAMS), hashish under 10 kilograms, or hashish oil under one kilogram. Carve-out: does NOT apply where there are 50 or more marihuana plants regardless of weight. Also expressly subject to paragraphs (4) and (5). Maximum 5 years, no mandatory minimum.
rows.quote: (D) In the case of less than 50 kilograms of marihuana, except in the case of 50 or more marihuana plants regardless of weight, 10 kilograms of hashish, or one kilogram of hashish oil, such person shall, except as provided in paragraphs (4) and (5) of this subsection, be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 5 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $250,000 if the defendant is an individual or $1,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Prior final conviction for a felony drug offense; maximum doubles from 5 to 10 years.
rows.quote: If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a felony drug offense has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 10 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $500,000 if the defendant is an individual or $2,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum supervised release: at least 2 years with no prior conviction, at least 4 years with such a prior conviction.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding section 3583 of title 18, any sentence imposing a term of imprisonment under this paragraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 2 years in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 4 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Any schedule III controlled substance in any quantity, except as provided in subparagraphs (C) and (D). Maximum 10 years; 15 years if death or serious bodily injury results (a victim-based enhancement with no quantity trigger).
rows.quote: (E)(i) Except as provided in subparagraphs (C) and (D), in the case of any controlled substance in schedule III, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 10 years and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 15 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $500,000 if the defendant is an individual or $2,500,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Prior final conviction for a felony drug offense; schedule III maximum rises to 20 years, or 30 years if death or serious bodily injury results.
rows.quote: (ii) If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a felony drug offense has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 20 years and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 30 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $1,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $5,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum supervised release: at least 2 years with no prior conviction, at least 4 years with such a prior conviction.
rows.quote: (iii) Any sentence imposing a term of imprisonment under this subparagraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 2 years in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 4 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Any schedule IV controlled substance in any quantity. Maximum 5 years; 10 years after a prior final felony drug offense conviction; mandatory supervised release of at least 1 year (2 years with a prior).
rows.quote: (2) In the case of a controlled substance in schedule IV, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 5 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $250,000 if the defendant is an individual or $1,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both. If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a felony drug offense has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 10 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $500,000 if the defendant is an individual or $2,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both. Any sentence imposing a term of imprisonment under this paragraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least one year in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 2 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Any schedule V controlled substance in any quantity. Maximum one year; 4 years after a prior final felony drug offense conviction. Supervised release here is permissive ("may") and only with a prior, unlike every other tier.
rows.quote: (3) In the case of a controlled substance in schedule V, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than one year, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $100,000 if the defendant is an individual or $250,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both. If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a felony drug offense has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 4 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $200,000 if the defendant is an individual or $500,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both. Any sentence imposing a term of imprisonment under this paragraph may, if there was a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of not more than 1 year, in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Mitigating provision, not an enhancement: distributing a small amount of marihuana for no remuneration. "Small amount" is undefined and has NO numeric bound in either direction. Displaces paragraph (1)(D) and routes the offender to simple-possession treatment under §844 and 18 U.S.C. §3607.
rows.quote: (4) Notwithstanding paragraph (1)(D) of this subsection, any person who violates subsection (a) of this section by distributing a small amount of marihuana for no remuneration shall be treated as provided in section 844 of this title and section 3607 of title 18.

rows.trigger: Cultivating or manufacturing a controlled substance on Federal property. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Imprisonment as otherwise provided in subsection (b); the enhancement is to the fine ceiling, which becomes the greatest of the four listed amounts.
rows.quote: (5) Any person who violates subsection (a) of this section by cultivating or manufacturing a controlled substance on Federal property shall be imprisoned as provided in this subsection and shall be fined any amount not to exceed— (A) the amount authorized in accordance with this section; (B) the amount authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18; (C) $500,000 if the defendant is an individual; or (D) $1,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual; or both.

rows.trigger: Violating subsection (a) OR ATTEMPTING to do so while knowingly or intentionally using a poison, chemical, or other hazardous substance on Federal land, where the use does any ONE of three things: (A) creates a serious hazard to humans, wildlife, or domestic animals, (B) degrades or harms the environment or natural resources, or (C) pollutes an aquifer, spring, stream, river, or body of water. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Separate five-year maximum.
rows.quote: (6) Any person who violates subsection (a), or attempts to do so, and knowingly or intentionally uses a poison, chemical, or other hazardous substance on Federal land, and, by such use— (A) creates a serious hazard to humans, wildlife, or domestic animals, (B) degrades or harms the environment or natural resources, or (C) pollutes an aquifer, spring, stream, river, or body of water, shall be fined in accordance with title 18 or imprisoned not more than five years, or both.

rows.trigger: Distributing a controlled substance or controlled substance analogue to an individual without that individual's knowledge, with intent to commit a crime of violence (as defined in 18 U.S.C. §16, including rape) against that individual. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity and no schedule limitation. Maximum 20 years.
rows.quote: Whoever, with intent to commit a crime of violence, as defined in section 16 of title 18 (including rape), against an individual, violates subsection (a) by distributing a controlled substance or controlled substance analogue to that individual without that individual's knowledge, shall be imprisoned not more than 20 years and fined in accordance with title 18.

rows.trigger: Definitional only; assigns no penalty. Defines the "without that individual's knowledge" element of (b)(7)(A).
rows.quote: For purposes of this paragraph, the term "without that individual's knowledge" means that the individual is unaware that a substance with the ability to alter that individual's ability to appraise conduct or to decline participation in or communicate unwillingness to participate in conduct is administered to the individual.

rows.trigger: Possessing a listed chemical with intent to manufacture a controlled substance. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Maximum 20 years if a list I chemical; otherwise 10 years.
rows.quote: (1) possesses a listed chemical with intent to manufacture a controlled substance except as authorized by this subchapter; ... shall be fined in accordance with title 18 or imprisoned not more than 20 years in the case of a violation of paragraph (1) or (2) involving a list I chemical or not more than 10 years in the case of a violation of this subsection other than a violation of paragraph (1) or (2) involving a list I chemical, or both.

rows.trigger: Possessing OR distributing a listed chemical knowing, or having reasonable cause to believe, it will be used to manufacture a controlled substance. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Maximum 20 years if a list I chemical; otherwise 10 years.
rows.quote: (2) possesses or distributes a listed chemical knowing, or having reasonable cause to believe, that the listed chemical will be used to manufacture a controlled substance except as authorized by this subchapter; or

rows.trigger: Structuring: receiving or distributing a reportable amount of any listed chemical in units small enough to avoid §830 recordkeeping/reporting, with intent to cause evasion. This paragraph never carries the 20-year list I penalty, it is always capped at 10 years, because the 20-year clause reaches only paragraphs (1) and (2).
rows.quote: (3) with the intent of causing the evasion of the recordkeeping or reporting requirements of section 830 of this title, or the regulations issued under that section, receives or distributes a reportable amount of any listed chemical in units small enough so that the making of records or filing of reports under that section is not required;

rows.trigger: Assembling, maintaining, placing, or causing to be placed a boobytrap on Federal property where a controlled substance is being manufactured, distributed, or dispensed. Maximum 10 years.
rows.quote: (1) Any person who assembles, maintains, places, or causes to be placed a boobytrap on Federal property where a controlled substance is being manufactured, distributed, or dispensed shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment for not more than 10 years or fined under title 18, or both.

rows.trigger: One or more prior convictions for an offense punishable under subsection (d); maximum doubles to 20 years. Note the predicate is not required to be "final," unlike the (b) enhancements.
rows.quote: (2) If any person commits such a violation after 1 or more prior convictions for an offense punishable under this subsection, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 20 years or fined under title 18, or both.

rows.trigger: Definitional only; assigns no penalty. Defines "boobytrap."
rows.quote: (3) For the purposes of this subsection, the term "boobytrap" means any concealed or camouflaged device designed to cause bodily injury when triggered by any action of any unsuspecting person making contact with the device. Such term includes guns, ammunition, or explosive devices attached to trip wires or other triggering mechanisms, sharpened stakes, and lines or wires with hooks attached.

rows.trigger: Additional, cumulative penalty (not a substitute): a person convicted of ANY felony violation of §841 relating to receipt, distribution, manufacture, exportation, or importation of a listed chemical may be enjoined from listed-chemical transactions for up to ten years.
rows.quote: In addition to any other applicable penalty, any person convicted of a felony violation of this section relating to the receipt, distribution, manufacture, exportation, or importation of a listed chemical may be enjoined from engaging in any transaction involving a listed chemical for not more than ten years.

rows.trigger: Knowingly distributing a listed chemical in violation of the subchapter, other than a §830 recordkeeping/reporting violation, and except to the extent §842(a)(12), (13), or (14) applies. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Maximum 5 years.
rows.quote: (1) Whoever knowingly distributes a listed chemical in violation of this subchapter (other than in violation of a recordkeeping or reporting requirement of section 830 of this title) shall, except to the extent that paragraph (12), (13), or (14) of section 842(a) of this title applies, be fined under title 18 or imprisoned not more than 5 years, or both.

rows.trigger: Possessing any listed chemical knowing §830 recordkeeping/reporting requirements have not been adhered to and failing to take immediate remedial steps after acquiring that knowledge. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Maximum one year.
rows.quote: (2) Whoever possesses any listed chemical, with knowledge that the recordkeeping or reporting requirements of section 830 of this title have not been adhered to, if, after such knowledge is acquired, such person does not take immediate steps to remedy the violation shall be fined under title 18 or imprisoned not more than one year, or both.

rows.trigger: Knowingly using the Internet to distribute a date rape drug knowing or with reasonable cause to believe EITHER (A) the drug would be used in the commission of criminal sexual conduct, OR (B) the person is not an authorized purchaser. Subparagraph (B) requires no sexual-conduct element at all, mere distribution to a non-authorized purchaser carries the same 20-year maximum. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity.
rows.quote: (1) Whoever knowingly uses the Internet to distribute a date rape drug to any person, knowing or with reasonable cause to believe that— (A) the drug would be used in the commission of criminal sexual conduct; or (B) the person is not an authorized purchaser; shall be fined under this subchapter or imprisoned not more than 20 years, or both.

rows.trigger: Definitional only; assigns no penalty. Defines "date rape drug" (GHB and its analogues including GBL and 1,4-butanediol; ketamine; flunitrazepam; and any substance the Attorney General designates by rulemaking) and "authorized purchaser."
rows.quote: (2) As used in this subsection: (A) The term "date rape drug" means— (i) gamma hydroxybutyric acid (GHB) or any controlled substance analogue of GHB, including gamma butyrolactone (GBL) or 1,4–butanediol; (ii) ketamine; (iii) flunitrazepam; or (iv) any substance which the Attorney General designates, pursuant to the rulemaking procedures prescribed by section 553 of title 5, to be used in committing rape or sexual assault.

rows.trigger: Rulemaking authority only; assigns no penalty. Records/reports required by these regulations become records or reports required under the chapter, which can expose a person to §842 liability.
rows.quote: (3) The Attorney General is authorized to promulgate regulations for record-keeping and reporting by persons handling 1,4–butanediol in order to implement and enforce the provisions of this section. Any record or report required by such regulations shall be considered a record or report required under this chapter.

rows.trigger: Prohibited-act provision: delivering, distributing, or dispensing a controlled substance by means of the Internet, or aiding or abetting such activity. Penalty comes from (h)(4). (The OLRC heading "In general" precedes this text but is not part of the operative sentence and is not quoted.)
rows.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly or intentionally— (A) deliver, distribute, or dispense a controlled substance by means of the Internet, except as authorized by this subchapter; or (B) aid or abet (as such terms are used in section 2 of title 18) any activity described in subparagraph (A) that is not authorized by this subchapter.

rows.trigger: Non-exhaustive examples of conduct violating (h)(1) ("include, but are not limited to"); assigns no separate penalty. Includes unregistered online pharmacies, prescriptions written for Internet dispensation in violation of §829(e), acting as an intermediary bringing buyer and seller together, filling a prescription based solely on an online medical questionnaire, and false statements in §831 notifications or declarations. (The OLRC heading "Examples" precedes this text but is not part of the operative sentence and is not quoted.)
rows.quote: Examples of activities that violate paragraph (1) include, but are not limited to, knowingly or intentionally— (A) delivering, distributing, or dispensing a controlled substance by means of the Internet by an online pharmacy that is not validly registered with a modification authorizing such activity as required by section 823(g) of this title (unless exempt from such registration); ...

rows.trigger: Exemption provision; assigns no penalty. Excludes nonpractitioner delivery within registration, mere advocacy or pricing information posted online, and pure telecommunications/Internet access/hosting conduct, but subparagraph (B) withdraws the telecommunications and hosting exceptions from anyone acting in concert with a violator.
rows.quote: (B) The exceptions under subclauses (I) and (II) of subparagraph (A)(iii) shall not apply to a person acting in concert with a person who violates paragraph (1).

rows.trigger: Any knowing or intentional violation of subsection (h) is sentenced under the full subsection (b) ladder, including its mandatory minimums, rather than under a separate cap. (The OLRC heading "Knowing or intentional violation" precedes this text but is not part of the operative sentence and is not quoted.)
rows.quote: Any person who knowingly or intentionally violates this subsection shall be sentenced in accordance with subsection (b).

usc-18-1956.title: 18 U.S.C. §1956 - Laundering of monetary instruments
unread: Every subsection of the operative text, (a) through (j), was re-fetched and read start to finish for this repair, including all four paragraphs of (b), all nine paragraphs of (c), all seven subparagraphs of (c)(7), the seven clauses of (c)(7)(B), and the full receiver tree of (b)(4). Every provision read is rowed below.
NOT READ - the Source Credit / public-law amendment history block following subsection (j).
NOT READ - the Editorial Notes block (References in Text, Codification, Amendments).
NOT READ - the Statutory Notes and Related Subsidiaries block (effective-date notes and Rule of Construction).

NOT READ - the external statutes incorporated by reference and not reproduced on this page: 18 U.S.C. §1961(1), 18 U.S.C. §1957, 28 U.S.C. §754, 31 U.S.C. §5312(a)(2), and every predicate statute cross-referenced in (c)(7)(A) through (G).

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Federal statute assigns no felony degree. Conducting or attempting a financial transaction knowing the property represents proceeds of some form of unlawful activity, where the transaction in fact involves proceeds of specified unlawful activity, PLUS any one of the four alternative mental states in (A)(i), (A)(ii), (B)(i), or (B)(ii). There is no dollar threshold of any kind: the $500,000 figure is a FINE CAP, not a value trigger. Any amount, however small, is covered.
rows.quote: Whoever, knowing that the property involved in a financial transaction represents the proceeds of some form of unlawful activity, conducts or attempts to conduct such a financial transaction which in fact involves the proceeds of specified unlawful activity- ... shall be sentenced to a fine of not more than $500,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater, or imprisonment for not more than twenty years, or both. For purposes of this paragraph, a financial transaction shall be considered to be one involving the proceeds of specified unlawful activity if it is part of a set of parallel or dependent transactions, any one of which involves the proceeds of specified unlawful activity, and all of which are part of a single plan or arrangement.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state 1 of 4 under (a)(1): intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(1) (fine up to the greater of $500,000 or twice the value of the property, imprisonment up to 20 years, or both). No value element.
rows.quote: (A)(i) with the intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state 2 of 4 under (a)(1): intent to engage in tax evasion or false-return conduct. Carries the same flush penalty of (a)(1). No value element.
rows.quote: (ii) with intent to engage in conduct constituting a violation of section 7201 or 7206 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state 3 of 4 under (a)(1), reached through the (B) chapeau 'knowing that the transaction is designed in whole or in part-': concealment. Carries the same flush penalty of (a)(1). No value element.
rows.quote: (B) knowing that the transaction is designed in whole or in part- (i) to conceal or disguise the nature, the location, the source, the ownership, or the control of the proceeds of specified unlawful activity; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state 4 of 4 under (a)(1): avoiding a transaction reporting requirement. Carries the same flush penalty of (a)(1). No value element, and note this reaches structuring-type intent with no dollar floor stated in this section.
rows.quote: (ii) to avoid a transaction reporting requirement under State or Federal law,

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. International transportation, transmission, or transfer of a monetary instrument or funds into or out of the United States, plus a mental state under (A) or (B). No dollar threshold: the $500,000 figure is a FINE CAP, not a trigger. Any amount is covered.
rows.quote: Whoever transports, transmits, or transfers, or attempts to transport, transmit, or transfer a monetary instrument or funds from a place in the United States to or through a place outside the United States or to a place in the United States from or through a place outside the United States- ... shall be sentenced to a fine of not more than $500,000 or twice the value of the monetary instrument or funds involved in the transportation, transmission, or transfer, whichever is greater, or imprisonment for not more than twenty years, or both. For the purpose of the offense described in subparagraph (B), the defendant's knowledge may be established by proof that a law enforcement officer represented the matter specified in subparagraph (B) as true, and the defendant's subsequent statements or actions indicate that the defendant believed such representations to be true.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state under (a)(2): intent to promote specified unlawful activity. Note this subparagraph does NOT require knowledge that the funds are criminal proceeds, unlike (B). Carries the flush penalty of (a)(2).
rows.quote: (A) with the intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state under (a)(2) via the (B) chapeau: knowledge of criminal proceeds plus concealment design. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(2). Government's proof of knowledge may be by law enforcement representation (sting) under the flush language.
rows.quote: (B) knowing that the monetary instrument or funds involved in the transportation, transmission, or transfer represent the proceeds of some form of unlawful activity and knowing that such transportation, transmission, or transfer is designed in whole or in part- (i) to conceal or disguise the nature, the location, the source, the ownership, or the control of the proceeds of specified unlawful activity; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state under (a)(2) via the (B) chapeau: knowledge of criminal proceeds plus design to avoid a reporting requirement. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(2). No value element.
rows.quote: (ii) to avoid a transaction reporting requirement under State or Federal law,

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Sting / undercover offense: the property need only be REPRESENTED to be proceeds of specified unlawful activity, or property used to conduct or facilitate specified unlawful activity. Actual criminal proceeds are not required. No dollar threshold at all. Penalty is a fine under this title (no $500,000 cap language) and up to 20 years.
rows.quote: Whoever, with the intent- ... conducts or attempts to conduct a financial transaction involving property represented to be the proceeds of specified unlawful activity, or property used to conduct or facilitate specified unlawful activity, shall be fined under this title or imprisoned for not more than 20 years, or both. For purposes of this paragraph and paragraph (2), the term "represented" means any representation made by a law enforcement officer or by another person at the direction of, or with the approval of, a Federal official authorized to investigate or prosecute violations of this section.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative intent 1 of 3 under (a)(3): promotion. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(3).
rows.quote: (A) to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity;

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative intent 2 of 3 under (a)(3): concealment of property BELIEVED to be proceeds. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(3).
rows.quote: (B) to conceal or disguise the nature, location, source, ownership, or control of property believed to be the proceeds of specified unlawful activity; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative intent 3 of 3 under (a)(3): avoiding a transaction reporting requirement. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(3).
rows.quote: (C) to avoid a transaction reporting requirement under State or Federal law,

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. CIVIL penalty, not a criminal degree, and it is cumulative with the criminal penalties. Reaches conduct described in (a)(1), (a)(3), (a)(2), OR section 1957. Liability attaches at ANY dollar value; the penalty AMOUNT is capped at the greater of the property value and $10,000. Neither figure is a trigger threshold.
rows.quote: (1) In general.-Whoever conducts or attempts to conduct a transaction described in subsection (a)(1) or (a)(3), or section 1957, or a transportation, transmission, or transfer described in subsection (a)(2), is liable to the United States for a civil penalty of not more than the greater of- (A) the value of the property, funds, or monetary instruments involved in the transaction; or (B) $10,000.

rows.trigger: First of two alternative civil penalty measures under (b)(1); the court applies whichever of (A) and (B) is greater. Value-based measure of the penalty AMOUNT, not a value element of liability. No trigger threshold.
rows.quote: (A) the value of the property, funds, or monetary instruments involved in the transaction; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Second of two alternative civil penalty measures under (b)(1): a flat $10,000 that governs the penalty AMOUNT when it exceeds the property value. It is a penalty figure, NOT a value threshold for liability, so it is not typed into min or max: (b)(1) liability attaches at any dollar value.

NO LOWER BOUND. Jurisdiction over FOREIGN persons, including foreign financial institutions, for adjudicating or enforcing a (b) civil penalty, provided service of process is made, plus any one of the three alternative hooks in (A), (B), or (C). No dollar value element in any of them: this reaches a foreign actor at ANY value, unlike the (f)(2) extraterritorial-jurisdiction threshold, which does not apply here.
rows.quote: (2) Jurisdiction over foreign persons.-For purposes of adjudicating an action filed or enforcing a penalty ordered under this section, the district courts shall have jurisdiction over any foreign person, including any financial institution authorized under the laws of a foreign country, against whom the action is brought, if service of process upon the foreign person is made under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure or the laws of the country in which the foreign person is found, and-

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Jurisdictional hook 1 of 3 under (b)(2): the foreign person commits a subsection (a) offense involving a financial transaction occurring in whole or in part in the United States. ANY dollar value suffices; there is no $10,000 floor for reaching a foreign person under this paragraph.
rows.quote: (A) the foreign person commits an offense under subsection (a) involving a financial transaction that occurs in whole or in part in the United States;

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Jurisdictional hook 2 of 3 under (b)(2): the foreign person converts to his or her own use property in which the United States holds an ownership interest by virtue of a forfeiture order. No value element of any kind.
rows.quote: (B) the foreign person converts, to his or her own use, property in which the United States has an ownership interest by virtue of the entry of an order of forfeiture by a court of the United States; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Jurisdictional hook 3 of 3 under (b)(2): status-based. The foreign person is a financial institution that maintains a bank account at a financial institution in the United States. No conduct-value element at all.
rows.quote: (C) the foreign person is a financial institution that maintains a bank account at a financial institution in the United States.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Court authority over assets: pretrial restraining order or ANY other action necessary to keep any bank account or other property held by the defendant in the United States available to satisfy a judgment under this section. Available pretrial, no dollar floor, no degree.
rows.quote: (3) Court authority over assets.-A court may issue a pretrial restraining order or take any other action necessary to ensure that any bank account or other property held by the defendant in the United States is available to satisfy a judgment under this section.

rows.trigger: Chapeau of the Federal receiver paragraph; the operative content is in subparagraphs (A) and (B), each rowed below. No value element.
rows.quote: (4) Federal receiver.-

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Penalty-enforcement provision: the court may appoint a Federal Receiver to take custody of ALL assets of the defendant, WHEREVER LOCATED, to satisfy a (b) civil judgment, a §981 or §982 forfeiture judgment, or a CRIMINAL sentence under §1957 or subsection (a), including restitution to any victim of a specified unlawful activity. Reaches worldwide assets at any value.
rows.quote: (A) In general.-A court may appoint a Federal Receiver, in accordance with subparagraph (B) of this paragraph, to collect, marshal, and take custody, control, and possession of all assets of the defendant, wherever located, to satisfy a civil judgment under this subsection, a forfeiture judgment under section 981 or 982, or a criminal sentence under section 1957 or subsection (a) of this section, including an order of restitution to any victim of a specified unlawful activity.

rows.trigger: Chapeau for the appointment and authority of the Federal Receiver; the three clauses (i) through (iii) are rowed below. No value element.
rows.quote: (B) Appointment and authority.-A Federal Receiver described in subparagraph (A)-

rows.trigger: Appointment mechanism: upon application of a Federal prosecutor or a Federal or State regulator, by the court with jurisdiction over the defendant. No value element.
rows.quote: (i) may be appointed upon application of a Federal prosecutor or a Federal or State regulator, by the court having jurisdiction over the defendant in the case;

rows.trigger: The receiver is an officer of the court with the powers set out in 28 U.S.C. §754 (receiver's territorial powers over property in different districts). No value element.
rows.quote: (ii) shall be an officer of the court, and the powers of the Federal Receiver shall include the powers set out in section 754 of title 28, United States Code; and

rows.trigger: Chapeau: the receiver has standing equivalent to a Federal prosecutor to request asset information from the two sources in subclauses (I) and (II), rowed below. No value element.
rows.quote: (iii) shall have standing equivalent to that of a Federal prosecutor for the purpose of submitting requests to obtain information regarding the assets of the defendant-

rows.trigger: Asset-information source 1 of 2: FinCEN. No value element.
rows.quote: (I) from the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network of the Department of the Treasury; or

rows.trigger: Asset-information source 2 of 2: a foreign country under a mutual legal assistance treaty, multilateral agreement, or other international law enforcement assistance arrangement, subject to Attorney General policies. No value element.
rows.quote: (II) from a foreign country pursuant to a mutual legal assistance treaty, multilateral agreement, or other arrangement for international law enforcement assistance, provided that such requests are in accordance with the policies and procedures of the Attorney General.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Definitional provision that widens liability rather than narrowing it: the defendant need not know WHICH form of unlawful activity produced the property, and the underlying activity need not be one of the offenses enumerated in (c)(7). Any felony under State, Federal, or foreign law satisfies the knowledge element. Recorded because it materially controls whether the (a) penalties attach.
rows.quote: (1) the term "knowing that the property involved in a financial transaction represents the proceeds of some form of unlawful activity" means that the person knew the property involved in the transaction represented proceeds from some form, though not necessarily which form, of activity that constitutes a felony under State, Federal, or foreign law, regardless of whether or not such activity is specified in paragraph (7);

rows.trigger: Definition of 'conducts', an element of the (a)(1) and (a)(3) offenses: includes initiating, concluding, or participating in initiating or concluding a transaction. No value element.
rows.quote: (2) the term "conducts" includes initiating, concluding, or participating in initiating, or concluding a transaction;

rows.trigger: Definition of 'transaction', an element of the (a) offenses; extremely broad, reaching gifts, deposits, safe deposit box use, and any payment, transfer, or delivery through a financial institution by whatever means. No value element.
rows.quote: (3) the term "transaction" includes a purchase, sale, loan, pledge, gift, transfer, delivery, or other disposition, and with respect to a financial institution includes a deposit, withdrawal, transfer between accounts, exchange of currency, loan, extension of credit, purchase or sale of any stock, bond, certificate of deposit, or other monetary instrument, use of a safe deposit box, or any other payment, transfer, or delivery by, through, or to a financial institution, by whatever means effected;

rows.trigger: Definition of 'financial transaction', the core element of (a)(1) and (a)(3): either (A) a transaction affecting interstate or foreign commerce in any way or degree via (i) movement of funds, (ii) monetary instruments, or (iii) transfer of title to real property, vehicle, vessel, or aircraft, or (B) any use of a financial institution engaged in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce. No value element.
rows.quote: (4) the term "financial transaction" means (A) a transaction which in any way or degree affects interstate or foreign commerce (i) involving the movement of funds by wire or other means or (ii) involving one or more monetary instruments, or (iii) involving the transfer of title to any real property, vehicle, vessel, or aircraft, or (B) a transaction involving the use of a financial institution which is engaged in, or the activities of which affect, interstate or foreign commerce in any way or degree;

rows.trigger: Definition of 'monetary instruments', an element of the (a)(2) transportation offense: coin or currency of any country, travelers' checks, personal checks, bank checks, money orders, and bearer-form investment securities or negotiable instruments. No value element.
rows.quote: (5) the term "monetary instruments" means (i) coin or currency of the United States or of any other country, travelers' checks, personal checks, bank checks, and money orders, or (ii) investment securities or negotiable instruments, in bearer form or otherwise in such form that title thereto passes upon delivery;

rows.trigger: Chapeau of the 'financial institution' definition; the two inclusion subparagraphs are rowed below. No value element.
rows.quote: (6) the term "financial institution" includes-

rows.trigger: 'Financial institution' includes any institution defined in 31 U.S.C. §5312(a)(2) or its regulations. No value element.
rows.quote: (A) any financial institution, as defined in section 5312(a)(2) of title 31, United States Code, or the regulations promulgated thereunder; and

rows.trigger: 'Financial institution' includes any foreign bank as defined in section 1 of the International Banking Act of 1978. No value element.
rows.quote: (B) any foreign bank, as defined in section 1 of the International Banking Act of 1978 (12 U.S.C. 3101);

rows.trigger: Chapeau of the 'specified unlawful activity' definition. Seven subparagraphs (A) through (G) follow, each rowed below. Only two clauses in the entire definition carry dollar floors (the food-benefits clause inside (D) and the wildlife clause (G)); every other predicate qualifies at ANY value.
rows.quote: (7) the term "specified unlawful activity" means-

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. The single largest predicate category: every offense listed in the RICO predicate list, 18 U.S.C. §1961(1), except acts indictable under subchapter II of chapter 53 of title 31 (Bank Secrecy Act reporting offenses). Qualifies as specified unlawful activity at ANY value.
rows.quote: (A) any act or activity constituting an offense listed in section 1961(1) of this title except an act which is indictable under subchapter II of chapter 53 of title 31;

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Foreign-nation offenses as predicates, for financial transactions occurring in whole or in part in the United States; seven clauses (i) through (vii), each rowed below and each qualifying at ANY value. This subparagraph is also what triggers the 7-year limitations period in subsection (j).
rows.quote: (B) with respect to a financial transaction occurring in whole or in part in the United States, an offense against a foreign nation involving-

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Foreign offense predicate 1 of 7: controlled substance manufacture, importation, sale, or distribution. Any value.
rows.quote: (i) the manufacture, importation, sale, or distribution of a controlled substance (as such term is defined for the purposes of the Controlled Substances Act);

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Foreign offense predicate 2 of 7: murder, kidnapping, robbery, extortion, destruction of property by explosive or fire, or a crime of violence as defined in section 16. Any value.
rows.quote: (ii) murder, kidnapping, robbery, extortion, destruction of property by means of explosive or fire, or a crime of violence (as defined in section 16);

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Foreign offense predicate 3 of 7: fraud, or any scheme or attempt to defraud, by or against a foreign bank. Any value.
rows.quote: (iii) fraud, or any scheme or attempt to defraud, by or against a foreign bank (as defined in paragraph 7 of section 1(b) of the International Banking Act of 1978));

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Foreign offense predicate 4 of 7: bribery of a public official, or misappropriation, theft, or embezzlement of public funds by or for the benefit of a public official. Any value.
rows.quote: (iv) bribery of a public official, or the misappropriation, theft, or embezzlement of public funds by or for the benefit of a public official;

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Foreign offense predicate 5 of 7: smuggling or export control violations involving either (I) a United States Munitions List item or (II) an item controlled under the Export Administration Regulations. Any value.
rows.quote: (v) smuggling or export control violations involving- (I) an item controlled on the United States Munitions List established under section 38 of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2778); or (II) an item controlled under regulations under the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. Parts 730–774);

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Foreign offense predicate 6 of 7: offenses subject to a multilateral extradite-or-prosecute treaty obligation. Any value.
rows.quote: (vi) an offense with respect to which the United States would be obligated by a multilateral treaty, either to extradite the alleged offender or to submit the case for prosecution, if the offender were found within the territory of the United States; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Foreign offense predicate 7 of 7: trafficking in persons, selling or buying of children, sexual exploitation of children, or transporting, recruiting, or harboring a person, including a child, for commercial sex acts. Any value.
rows.quote: (vii) trafficking in persons, selling or buying of children, sexual exploitation of children, or transporting, recruiting or harboring a person, including a child, for commercial sex acts;

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Predicate: any act or acts constituting a continuing criminal enterprise under 21 U.S.C. §848. Any value.
rows.quote: (C) any act or acts constituting a continuing criminal enterprise, as that term is defined in section 408 of the Controlled Substances Act (21 U.S.C. 848);

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND for the subparagraph as a whole. An enumeration of roughly one hundred Federal predicate offenses (destruction of aircraft, espionage, bank fraud entries, computer fraud, murder, kidnaping, hostage taking, robbery, child pornography, copyright and counterfeit goods trafficking, terrorism and material support offenses, export control and sanctions violations, equity skimming, FARA, FCPA, atomic weapons, North Korea sanctions, and more), every one of which qualifies as specified unlawful activity at ANY value, with a single exception: the food-and-nutrition-benefits clause, rowed separately below, which alone carries a $5,000 floor.

The statute says 'not less than $5,000', so the $5,000 figure is an INCLUSIVE floor and min 5000 is exact. Every other offense listed in (c)(7)(D) qualifies as a predicate at ANY value. rows.trigger: Chapeau: extraterritorial jurisdiction over conduct prohibited by this section exists only if BOTH conjunctive conditions (1) and (2), each rowed below, are met. This governs extraterritorial reach only; it does not limit domestic prosecutions under (a), and it does not limit the (b)(2) civil jurisdiction over foreign persons, which attaches at any value.
rows.quote: (f) There is extraterritorial jurisdiction over the conduct prohibited by this section if-

rows.trigger: Extraterritorial-jurisdiction condition 1 of 2 (conjunctive with (f)(2)): the conduct is by a United States citizen, or, for a non-citizen, the conduct occurs in part in the United States. No value element.
rows.quote: (1) the conduct is by a United States citizen or, in the case of a non-United States citizen, the conduct occurs in part in the United States; and

rows.trigger: JURISDICTIONAL threshold, not a penalty tier and not a degree trigger. The statutory floor is exclusive: exactly $10,000 does NOT satisfy (f)(2), so the inclusive min is recorded as 10000.01. This threshold applies ONLY to the extraterritorial jurisdiction question: it does NOT limit domestic prosecutions under (a), which have no dollar floor, and it does NOT limit (b)(2), which gives district courts civil jurisdiction over foreign persons at ANY value.
rows.quote: (2) the transaction or series of related transactions involves funds or monetary instruments of a value exceeding $10,000.

rows.quote: (g) Notice of Conviction of Financial Institutions.-If any financial institution or any officer, director, or employee of any financial institution has been found guilty of an offense under this section, section 1957 or 1960 of this title, or section 5322 or 5324 of title 31, the Attorney General shall provide written notice of such fact to the appropriate regulatory agency for the financial institution.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Conspiracy to commit any §1956 or §1957 offense carries the SAME penalty as the completed object offense. No overt act requirement stated, no reduction from the substantive penalty, no value element.
rows.quote: (h) Any person who conspires to commit any offense defined in this section or section 1957 shall be subject to the same penalties as those prescribed for the offense the commission of which was the object of the conspiracy.

rows.trigger: Venue chapeau for §1956 and §1957 prosecutions, subject to the attempt/conspiracy rule in (i)(2); the two alternative districts are in (A) and (B), rowed below. No value element.
rows.quote: (i) Venue.-(1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), a prosecution for an offense under this section or section 1957 may be brought in-

rows.trigger: Venue option 1 of 2: any district in which the financial or monetary transaction is conducted. No value element.
rows.quote: (A) any district in which the financial or monetary transaction is conducted; or

rows.trigger: Venue option 2 of 2: any district where the underlying specified unlawful activity could be prosecuted, if the defendant participated in transferring the proceeds from that district to the transaction district. No value element.
rows.quote: (B) any district where a prosecution for the underlying specified unlawful activity could be brought, if the defendant participated in the transfer of the proceeds of the specified unlawful activity from that district to the district where the financial or monetary transaction is conducted.

rows.trigger: Venue for attempt and conspiracy: the district where venue lies for the completed offense under (i)(1), or any other district where an act in furtherance took place. No value element.
rows.quote: (2) A prosecution for an attempt or conspiracy offense under this section or section 1957 may be brought in the district where venue would lie for the completed offense under paragraph (1), or in any other district where an act in furtherance of the attempt or conspiracy took place.

rows.trigger: Single continuing transaction rule: a transfer of funds from one place to another, by wire or any other means, is one continuing transaction, and any person conducting any portion of it may be charged in any district in which the transaction takes place. No value element.
rows.quote: (3) For purposes of this section, a transfer of funds from 1 place to another, by wire or any other means, shall constitute a single, continuing transaction. Any person who conducts (as that term is defined in subsection (c)(2)) any portion of the transaction may be charged in any district in which the transaction takes place.

rows.trigger: STATUTE OF LIMITATIONS, not a punishment limit and not a degree or enhancement: a bar on commencing prosecution. Applies ONLY where the specified unlawful activity is a foreign offense defined in (c)(7)(B): a 7-year limitations period, notwithstanding the general period in section 3282. No value element.
rows.quote: (j) Seven-year Limitation.-Notwithstanding section 3282, no person shall be prosecuted, tried, or punished for a violation of this section or section 1957 if the specified unlawful activity constituting the violation is the activity defined in subsection (c)(7)(B) of this section, unless the indictment is found or the information is instituted not later than 7 years after the date on which the offense was committed.
